The path for whoever reports: "Under the repository name, click the Security and quality tab" and "Click Report a vulnerability to open the advisory form" ([GitHub Docs, Privately reporting a security vulnerability](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/security-advisories/guidance-on-reporting-and-writing-information-about-vulnerabilities/privately-reporting-a-security-vulnerability), read 2026-10-19).
- **For the whole organization.**
  - Without the button, the "standard process" remains: an issue asking for a contact, and "it should not include any information about the bug" ([GitHub Docs, Coordinated disclosure of security vulnerabilities](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/vulnerability-reporting-and-management/coordinated-disclosure), read 2026-10-19).
  - The organization's configuration enables the button in new repositories too: "Use as default for newly created repositories" ([GitHub Docs, Creating a custom security configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-at-scale/configure-organization-security/establish-complete-coverage/creating-a-custom-security-configuration), read 2026-10-19).
  - It costs no money. Only the features protecting code and secrets are paid, and only for private repositories: "these features incur usage costs (or require GitHub Advanced Security licenses) when applied to private and internal repositories" (ibid.). The NovaTrail repositories are public (R18).
  - The ready configuration "GitHub recommended" does not fit. It also enables CodeQL default setup — `code_scanning_default_setup: "enabled"` (the GitHub API, `orgs/altnovatrail/code-security/configurations`, 2026-10-19) —, while CodeQL comes by NovaTrail's own workflows.
- **A time limit.** `spec` has the OpenSSF Best Practices badge (R48), and its criterion `vulnerability_report_response` is a MUST: "The project's initial response time for any vulnerability report received in the last 6 months MUST be less than or equal to 14 days" (ossf/best-practices-badge, `criteria/criteria.yml` and `config/locales/en.yml`, branch `production` 2ea9de2, read 2026-10-26). With "promises no response time" in SECURITY.md the badge would hold only until the first late response, and the policy would contradict the badge.
- **DCO.**
  - The DCO confirms that the contributor has the right to give the contribution; the license for the contribution is given by section 5 of the license.
  - The text of the DCO is copied only unchanged: "Everyone is permitted to copy and distribute verbatim copies of this license document, but changing it is not allowed" ([Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1](https://developercertificate.org/), read 2026-10-19).
  - The sign-off is public forever — item (d): "a record of the contribution (including all personal information I submit with it, including my sign-off) is maintained indefinitely". So CONTRIBUTING says so plainly and allows signing off with the GitHub noreply address.
  - GitHub makes compulsory only the sign-off of web commits: "Compulsory commit signoffs only apply to commits made via the web interface" ([GitHub Docs, Managing the commit signoff policy for your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/managing-the-commit-signoff-policy-for-your-organization), read 2026-10-19).
- **Forms.** A compulsory field holds while the repository is public: `required` says "Only for public repositories" ([GitHub Docs, Syntax for GitHub's form schema](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-githubs-form-schema), read 2026-11-01). The NovaTrail repositories are public (R18).
  - Forms have not become a generally available feature yet: "Issue forms are currently in public preview and subject to change" ([GitHub Docs, Syntax for issue forms](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/syntax-for-issue-forms), read 2026-11-01). If GitHub changes them, `.github` edits the forms, and the decision stays.
- **A blank issue** is not closed for everyone: "users with write access or above (Write, Maintain, or Admin roles) will still see the Blank issue option in the template chooser, labeled Maintainers only" ([GitHub Docs, Configuring issue templates for your repository](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository), read 2026-11-01).
- **A type, not a label.**
  - Labels live in each repository separately, and they do not suit a default form: "If a label does not already exist in the repository, it will not be automatically added to the issue" (Syntax for issue forms).
  - Types, though, are "defined at the organization level" (ibid.). The organization has Task, Bug and Feature enabled (the GitHub API, `orgs/altnovatrail/issue-types`, read 2026-11-01).
  - Whether the form sets the type on an issue of a third-party author too, the documentation does not say. It will be seen by the first such issue, and if it does not, a maintainer sets the type.
- **Sessions' pull requests** get no template, and they do not need it: they follow the RUN.md of their repository. `gh pr create` asks for the text of the pull request in interactive mode, and "Use `--title` and `--body` to skip this" ([GitHub CLI manual, gh pr create](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_pr_create), read 2026-11-01).

— *Rejected:*
- the Contributor Covenant 3.0 (2025): it is under CC BY-SA 4.0, and our edit would stay under share-alike too;
- a code of our own under Apache-2.0 — a new sensitive text that would have to be written and maintained;
- an email address for vulnerabilities and complaints;
- a CLA: it needs a party with which it is signed, and a service that keeps the signers' data;
- private vulnerability reports repository by repository: until each was set up there would be no button;
- keeping "no response time": the badge would promise what the policy does not;
- templates before the first code and CI — a checklist written then would be rewritten when CI came; waiting for the first code of the format — the templates need no format code, and the warning about learners' data would meanwhile stand only in CONTRIBUTING;
- a copy of the templates in each repository through `repo-template/`: thirteen copies would diverge, and an edit would go into each repository by its move to a tag;
- one bug form with the blank issue open: a blank issue has no warning about learners' data;
- a form for the private vulnerability report, `VULNERABILITY_REPORT.yml`, — also a default file of `.github`. It would give little: "If the repository has a security policy, the policy is displayed above the reporting form" ([GitHub Docs, Privately reporting a security vulnerability](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/report-and-fix-vulnerabilities/report-privately), read 2026-11-01), and SECURITY.md already asks not to copy learners' data into the report;
- Markdown templates: their text can be erased whole, and nothing in it is compulsory;
- people writing in English or Russian; pull requests in English, issues in either; templates in two languages — two texts that would have to be kept in agreement; in Russian — against R14.

— *Consequence:* architecture 3.11; the files of `.github` — CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` and `.github/pull_request_template.md`; R20; R30; RULES.md, Hard rules, Licenses; `.bestpractices.json`.

## Questions of the components' detailing

On 2026-10-19 the author charged the executor with deciding the questions of table 3 of RUN.md that the detailing of the components brought, by the recommendations. Where a recommendation put the choice off until the component's task, and the entry makes it, the entry calls this the executor's proposal.

**R23. The success corridor is a rule of `engine`, and the threshold "mastered" is a rule of `learner-model`. `learner-model` gives the probability of a correct answer, and which corridor to aim at `engine` decides. The threshold "mastered" lives in `learner-model` and follows the corridor's target by a constant of the model; by the same threshold the model gives the review date, and whether to return a mastered skill into rotation and when to give a skill whose date has come, `engine` decides.** The corridor — the recommendation on question В10; the threshold — the author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the rows «в реестр spec» `learner-model` В4 and В5, by their recommendations.
- **The corridor.** Card 3.8 and concepts 12 assign it to the engine: it is part of the choice rule, "the learner solves the task with a probability from 0.70 to 0.85". Choosing a task is the engine's business, not the learner model's (concepts 11, 12): a model that knew the corridor would start deciding what to give next.
- **The threshold** is a constant of `learner-model`, one for all modules: the cautious estimate of a skill on an average task of the band holds the threshold without guessing. Now it is σ(λ − β) ≥ 0.71875 at the cautious level λ, that is, P = 0.775 for a task with five options — the middle of standalone's corridor (R03 learner-model). In standalone the middle of the corridor is both the target of the recommendation and the line at or below which an answer counts toward mastering: "CorridorMiddle is what the recommendation aims at, and the line an answer has to be at or below to count toward mastering a topic" ([`internal/domain/rating/corridor.go`](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/internal/domain/rating/corridor.go), used by `mastery.go`; commit c6cbeb2, read 2026-10-19). The number belongs to `learner-model`, not to `spec`, as the corridor's numbers belong to `engine`.
- **What `engine` reads:** "mastered" and the mastery band — the highest of the bands where the skill is taught at which the threshold holds — in the skill's state (concepts 11). The engine neither sets nor passes the threshold: a number of `engine` in the computation's input would make the cache depend on what is not in its mark (R80).
- **The threshold and the corridor's target.** Without guessing, the threshold coincides with the corridor's target only for a choice of five, and for a free answer and a choice of two they diverge — this is a measure of the simulator. A new target of the corridor is a new constant of the model: both go in one tag of `sim`, whose gate file names the commits of both libraries; `learner-model` is merged when the pull request of `engine` has passed review, and `api` moves to both versions together (R103).
- **The review date** — by the same threshold: the moment when the cautious probability of a mastered skill with retention falls below the threshold, but not earlier than the model's smallest pause after the last practice, and "already" if the threshold does not hold even without forgetting (R04 learner-model). There is no second threshold, "due", in the engine: "due" is a time of choice not earlier than the date. When to give a skill whose date has come, how many repetitions a day and how they share the queue, is a rule of `engine` (concepts 12).
- **The return into rotation** is a rule of `engine`: in standalone a mastered topic came back when its recommended point went above the band at which it was mastered. The model's "mastered" stays as it is meanwhile: from it are derived the knowing of an anchor skill and the skill map (architecture 3.3). A threshold of the engine's own would be a second threshold: it comes only by a row «в реестр spec».

— *Rejected:*
- the corridor in `learner-model`; the corridor's numbers in `spec` — they change together with the choice rule and pass the simulator `sim`, like any change of `engine`;
- the threshold as an input from `engine` at each computation (R80, above);
- "mastered" decided by `engine` from the estimate and the uncertainty from the model — the engine would need the history of answers: five answers in the skill, an answer without a hint, two errors in a row, — and "mastered" is part of the skill's state (concepts 11);
- only the estimate at the time of choice for the engine — the threshold "due" would live as a second one, in the engine; only the date — the corridor would not see forgetting and after a long break would give a task of the former difficulty;
- waiting for the detailing of `engine` — `engine` and `sim` would be planned under an open question, while `learner-model` already read "mastered" with the mastery band.

— *Consequence:* architecture 1, 3.3, 3.8; concepts 11, 12; repositories 7; R03 and R04 learner-model; R103.

**R24. The eval sets of modules in the CI of `modules` and the samples of adult volunteers in the measurement of stage 2 are run with a separate key of the platform — only for eval, not with the key of the service account of `api` and not with the author's own key. The platform pays. The keys lie in the Secret Manager of `infra`, a secret per provider, and the CI of `modules` and `tutor` reads them through Workload Identity Federation, with a pool of its own `github-eval`, from the GitHub environment `eval` (R120).** The recommendation on question В14; the key's place, the author's answer of 2026-11-09 to Т-28. The provider's terms for this key are checked as in privacy 5.3, and the price of a run is named before the first launch (rule 4 of RUN.md).
- **A job with a secret**, in every repository, not only eval (R05 .github):
  - the shared workflows take no secrets: a shared workflow without secrets has nothing to leak;
  - `pull_request_target` is used nowhere: "Workflows triggered by `pull_request_target` run with elevated trust: the job receives the base repository's `GITHUB_TOKEN` and access to repository and organization secrets" ([GitHub Docs, Securely using pull_request_target](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/securely-using-pull_request_target)), and the code of a pull request from a fork is someone else's;
  - a job with a secret does its work only on a push to `main` and on a pull request from a branch of the repository itself. Without the secret it is not skipped but fails at once and names the reason. This happens on a pull request from a fork: "With the exception of `GITHUB_TOKEN`, secrets are not passed to the runner when a workflow is triggered from a forked repository" ([GitHub Docs, Using secrets in GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)). And a job must not be skipped: "A job that is skipped will report its status as "Success". It will not prevent a pull request from merging, even if it is a required check" ([GitHub Docs, Status checks](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/reference/status-checks)). A failed job holds the merge until a maintainer reads the code of the change and carries it into a branch of the repository: until then someone else's code is given no secrets. All three places were read 2026-10-20.
- **A Dependabot pull request** comes from a branch of the repository, but gets no Actions secrets: "Secrets are populated from Dependabot secrets. GitHub Actions secrets are not available" ([GitHub Docs, Dependabot on GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-on-actions), read 2026-10-20). Whether a job with a secret fails on it or takes a Dependabot secret is decided together with the job itself; the eval job fails, and the change is carried into a branch of one's own.
- **Does not cover** children's samples in the measurement of stage 2: they lie outside the repositories and go to an AI provider only with the platform's key under an agreement that admits children (R121), and only once the admission table admits to it the work of a child under 13, the strictest category, since the sample file names no category (R125); until then they go to none.

— *Why:*
- The keys with which `api` serves learners are read by its service account (R15). A CI that read them too is one more place they would leak from.
- The eval sets of modules hold no learners' work (concepts 3): there are synthetic samples and samples of adult volunteers and authors.
- The platform cannot promise that a model is admitted by eval if the run went on someone else's terms.

— *Rejected:* the key of the service account of `api`; the module author's own key; `pull_request_target` for eval on a pull request from a fork; skipping the job on a fork.

— *Consequence:* architecture 3.6, 3.10; R120.

**R25. The samples page for the first measurement on volunteers' samples is without hosting until it moves to Firebase Hosting as a site of its own, the tasks and media files are put into it at build time, and children's samples are made with it too, but without a pull request.** The recommendations on questions В15–В17, and the author's answers to the rows «в реестр spec» `canvas` В4, В6, В25 and В64, `tutor` В20, `modules` В7 and `infra` В6 and of 2026-11-09, each by its recommendation.
- **Where.** The page's build is downloaded from the release of `canvas` and opened on the volunteer's device. It works without the network, and while the volunteer writes, nobody's log sees their IP address. GitHub sees the IP address of whoever downloads the build: "We collect data about your interactions with the Services, such as IP address, device information, session details" ([GitHub General Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement), section "Automatically", the version of 27 April 2026, read 2026-10-20). The page says so when it opens (architecture 3.6 canvas). That the build works when opened from a file, a trial of `canvas` checks (R09 canvas).
- **Devices.** Without hosting the page opens on a computer and on Android, but not on an iPad: the Files app («Файлы») of iPadOS opens it in Quick Look, where the script does not run. The trials of `canvas` (architecture 4 canvas): on iPadOS 26.5 and 27 in the iPad Simulator, Safari downloads the file to "On My iPad" («На iPad») → "Downloads", and Files opens it in Quick Look, the markup is visible, and the script does not run. The first measurement runs on computers and Android, and the page opened on an iPad says that it cannot be opened here.
- **Hosting.** The hosting of the build of `app` is Firebase Hosting (R06 infra). The page moves to it as a separate site of the same Firebase project, with its own origin, and the iPad comes with it; when, the author decides, by R128: Google is a processor for Hosting, and Hosting keeps IP addresses — "Hosting retains IP data for a few months", — a period that cannot be configured ([Privacy and Security in Firebase](https://firebase.google.com/support/privacy), "Last modified: September 24, 2026", read 2026-11-08). An origin of its own, because `app`'s erasures on the device take the storage of its origin — all of it by "Erase everything on this device", an account's by another account's sign-in (architecture 3.7 app) —, and Hosting keeps several sites in one project.
- **The tasks and media files** the page's build takes from the packages of the release of `modules`, by exact tag: the open views of the tasks, which the CLI of `module-kit` builds from the server part, and the media files, files of the device part (R62). Whether the CLI needs a command of its own for this, the detailing of `module-kit` decides. While working, the page does not go to the network, and the package of `canvas` still knows no subjects (architecture 3.2): only the page's build gets the data. This is the link "a CI tool at an exact tag" (repositories 1): the CI of `canvas` takes the CLI of `module-kit` and the release of `modules` by tag, as the CI of `modules` takes `module-kit` and `sim`.
- **A withdrawn version** (R63). Before building the page, the CI of `canvas` reads the withdrawal marks in the index of the newest release of `modules` and builds no page from a withdrawn version, and a child sample session runs with the build of the latest release of `canvas`, which the page tells the adult (Д45). The newest index is read only for the marks, since only it knows of all the withdrawals: the one exception to "by exact tag" here.
- **Before the first content of `modules`**, which comes by [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md), the CI of `canvas` puts into the page's build the open views of the measurement tasks from the release of `tutor`: a file without keys, solutions and traps, by exact tag and checksum, its tasks by the task schema of format v0 (R51). The keys stay with `tutor`, and only the open view gets into the build (R05); `tutor` builds it for a time, as its runner for a time gives the verdict in place of `module-kit` (R05 tutor). The volunteer still has one file, the page does not go to the network, and the package of `canvas` knows no subjects: only the source changes, and for a time. This is the link "a CI tool at an exact tag" `canvas` → `tutor`; the reverse one is the synthetic samples of `canvas` in the CI of `tutor` (R38). This release of `tutor` and the measurement on volunteers' samples wait with the large measurement, which R43 put off: in the epic E3 of `tutor` and the epic E5 of `canvas`.
- **The measurement of the course of writing** did not use the page: it was narrowed to one question, on the author's sheet and synthetic data, and needed no volunteers' samples (R24 tutor). Sheet 1 the author wrote in the board's recording mode of `tutor`, which records strokes with time and pressure, erasures and markup in the format `tutor-sample` v0, outside git (R25 tutor); the other 39 code drew, `tutor-eval draw`, in the same format and with `writer` set to `synthetic` (R26 tutor). The page records the samples of volunteers and children: "the first measurement" in the heading is the first on volunteers' samples.
- **A volunteer's sample** is brought into the eval set by the eval-set organizer, a maintainer of `modules`, and the volunteer needs no GitHub account (R04 modules). The page says "pass the file to the organizer", not "pull request", and the CONTRIBUTING of `.github` says that only the organizer brings in the samples of an eval set. What is in the volunteer's form is R126.
- **Children's samples** are needed before the beta (product 10). They are made with the same canvas and the same page, but the page opens no pull request: learners' work does not get into the repositories (concepts 3; R15). The file goes to the operator's closed bucket, to the measurement's organizer, for 2 years from the session (R125). The build for a child's session is downloaded from the release of `canvas` by the adult who runs the session, like any visitor of GitHub, and GitHub sees that adult's IP address; but the file holds neither a sample nor a child's data, and the sample goes nowhere by this path. The text of the separate consent to children's samples says so.

— *Why:*
- No hosting of its own while the volunteer writes: nobody's log sees their IP address, and what a hosting keeps of it the author weighs by R128 (Т-17).
- Without tasks the page will not get into the measurement for which it is built (repositories 6).
- The measurement does not need all devices at once.
- `tutor`'s board already had input, and the page of `canvas` had no release, when the measurement of the course of writing ran.

— *Rejected:*
- hosting the page before the author decides by R128 — for the iPad's sake, by Firebase Hosting, the IP addresses of the devices on which children's samples are made would land in Firebase's logs months before the lawyer saw them; by GitHub Pages of `canvas`, Pages records the IP address of each visitor, which is why hosting was avoided;
- the same origin as `app` — `app`'s erasures on the device would take the page's storage;
- for the iPad, an app that opens a local file with its own server — someone else's app with its own terms and its own data about the person; a laptop on the local network serving the build over `http://` — on an iPad this is not a secure context, and there is no `getCoalescedEvents` (R05 canvas);
- children's samples by a separate build — a second build for one measurement; in `app` — its code starts after the measurement (repositories 6); without children's samples, or only after the page moves to hosting — it diverges from product 10;
- the build brought to the device by whoever collects the samples — for the sake of the IP address of an adult who goes to the internet anyway;
- for the volunteers' and children's samples, waiting for `modules` and `module-kit` and until then writing them with the recording page of `tutor`; a task file that the adult opens on the page itself — a fallback path, if `tutor` does not release the file; tasks without the page — the volunteer types the task's number from the sheet of `tutor`, and the sheet then is not the one the learner has;
- a page that makes the sheets of the measurement of the course of writing — `tutor` gave them;
- a decision that rests on the volunteer opening a pull request on GitHub anyway — they need no GitHub account.

— *Consequence:* architecture 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12; repositories 2.1, 3, 6; concepts 15; Т-17; О-16; R114, R125, R126, R128.

**R26. One account may hold both the owner profile as a learner and the profiles of their children.** The recommendation on question В18. Privacy 2 and concepts 13 name such an account.
- **The own key** comes only with the owner profile of the category `adult` (R122), and who else may have one is still О-4. On an account that holds a profile of another category, the owner profile opens only by the PIN of the section for adults; the key lies on the device only if its owner decided so on this device, otherwise only in the tab's memory while the profile is open, and on the server only in the request's memory (R84).

- A parent who is learning Spanish themselves does not set up a second sign-in.
- Consent is still recorded for each learner (privacy 4).

— *Rejected:* two accounts with two sign-ins.

— *Consequence:* privacy 2, 4; concepts 13; О-4; R84, R98, R117, R122.

**R27. The random generator and the derivation of seeds from `spec` are one for `module-kit`, the widgets and `sim`; the algorithm is R59. The engine takes no randomness (R07 engine), so it takes no generator, and the seed in the record of its choice is empty (R107); the generator and the derivation come to `engine` only if its rule takes randomness by a new decision.** The recommendation on question В20; how its rejected option reads, the author's answer to В1 `engine`.
- architecture 1 already assigns the generator of `spec` to the reproducibility of the choice too, while the recommendation on the generator named only `module-kit` and the widgets.
- standalone's simulator, which moves to `sim`, derives seeds by a scheme of its own: the function `seeded` in `tools/learners/child.go` hashes four fields, `"%d|%s|%s|%s"` — the main seed, the experiment, the unit and the purpose — by FNV-64a, and takes `rand.NewPCG(hash, main seed)` ([mathtrail-standalone, commit 4dece74](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/4dece74/tools/learners/child.go), read 2026-10-27; the file has not changed since ca6a7c2). Two schemes on one platform would set the test vectors of `spec` and the simulator's seeds apart, so R59 takes it as it is, a special case of the platform's derivation.

— *Rejected:* a scheme of its own for `sim`; the engine's choice without randomness, as in standalone, given as a ready answer before the detailing of `engine` — the choice rule is not narrowed in advance: whether the engine needed randomness the detailing decided itself, by the facts an entry of `engine`'s log names; considering the question closed before it — R27 would have decided for the detailing what it left to it.

**R28. `learner-model` sets the graph's types, and `engine` takes them from it.** The types stay the libraries' own and simple, not from `module-kit` (architecture 3.8). — *Why:* the recommendation on question В21 put the choice off until the tasks of the two repositories; the option is the executor's proposal.

## Checks

**R30. The CI checks are the same for all NovaTrail repositories. The merge into `main` is held by all the checks but Scorecard, the quality gate of SonarCloud included, and, in `spec`, but the job "Orchestrator image". Which of them become shared workflows, `.github` itself decides.**
- **Each repository has:**
  - its own checks — what only it knows. In `spec` these are the job "Documents and tools", below. Repositories with code have the language checks, with the first code (repositories 6), and with them the shared license check of Go and TypeScript (architecture 3.11);
  - a secret search — with the gitleaks binary;
  - CodeQL — for the workflows, the language `actions`, and for the repository's languages;
  - OpenSSF Scorecard;
  - a DCO check: each commit of a pull request, but merge commits, has a `Signed-off-by` of its author (R22). It is a job of its own, without a third-party app;
  - SonarQube Cloud (SonarCloud) on the OSS plan, with Automatic Analysis;
  - GitHub's own means: secret scanning and push protection, private vulnerability reports, Dependabot.
- **What holds the merge.** Each repository has its own ruleset of the branch `main`:
  - only through a pull request, without approvals: there is one author;
  - the required checks are the repository's own jobs and the shared checks: "Secrets / gitleaks", "DCO / sign-off", "Documents / docs-check-repo" (in `spec`, its own "Documents and tools" instead) and "CodeQL / analyze (<language>)" — a check per language, `actions` in all —, with the language checks, as "Go / lint", "Go / test", "Go / vuln" and "Go / licenses". The GitHub Actions checks are bound to their app, `integration_id` 15368. With them, "SonarCloud Code Analysis", bound to SonarCloud's app, 12526, and, where coverage goes to Codecov, `codecov/patch`, bound to the Codecov app, 254 (R48). Scorecard, the jobs that upload coverage — "Coverage", "Go / coverage" — and `codecov/project`, which never arrives, are not required;
  - CodeQL's findings hold it by the rule "Require code scanning results", as R50 canvas-api: the tool CodeQL, the alert threshold — errors (`errors`), the security alert threshold — high and above (`high_or_higher`);
  - the branch is up to date before the merge, and the merge is only by a merge commit;
  - no force push and no deletion of the branch; the bypass list is empty.

  The ruleset, immutable releases and the ruleset of tags are GitHub settings: the author sets them, or the executor with the author's confirmation (rule 4 of RUN.md). A new check becomes required after its first green run on a pull request.
- **Secrets.** In the CI of any repository the shared workflows take no secrets, there is no `pull_request_target`, and a job without its secret, as on a pull request from a fork, fails and names the reason rather than being skipped (R24).
- **Where.** Which checks become shared workflows in `.github`, what their inputs are and how their SHAs are updated, `.github` decides in its own container (architecture 3.11), and so the texts of the calling files and the shared workflows (R03 .github). Who writes a repository's CI files:
  - **the session of `spec`** sets up a repository with the calling files that are the same for all, before there is any code (repositories 2.2), and makes the changes that are the same for all repositories;
  - **the session of the repository itself**, in its own container, writes what its code adds to the calling files: the job of its language in `ci.yml`, the input `languages` of CodeQL, the Dependabot ecosystem, `release.yml`, its own jobs, and raising the references to `.github` when a new job or input needs a new release. It takes the texts from architecture 3.3 .github, by the latest release of `.github`, and its own log records it; what is still to do with the first code is Д9.
- **The image.** The own checks run in the `toolchain` stage of the repository's devcontainer — with the same Node and just as locally. CI takes the image from the GitHub Actions cache, by the key `toolchain-<OS>-<architecture>-<sha256 .devcontainer/Dockerfile>`, and builds it only on a miss, while releases always build it from the Dockerfile (R31); where the cache is not in place yet is Д146. The image is published nowhere.
- **Versions.** Dependabot updates what it sees: actions together with the version comment, the references to `.github`, the base image, the languages' packages. Its security updates are enabled in all the repositories by the security configuration "NovaTrail", together with Dependabot alerts and the dependency graph; its security pull requests do not wait for the `cooldown` pause and, like any, pass the ruleset and CI. It does not see the `ARG`s in the Dockerfile, the VS Code extensions in `devcontainer.json` and in `repo-template/kinds.json`, and the Go tools that a recipe runs by `go run`: the executor checks them against the latest releases before each new tag of `spec`, as every new repository copies this devcontainer. The author turns off the auto-update of VS Code extensions in their user settings, `"extensions.autoUpdate": "off"`: it is an application-level setting, which `devcontainer.json` cannot turn off, and without it an extension that VS Code updated by itself would stay in the container's volume beside the exact version in `devcontainer.json`.
- **SHA.** The author enables in the organization "Require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA": GitHub checks the pinning, not review.
- **The checks of `spec`.** The required check "Documents and tools" of `ci.yml` runs no check itself: it needs the job "Checks", which runs every check of `spec` — `docs-check`, the license check of `tools/`, whose lock file only `spec` has, the step "Go module" (the recipe `go-check`), the step "Release files" (`release-files`) and the steps of the release's version and files —, and the three jobs "Tests (1/3)", "Tests (2/3)" and "Tests (3/3)", which run the tests of `tools/` in parts. It runs whatever they gave, `always()`, and passes only when all four succeeded and every module of `tools/` is in the report of some part. The ruleset of `main` of `spec` is 25424994.
  - **Coverage.** `just coverage` runs the tests of `tools/` in one run with coverage, and the Go tests through `ci-test`. A module of `tools/` that no test loads fails it: Node puts no such file in the report, and `codecov/patch` would not see its lines. Node measures only JavaScript: `toolchain.sh` and the bash recipes of the `justfile` have tests, but no coverage. The lcov reports go as artifacts to the job "Coverage", and that job sends them to Codecov by OIDC; it alone has the permission `id-token: write`. Any failure of it fails the run of a pull request, so that a missing `codecov/patch` has a visible cause; on `main` it has `continue-on-error`, as the release waits for green CI and a failure of Codecov must not hold it. The report is kept for a week: after a failure, the job can be rerun.
  - **Go.** CodeQL reads Go too, with the Go of the stage `toolchain`, and Dependabot watches `gomod` in `tools/gomod`. The job "Go" in `ci.yml` calls the shared `go.yml` of `.github` by SHA with the version beside it (R04 .github), with no inputs, and gives it `contents: read` and `id-token: write`: its job "Go / coverage" sends the profile `coverage/go.out` to Codecov by OIDC, a called workflow can only lower permissions, and without `id-token: write` the run does not start at all. `canvas` calls `typescript.yml` the same way (R43 canvas). A failure of "Go / coverage" fails the pull request and not the run of `main`, as `go.yml` is built. `go.yml` builds the stage `toolchain` from `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` without a context and runs in it one recipe per check, as the runner's user (R16 .github); the stage of `spec` copies nothing from the repository and builds so too, and gcc, without which there is no `-race`, comes from the base image.
  - **Four recipes** of the justfile follow the pattern of `module-kit` (R04 module-kit). Each checks all Go modules of `spec`: the root one and the modules of `tools/`, which `./...` from the root does not reach. A module is each `go.mod` that git knows, outside any `testdata/`, and a new module is checked with no change to the recipes:
    - `ci-lint` — `gofmt -l` over the Go files that git knows, and `go vet`;
    - `ci-test` — `go test -race`, with a coverage profile in `coverage/go.out`;
    - `ci-vuln` — govulncheck;
    - `ci-licenses` — go-licenses, by the list `ALLOWED_LICENSES` that `go.yml` gives, and without it by the own list of `spec`: the recipe `licenses-allowed` prints it (R12, R39), and `.github` compares the copy in `go.yml` with it too.

    A module of `tools/` is the own code of `spec` under the `LICENSE` in the root, and go-licenses looks for a license no higher than the module's root: "Did not find license for library 'github.com/altnovatrail/spec/tools/gomod'". So the recipe skips such a module's own packages (`--ignore`), and checks the packages it is built from: for `tools/gomod` — `golang.org/x/mod`, BSD-3-Clause, for `tools/types/roundtrip` — `spec` itself, Apache-2.0.

    The tools run through `go run` by an exact version, set in the justfile: the Go proxy serves it, and go checks it against the checksum database. They are raised by hand, like an `ARG` of the Dockerfile.
  - **`go-check`** checks what only it knows: that the root module requires nothing, and the zip of `HEAD` (R64). Vet and the tests of all modules are with `ci-lint` and `ci-test`.
  - **"Go / vuln"** fails on the run of `main` too, when a vulnerability appears in the vulnerability database in code that a module reaches — in the standard library of its Go as well. Then CI on `main` is red, and there is no release until Go in the Dockerfile or the dependency is raised. So it is in `module-kit` and `tutor` too: a check that passes with a known vulnerability would not hold it.
  - **govulncheck and go-licenses** are CI tools and ship nowhere, and they need no exception: govulncheck is BSD-3-Clause, go-licenses is Apache-2.0, and each package they are built from is under a license of category A. For govulncheck these are `golang.org/x/vuln`, `x/tools`, `x/mod`, `x/sync` and `x/telemetry`, all BSD-3-Clause; for go-licenses — Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, ISC and MIT (`go-licenses report` on each, 2026-11-01). The Go telemetry of govulncheck is in its default mode: "When `mode` is `local`, telemetry data is collected and stored on the local computer, but never uploaded to remote servers" ([Go Telemetry](https://go.dev/doc/telemetry), read 2026-11-01), and nobody calls `go telemetry on`.
  - **"Orchestrator image".** The workflow `orchestrator.yml` builds the stage `orchestrator` of `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` on `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm` and runs `docker ps` in it with the runner's socket (R156). It runs only when `.devcontainer/` or the workflow changes, and it is not required: it checks no file of the repository, no check runs in that stage, and a required check whose workflow a filter of paths skips stays "Pending" and blocks the merge (sources 6.2). A red run is seen on the pull request and named in the task's report.

— *Why:* the author's decisions of 2026-10-19: SonarCloud holds the merge and analyses by itself, the image is published nowhere, versions outside Dependabot are checked by hand, the DCO is checked, `.github` decides the shared workflows. The list of checks, the details of the ruleset, Scorecard not holding the merge, and pinning by SHA for the whole organization are the proposal of the plan the author approved on 2026-10-19. Who writes the CI files is the author's decision of 2026-10-21, by the recommendation of `tutor`; the coverage of `spec` and its required check, the author's decision of 2026-10-23; the Go checks of `spec`, the author's answers of 2026-10-28 and 2026-11-01, by the plan's recommendations, and what goes beyond them is the plan's proposals. Scorecard runs only on `main` and on a schedule: "The following GitHub triggers are supported: `push`, `schedule` (default branch only). The `pull_request` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers are experimental" ([ossf/scorecard-action, README](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard-action), read 2026-10-19). A pull request has no result of it. The other arguments are from the documentation, read 2026-10-19 unless said:
- **A ruleset in each repository.** "Rulesets are available in public repositories with GitHub Free and GitHub Free for organizations" ([GitHub Docs, About rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)). Rules for the whole organization are not: "For customers on GitHub Team or GitHub Enterprise plans you can create rulesets in your organization" ([GitHub Docs, Creating rulesets for repositories in your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/creating-rulesets-for-repositories-in-your-organization)). The organization is on the Free plan.
- **Shared workflows.** A workflow from another repository can be called if "The called workflow is stored in a public repository, and your organization allows you to use public reusable workflows" ([GitHub Docs, Reusing workflow configurations](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/reusing-workflow-configurations)). Pin by SHA: "Using the commit SHA is the safest option for stability and security" ([GitHub Docs, Reuse workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/reuse-automations/reuse-workflows)). A required check from it is named "`<job name> / <reusable job name>`" ([GitHub Docs, Troubleshooting rules](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/troubleshooting-rules)).
- **It costs no money.** The repositories are public (R18):
  - "GitHub Actions usage is **free** for **self-hosted runners** and for **public repositories** that use standard GitHub-hosted runners" ([GitHub Docs, GitHub Actions billing](https://docs.github.com/en/billing/concepts/product-billing/github-actions));
  - "Code scanning is available for the following repository types: Public repositories on GitHub.com" ([GitHub Docs, Code scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/code-scanning));
  - for public repositories "Secret scanning runs automatically for free" ([GitHub Docs, About secret scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/introduction/about-secret-scanning));
  - "Public, OSI-licensed repos get SonarQube for OSS and Gitar AI Code Review for OSS, with the same features as the paid Pro plan" ([SonarQube Cloud, Plans and pricing](https://www.sonarsource.com/plans-and-pricing/sonarcloud/)).
- **SonarCloud.**
  - It holds the merge by its own check: "SonarQube Cloud adds the quality gate status as a GitHub check" ([SonarQube Cloud, GitHub integration](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-cloud/managing-your-projects/administering-your-projects/devops-platform-integration/github)).
  - Automatic analysis and analysis in CI do not work together: "Automatic analysis is not intended to be used in conjunction with CI-based analysis". It accepts no coverage: "Code coverage information is not supported" ([SonarQube Cloud, Automatic analysis](https://docs.sonarsource.com/sonarqube-cloud/analyzing-source-code/automatic-analysis)).
  - Analysis in CI needs a token, and a pull request from a fork will not get it: "With the exception of `GITHUB_TOKEN`, secrets are not passed to the runner when a workflow is triggered from a forked repository" ([GitHub Docs, Using secrets in GitHub Actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-secrets)). The required check of such a pull request would not come at all.
- **The rule for CodeQL's findings.** The check "CodeQL / analyze" is green if the analysis ran, even when it found a vulnerability, while the rule holds the merge when "A required tool finds a code scanning alert of a severity that is defined in the ruleset", and also when "A required tool's analysis is still in progress" or "A required tool is not configured for the repository" ([GitHub Docs, Available rules for rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets), read 2026-10-20). The apps the checks are bound to were read in the ruleset `main` of `spec` by the GitHub API, 2026-10-20.
- **DCO.** GitHub does not check the sign-off of commits from the command line, so a contribution without it could be merged unnoticed. A squash puts a new commit on `main`: "When you select the Squash and merge option on a pull request, the pull request's commits are squashed into a single commit", and "When you squash and merge, GitHub generates a default commit message that you can edit" ([GitHub Docs, About pull request merges](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/collaborating-with-pull-requests/incorporating-changes-from-a-pull-request/about-pull-request-merges), read 2026-10-20). Nobody checks the sign-off in such a message. With a merge commit, exactly the commits that the DCO checked land on `main`.
- **`codecov/patch`.** A required check bound to an app needs the app to be sending it already: "The app must be installed in the repository with the `statuses:write` permission, must have recently submitted a check run, and must be associated with a pre-existing required status check in the ruleset" ([GitHub Docs, Available rules for rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#require-status-checks-to-pass-before-merging), read 2026-10-23). Codecov sets it as a check run of its app, as on pull request #144 of standalone, whose ruleset of `main`, 23788682, binds it so (the GitHub API, 2026-10-23). GitHub's documentation says two things about the permissions of Dependabot's runs, and without OIDC a required check would hold every pull request of Dependabot: it became required once the first pull requests of Dependabot in `spec`, #40–#42, got an OIDC token and `codecov/patch` arrived on them, 2026-10-23. The job "Coverage" is not required: without the upload `codecov/patch` does not arrive, and the merge waits anyway. `continue-on-error` "Prevents a workflow run from failing when a job fails" ([GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idcontinue-on-error), read 2026-10-23).
- **The tests in parts.** The tests of `tools/` took most of the time of the slowest job of `spec`'s CI (measurements 3.1). A job that a condition skips gives a required check that passes, so "Documents and tools" runs always and fails on a part that failed or was cancelled.
- **Versions.** The Dependabot ecosystem for devcontainers is only Features: "to update Features in your `devcontainer.json` configuration files" ([GitHub Docs, Dependabot supported ecosystems and repositories](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/ecosystems-supported-by-dependabot/supported-ecosystems-and-repositories)). And actions pinned by SHA it keeps together with the comment: "Dependabot updates the version documentation of GitHub Actions when the comment is on the same line" (ibid.). The API accepted the security updates only together with the alerts and the graph: "Dependabot alerts must be enabled when Dependabot security updates is enabled" and "Dependency graph must be enabled when Dependabot alerts is enabled" (the API's responses, 2026-10-19); in public repositories both are enabled anyway.
- **SHA.** "When you enable **Require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA**, all actions must be pinned to a full-length commit SHA to be used" ([GitHub Docs, Disabling or limiting GitHub Actions for your organization](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/disabling-or-limiting-github-actions-for-your-organization)).
- **Who writes the CI files.** These lines come together with the code they check: a language's job without code fails, and code without its job goes to `main` unchecked, as it did in `tutor` (R13 tutor). `module-kit` added in its own session the input `go` of CodeQL and `release.yml` (R06, R07 module-kit), and `tutor` wrote itself the job "Go", the input `go` of CodeQL and the ecosystem `gomod`, and raised its references to `.github`. The texts are ready to copy and checked in architecture 3.3 .github: there is nothing in them for the session of `spec` to decide. R03 .github's exception for `module-kit`, whose files the session of `.github` wrote, stays an exception.
- **"Orchestrator image".** The stage is built nowhere else — the devcontainer has no Docker —, and building it on every pull request would download all its tools and Docker's 82 MB each time, for changes that cannot touch it; an edit of the stage still misses the cache of `toolchain`, whose key is the whole Dockerfile's sha256, until a run on `main` saves it again.

— *Rejected:*
- `gitleaks-action`: "Since v2.0.0 of Gitleaks-Action, the license has changed from MIT to a license" — it is the EULA of Gitleaks LLC. And an organization needs a key: "Clicking "Sign Up" will take you to a google form where you will need to supply name, email, and company" ([gitleaks-action, README](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks-action), read 2026-10-19). gitleaks itself is under MIT;
- SonarCloud that only reports, as in MathTrail (R50 canvas-api, R31 standalone): the author decided that its quality gate holds the merge;
- SonarCloud analysis in CI now: a token in the secrets and pull requests from forks without a check, and its action under LGPL-3.0 would have to be named an exception of the license rule. Return to it when the quality gate needs code coverage;
- Renovate: it does not see VS Code extensions either — its devcontainer manager "Extracts all Docker images from the image and features properties" ([Renovate, devcontainer manager](https://docs.renovatebot.com/modules/manager/devcontainer/), read 2026-10-19). It would raise the `ARG`s, but at the cost of a second update bot beside Dependabot and a third-party app with write access;
- a signed image in GHCR, as in canvas-api: R49, R53 — a whole mechanism for one check of documents. Return when building the image becomes long; `.github` decides;
- the DCO app — a third party with its own terms;
- organization rulesets — they do not exist on the Free plan;
- a required check "CodeQL" from GitHub Advanced Security — its thresholds are set in each repository's settings, not in the ruleset; no rule for findings at all — then the merge would be held only by the analysis itself;
- merge and rebase, or all three ways of merging;
- the session of `spec` writing every CI file, or an exception for `tutor` alone: each next language, input of CodeQL or release — for `tutor` its release and the recipe of compatibility with `canvas` in CI — would wait for a session of `spec` or a new exception;
- golangci-lint, as in `tutor` (R12 tutor): a named exception for GPL-3.0 and a binary in the stage `toolchain`, for a module whose code is a wrapper over files, and for two CI tools;
- a copy of `LICENSE` in each module of `tools/`: a file that has to be kept the same as the root's, for a check that the code of `spec` is under the license of `spec`;
- Go coverage as a separate recipe: the Go tests would run two ways, and the contract of `ci-test` already tells the recipe to write the report;
- `go-check` with vet and the tests: vet would run in CI twice, and the tests three times, under three names;
- `ALLOWED_LICENSES` required, as in `module-kit`: in `spec` this list is its own;
- "Orchestrator image" as a job in `ci.yml` on every run; as a required check with a filter of paths.

— *Consequence:* architecture 3.11; repositories 2.2, 2.3, 5; README.md; CLAUDE.md, Environment; R12, which names the tools that do not ship; R31, R48, R64, R156; `.github/workflows/`; the justfile; `run/DEBT.md`, Д9, Д146.

## Releases

**R31. A release of `spec` comes out by itself: after green CI on `main`, the next patch of the line, the tag together with the release; nobody sets tags by hand. The release is immutable and GitHub's attestation signs it; from line 0.3 it carries the format's files, signed by cosign, and from line 0.7 a second tag, `contracts/<tag>`. The recipes that the releases of all repositories share live in `spec`, in one copy, and reach the callers with the tag.** The author's decision of 2026-10-19 and their answers since: to В8–В10, В16, В18, В25 and В28 of `.github`, В6 of `module-kit` and В65 of `canvas`, each by its recommendation, to Т-11, and their decisions of 2026-11-09 and of 2026-11-15 on the speed of CI.
- **The workflow** is the own `.github/workflows/release.yml` of `spec`, after the pattern of canvas-api: its `release.yml` and the recipe `release-version`, commit 0901af0 (R52 canvas-api). It starts after a run of CI on `main` — only a successful one, only from a push and only from the repository itself. The button releases the tip of `main` that has no release yet, works only on `main` after green CI of that commit, and sets no numbers. The release runs go in a queue, `queue: max`: "Up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can be `pending` in the concurrency group" ([GitHub Docs, Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax), read 2026-10-19), so every commit gets a release, not only the last.
- **Checkout without the event's commit.** `release.yml` takes `main` as it is and names the commit on which CI passed only by its SHA: the recipe `release-version` gets it as an argument and reads `RELEASE_LINE` from the `release.yml` of that commit, which is in the history of `main`, and the ruleset of `main` lets nobody rewrite it. A checkout of the event's commit is what Scorecard marks as Dangerous-Workflow: the trigger `workflow_run` "in conjunction with an explicit pull request checkout", and "This check does not detect whether untrusted code checkouts are used safely" ([Scorecard, docs/checks.md](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/6d4113e/docs/checks.md), read 2026-10-20), so a condition of the job that lets in only a push from the repository itself does not save the score. The price: the image and the recipes are the tip's. The files are still built from the event's commit: the tip's recipe reads only the objects of that commit, by `git archive`.
- **Copies of the checkout.** The number step, before the first container, takes a copy of the checkout — `cp -a` into `RUNNER_TEMP`, with all the history and tags — and runs `tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` from it. After a refusal of the Releases API, `release-refusal` runs in a new copy taken after `git fetch`, and the files are built in a new copy too: the first copy lacks the new tip, and its container could have changed it. The runner's `git` reads only the checkout itself, and no container mounts it. The script's checksum is not compared: the script never runs from a copy after its container. The script's contract stays: `run` mounts the folder it is called from. The price is a copy of the checkout on the runner's disk; the `.git` of `spec` weighs 15 MB.
- **The number** is the next patch of the line `RELEASE_LINE` in `release.yml`, computed by `just release-version`: `tools/release/version.mjs`, with tests. A commit is released once. The number only goes forward along the history of `main`: a commit whose history does not hold the newest release — an old commit whose CI passed late or again — gets no release. A line above the newest release starts from `.0`, and a line below it is an error. Tags not of the form `vX.Y.Z` do not count as releases — for `just new-repo` either, which takes the newest release by the same function.
- **A new line** comes by a change of `RELEASE_LINE` in the pull request that deserves it:
  - one that gives the module format a new version (R44), so that within one line the format is one: `release-version` refuses a commit that gives the format a new version in the line of the previous release, `tools/release/format-line.mjs`. A major version of the format raises the major version of `spec` too: while the format is v0, `spec` stays 0.x, and format v1 comes out with `spec` v1.0.0;
  - a breaking change of a contract, or a change of its meaning (R83): a contract's version is the suffix of its protobuf package and the tag of `spec`; an edit within a package only adds and comes out in any release of the line, and a breaking change is a new package `v2` and opens a new line, which `release-version` holds. The eval protocol is such a contract, `novatrail.eval.v1`;
  - a new version of another normative part with a version of its own: the admission table (R96), the deployment configuration (R85), the legal texts (R130), the table of the age of digital consent (R134) and the export format (R135). The widget protocol is still epic E5's;
  - one that brings a new kind of file into the release, so that a rerun of an old release builds the files it got.
- **The number for another repository.** `version.mjs` takes the line from the environment variable `RELEASE_LINE`, if it is set, and otherwise from the `release.yml` of `spec`; the recipe counts the tags of the repository it is called from. `just -f spec/justfile release-version <commit> <workflow>` outside `spec` reads `RELEASE_LINE` from the named workflow on that commit, whatever the environment sets — the `env` is the tip workflow's —, so the commit counts in the line in which it was made; a commit older than the workflow takes the line from its copy in the checkout, and the environment's variable counts only when no workflow is named. Without either the recipe does not work outside `spec`: another repository has a line of its own. In `spec` the recipe rejects a second argument. The caller calls the recipe as it is: it needs neither a copy of the wrapping nor the internal `tools/release/line.mjs`, which can be renamed without breaking another repository's release.
- **The release** gives the other repositories the tag itself, as a submodule (R21). The releases of `spec` are immutable, and the tag is locked on its commit: "its associated Git tag is locked to a specific commit, cannot be changed, and cannot be deleted while the release exists". The attestation that GitHub creates itself signs it: "a cryptographically verifiable record of a release containing the release tag, commit SHA, and release assets" ([GitHub Docs, Immutable releases](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/immutable-releases), read 2026-10-19). The check is `gh release verify <tag> -R altnovatrail/spec`, which the workflow runs itself too.
- **The files** (R64). A release of line 0.3 and newer carries `format-<version>.tar.gz` and its cosign bundle `<file>.sigstore.json`; v0.3.0 released format version 0.1. A release of a line before 0.3 — and the release of such a commit whose CI finished late — carries no files: the recipe `release-files` reads the line of the commit itself. The cosign signature stands on top of the attestation, since Scorecard Signed-Releases looks for signatures among the files and does not read the attestation. A draft with files, left by an interrupted run, is deleted by the publishing before the release is created and after a refusal. The release check downloads the files, compares them with the list of those built and checks each with `gh release verify-asset`; the step "Verify the Go module" checks the Go module of the release through the Go proxy.
- **The tag of the contracts.** From line 0.7, once the release is out and checked, the release sets `contracts/<tag>` on the same commit, the version of the Go module of the contracts. A tag `contracts/<tag>` on another commit the workflow takes as set by hand and fails on it.
- **The tags** `v*` and `contracts/v*` are protected by the ruleset "v-tags": moving, deleting and force push are forbidden, and nobody has a bypass. It does not restrict creation: GitHub does not accept a bypass for GitHub Actions — "Actor GitHub Actions integration must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization" (the API's answer, 2026-10-19). So the rule "only the release workflow sets tags" is held by this decision, not by a setting. A tag `v*` without a release — on the commit itself, or a newest "release" outside the history of `main` — the workflow takes as set by hand and fails on it: otherwise such a tag would silently stop all releases.
- **A refusal of the Releases API.** The publishing step runs with `pipefail`: an empty tip of `main` is an error, not "not the tip". After a refusal, `main` is fetched again, and the rule of when the refusal is skipped is the recipe `release-refusal <commit> <tip> <error file>`, in one copy: the commit is no longer the tip of `main` but is in its history — only then does the release of the tip cover it —, it adds or changes files `.github/workflows/` relative to the tip, which is the cause the documentation names, and the answer is 404 or "403 Resource not accessible by integration": "Otherwise, this endpoint returns 404 Not Found; some authentication paths surface 403 Resource not accessible by integration instead" ([GitHub Docs, REST API endpoints for releases](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/releases/releases), read 2026-10-20). A refusal can come both on creating the draft and on publishing it, and gh's error names HTTP 404 or 403 in both. The recipe exits with 0 when the refusal is that one, and with 1 and a reason in every other case, so an unclear refusal still fails the run. The `release.yml` of `spec` calls it in the stage of the release with the runner's temporary directory mounted read-only, and a release of another repository calls it the same way. The price is the tests of the recipe and one more start of the stage in the publishing step, only after a refusal.
- **The script** `tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh`, one copy for everyone, runs recipes in the stage of the Dockerfile on the runner. The runner runs it with its own shell from the repository's root: CI and the release of `spec` from `tools/`, the release of another repository from its submodule `spec/`, at the tag it is on.
  - `build` builds the stage from the repository's `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; `run` runs a command in it as the runner's user, with the home in `/tmp`, the repository in `/work` and the runner's temporary directory mounted read-only; `spec` runs in the same way a recipe from the justfile of `spec`, wherever it lies: `release-version`, `release-refusal`, `docs-check-repo` and the license recipes (R39).
  - How the stage is built and how a command runs in it is written once and reaches the callers with the tag. The script cannot be a `just` recipe: just is in the stage itself, and calling a recipe takes the `docker run` that the script does.
  - **The probe.** Before the number, the caller calls `spec --dry-run release-refusal` with the arguments the publishing step will give: a dry run of just parses the call and runs nothing, so a tag of `spec` in which the recipe disappeared or takes another number of arguments stops the run that moved to that tag, not the run of a refusal. The probe does not see arguments swapped. `spec` has none: the script, the recipes and their tests are one commit here.
  - **Quoting.** Paths go to docker as arguments, not as the text of a script, so `$`, the backquote, `"` and `\` in `$PWD` or `$RUNNER_TEMP` break nothing. A path with a colon the script rejects: docker splits `--volume` on it. The tests of the script with a fake docker check this — the recipe `just toolchain-test`.
- **The stages.** The release builds the stage `toolchain-core` — Node, just, Go and buf —, from the Dockerfile and with no cache. The stage `toolchain` is built over it with what the repository's tests need — in a copy of the kind `typescript` the browsers and their system packages (R79), in `spec` nothing —, and CI runs the checks in it; a release builds it only where its own recipes need a browser. `toolchain.sh build` takes the stage from the environment variable `TOOLCHAIN_STAGE`: unset, empty or `toolchain` — `toolchain`; `toolchain-core` — that stage, and a Dockerfile that has no such stage gets `toolchain`, with a notice; any other value stops the script. The image is `novatrail-toolchain` whichever the stage, and a caller that keeps both stages in the cache keys them by the stage. The `release.yml` of `spec` sets `TOOLCHAIN_STAGE=toolchain-core` and gains no time, since its `toolchain` adds nothing.
- **The cache of the image.** CI takes the image of the stage `toolchain` from the GitHub Actions cache, as R57 canvas does: a file of `docker save` by the key `toolchain-<OS>-<architecture>-<sha256 .devcontainer/Dockerfile>`; `actions/cache` restores it before the build and saves it right after the build, only on a miss, and the scope of `main` is filled by the run of CI on a push to `main`. The `go.yml` and `typescript.yml` of `.github`, which build the image without the submodule `spec`, do the same in their own steps by the same key, and the job "Go" of `spec` runs by that `go.yml`; the repositories still to move to the cached release of `.github` are Д146. The releases — the `release.yml` of `spec` and the shared one of `.github` — take no cache: the image of the job that signs the files is built from the Dockerfile.
  - `toolchain.sh build` takes the image file from the environment variable `TOOLCHAIN_IMAGE_FILE`, a full path that the caller sets; empty or unset means building the stage, and the releases do not set it.
  - The file is there: `docker load --quiet --input <file>` and `docker image inspect novatrail-toolchain`; if both succeed, the file is deleted and there is no build. The file did not load or gave no image: it is deleted, `::warning::`, the stage is built, and the file is not written.
  - There is no file: the build and `docker save --output <file> novatrail-toolchain`; a failed save gives `::warning::`, deletes the unfinished file and exits with 0, and a failed build gives its code.
  - The warning is a workflow command without the path, and the path is a line in stderr; it tells to delete the broken cache entry: an entry is immutable, and otherwise the hit would repeat.
- **The `paths` of another repository's release.** A release of another repository is given only by the files its output is built from: the pattern `paths` of its calling `release.yml` is their list, by the kind of the repository, not everything but exceptions. The list of each kind is held by the pattern in architecture 3.3 .github, which also writes how the rule applies to files that code embeds through `//go:embed` and to code in `testdata/`; here is only the rule: the list holds what the output is built from and what the consumer will get, and `release.yml`, so that a change of the line gives a release. The caller takes the pattern in a task of its own, like everything the repository's code adds to its CI files (R30). `spec` has no `paths` of its own: its release comes out after every green CI on `main`. The price is the changes that give a release without changing the output: the tools of the stage `devcontainer` in the Dockerfile, raising the reference to the shared `release.yml` of `.github`, and a new base image in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, which is in the list whole since the stage `toolchain` is built in it. Dependabot offers the last two once a week, and its pause `cooldown` does not hold the image: Microsoft's registry does not report the image's release date (architecture 3.3 and 3.5 .github). The price is named in full so that a new image is not taken for an error in `paths`.
- **The orchestrator's merges** (R156) are merges like any other: the release of `spec`, and of another repository by its `release.yml`, comes out by itself after green CI on `main`, and the orchestrator sets no tag and presses no button. Where the ruleset of `main` requires an up-to-date branch, it updates the branch and waits for the new checks before the merge. A wave that takes a new tag — wave 0, onto the latest tag of `spec` — waits for that release, not for the merge.

— *Why:*
- The author's decision of 2026-10-19: «релиз должен быть автоматическим», as in canvas-api: "Nobody tags anything by hand: the version is the next patch of the line the releases are numbered in, and the tag is created with the release" (`release.yml` of canvas-api, commit 0901af0). A workflow of its own, a release on every green `main`, an immutable release and protection of the tags without forbidding their creation are the author's decisions of that day. The submodules of all repositories and `just new-repo` depend on the tag of `spec`, and a manual tag can be forgotten, set on the wrong commit, or on a commit with red CI. A release on every `main` does not hurry the other repositories: each moves to a new tag in a task of its own (RULES.md, Across repositories). A release created with `GITHUB_TOKEN` starts no other workflows: "events triggered by the `GITHUB_TOKEN` will not create a new workflow run" ([GitHub Docs, GITHUB_TOKEN](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/github_token), read 2026-10-19).
- One copy of the rule of refusal, of the line and of the script: the workflows of `.github` repeated the script and the probe of the `release.yml` of `spec`, and a note in the `ci.yml` of `spec`, "a change here goes there", linked only two copies within `spec` itself. «Если новый рецепт потребует другого запуска — тома, переменной, флага, — до `.github` правка дойдёт не с тегом, а руками, и сломаться может как раз путь отказа» (В18 `.github`).
- The copies of the checkout: each container of the script gets write access to the folder it was started from and to its `.git`, and the release ran `release-version` in the checkout itself; after that container the runner worked in the same checkout, with `GH_TOKEN` and `contents: write`: the publishing step did `git fetch` by `.git/config`, a refusal called the script from the same checkout, and the post step of `actions/checkout` runs `git config` and `git submodule foreach` there (architecture 4 .github). The change passed the trial #54 in `.github`, one file of `spec` with the script's contract as before, and a local check of 2026-10-22, the steps of `release.yml` word for word with docker and `gh` faked: the script and `.git/config` of the checkout stayed the same, and `release-refusal` in the new copy saw the new tip. Only the release has a write token; CI runs with `contents: read` (`ci.yml`).
- The `paths`: a release of a library is when what its consumers get changes, as `module-kit` recommended in В6. The exceptions gave a release on any test, on Claude Code, gh or just-lsp in the stage `devcontainer`, on `devcontainer.json`, `.claude/` or `.gitignore`, and Dependabot would offer each such tag to the consumers, which R18 .github wanted to avoid. `spec` decides: the rule is one for all repositories with releases, and `.github` gave this choice to В6 of `module-kit`. A list written in two places diverges, and it did: the list for Go first written here, `**/*.go`, missed the Go files in the root, since in a git pathspec without the magic `glob` `*` matches `/` and `**/` requires a slash (a trial of 2026-11-01, git 2.56.0; architecture 4 .github); the pattern was corrected, and the decision was not.
- The cache: the Dockerfile pins everything by exact versions and checksums (R34, R40), so the image from the cache is the one it would have built, and on a hit the Dockerfile does not run and needs no network to nodejs.org, GitHub and the snapshot of the Ubuntu archive. On 2026-11-09 the build of the stage failed in `canvas` on nodejs.org and in `spec` on the archive of just from github.com: `curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 504` after three retries, in three attempts of the four of the CI run 42569536919. Only runs on `main` write to the scope of `main`: "When a cache is created by a workflow run triggered on a pull request, the cache is created for the merge ref (`refs/pull/.../merge`). Because of this, the cache will have a limited scope and can only be restored by re-runs of the pull request"; the limit is "10 GB per repository" ([GitHub Docs, Dependency caching reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching), read 2026-11-09), and the entry of the image of `canvas` is about 575 MB.
- `TOOLCHAIN_IMAGE_FILE` and `TOOLCHAIN_STAGE` are variables, not arguments: the workflows of `.github` call the script of the caller's submodule at whatever tag it is on — `documents.yml` since `v0.2.17` —, and an older `build` refuses any argument; an older script ignores the variable and builds `toolchain`, which holds all the core does, so the tag need not be checked, and the fallback holds a repository whose submodule has moved before its `.devcontainer/`. `image inspect` after `load` is needed because a file with another image would load "successfully", and the next `docker run novatrail-toolchain` would go for the image to Docker Hub. A file that was there is a hit, and no save follows it: a cache entry is immutable.
- The stage `toolchain-core`: the release of `app` built the whole stage, three browsers and 341 packages of apt, for `release-version`: its step "Work out the version" took 391 s, and that of `canvas` up to 826 s (measurements 3.1). No recipe a release runs — `release-version`, `release-files`, `release-verify`, `release-refusal` and the check of the Go module — needs more than its four tools.

— *Rejected:*
- manual tags, as it was with `v0.1.0`;
- a release only by the button: it would again depend on whether someone forgot to release it;
- a number set by the button: a new number comes only with `RELEASE_LINE`;
- a shared "signed release" from `.github` now (architecture 3.11): `spec` has no code, and `.github` itself needs the first tag with R30;
- a GitHub App of our own, the only one allowed to create the tags `v*`: one more secret and one more actor with write permission;
- closing Dangerous-Workflow as false, with a reason, as R51 canvas-api: the Scorecard score for the check would stay 0, and the pattern would go into the next releases;
- the release as a job in CI, without `workflow_run`: a file of another kind, a job with `contents: write` in CI, and a skipped check "Release" on every pull request;
- leaving the wrappings of the recipes with the callers and comparing them at each move to a tag of `spec`, or keeping the copies of the script and extending the note of `spec` to the copies outside it: the rule would live in two copies, and a change of `spec` would not reach them with the tag; leaving the copies as they were;
- the script's own mode `spec` running the recipe in a copy of the folder it is called from: it would close the path for every caller, and `.github` would drop its own copy, but the recipes with `_tools` would install the npm packages anew in each copy, and the checkout cannot be mounted read-only, since `_tools` writes `tools/node_modules`;
- accepting the release in the checkout itself, since its containers run the same commit of `spec` as `release.yml` and the image's tools are pinned: the protection costs one `cp -a`, and without it the release of `spec` would remain the only one in NovaTrail where the runner reads `.git` after a container;
- a copy with hard links, `git worktree add` and `git clone` from the checkout, by the arguments `.github` gave for its own releases: a file that the container changes in place would change in the checkout too, and the working copy of `git worktree` shares `.git` with it;
- the `paths` as exceptions, or as exceptions with the line changed together with a change of code: any test and any tool of the devcontainer would give a release;
- the list of each kind written here: two places that have to be kept the same, and whoever reads R31 and not the pattern would write `**/*.go`, so a change of Go code in the root would give no release; the rules of `//go:embed` and `testdata/` here: it is the same rule, and how it applies to Go is a detail of the pattern;
- buildx with the cache `type=gha`: two actions `docker/*` instead of one, as `canvas` rejected too; only retries of downloads: longer, each job still downloads everything, and a long failure brings the check down; the cache for the release too: the image of the job with the signing permission would be held by a cache entry and not by the Dockerfile, and a failed release is rerun; not caching;
- an argument `build <file>` or `build <stage>`: an older script refuses it; an explicit `env -u` in the release: nobody sets the variable there;
- a Dockerfile of the release's own: a second copy of the pins to keep the same; the release in `toolchain`: the cost above.

— *Consequence:* R21; R44; R64; R83; repositories 2.2, 5; architecture 3.11; `.github/workflows/release.yml`; `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; `tools/release/`; `tools/toolchain/toolchain.sh` and its tests; `tools/new-repo`; R03–R05 and R18 .github; architecture 3.3, 3.5 and 4 .github.

## The documents check

**R32. The documents of a NovaTrail repository other than `spec`, and the numbers of decisions in its comments of code, are checked by the `docs-check` of the `spec` its submodule is on. Citations of `spec` are checked against that submodule, and examples of citations are written in inline code.** The author's decisions of 2026-10-19 in the planning of T18 and the author's answers since to the rows «в реестр spec» `.github` В22, `tutor` В29 and `sim` В5; the comments of code by R160 (T205).
- **Running.** From the repository's root, `just -f spec/justfile docs-check-repo`; `_tools` installs the dependencies of `tools/` into `spec/tools/node_modules`, which `.gitignore` keeps out. The repository needs no justfile of its own: it comes with code (repositories 1). The root is `spec`, where the script lies, or with `--component` the repository around its `spec/` submodule, never a path from the command line: as git's working folder such a path would let whoever writes the command run git in any folder (SonarCloud, pull request #47: jssecurity:S8705 and S8707). git runs with `-c core.fsmonitor=false`, since `git ls-files` runs the hook `core.fsmonitor` of `.git/config` (a trial of 2026-10-26 on git 2.56.0).
- **What is read.** In a root with a `.git` of its own — a repository, the `spec/` submodule, a copy `just new-repo` built — the files `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-per-directory=.gitignore` lists: the tracked ones still in the working tree and the new ones the repository's own `.gitignore` files do not keep out. git does not enter a folder it ignores, so `samples/` of `tutor` stays unread (the same trial). The rules come from `.gitignore` alone, since `--exclude-standard` adds ".git/info/exclude … and the user's global exclusion file" ([git-ls-files](https://github.com/git/git/blob/v2.56.0/Documentation/git-ls-files.adoc), v2.56.0, read 2026-10-26), and the list would depend on the machine. If git gives no list, the check says so in one line. A root without `.git` — a draft of `just new-repo`, the tests' copies — is walked whole. `tools/docs-check/config.mjs` skips `spec/` in a repository, and the fixtures and `.repos/` in `spec`.
- **What is checked** in the repository, without `spec/`:
