  - links and anchors, into `spec/` too;
  - its own sections — `architecture 2`, `sources 1.1`, `measurements 1` without a suffix; a document it does not have yet is an error only where a link leads to it — and those of `spec`'s documents, `architecture 3.8 spec`;
  - its own log of R, empty with the next number R01 until the first decision, and `spec`'s numbers: `R18 spec` by `spec`'s log, О-, П-, Т- always by `spec`'s registers;
  - the tables «В» and «Д»: table 3 of `run/QUESTIONS.md` and table 4 of `run/DEBT.md`, under the headings «Table 3.» and «Table 4.» (R153, R154); a number does not repeat, and the next free one is above each; rows leave, so gaps are allowed and their citations are not checked; a table left in RUN.md or `DEBT.md` beside `run/`, under either heading or its Russian «Таблица N.», is a second copy, an error;
  - Mermaid diagrams, the rules of `.claude/rules/`, and the budgets of size (R145);
  - the numbers of decisions in comments of code, below.

  What is wrong in `spec` itself is `spec`'s to report.
- **How citations are read.**
  - «раздел N» or `section N` without a link, in a document with no numbered sections of its own — RUN.md —, is a section of `docs/architecture.md`. Right after an external link, after the name of a MathTrail repository and a comma — "`docs/spec.md` canvas-api, section 4.2" —, in an item nested under one whose last link is external, or before «лицензии», `of` or `in` — `section 3 of the license`, `sections 9–11 in SB 297` —, it is a section of another text, and not checked.
  - A document of `spec` cited without its suffix is an error, with a hint on how to cite it.
  - The name of a NovaTrail or MathTrail repository after a number or a section is a suffix wherever a word boundary follows it, a name that is also a word of prose included: `R03 modules сравнивает граф` is R03 of `modules`, `R10 engine решил` R10 of `engine`. An own citation never puts a repository's name after it as a word of prose. After О-, П- and Т- a NovaTrail name is a word of the sentence: those registers are `spec`'s alone. A list `canvas-api: R37, R38` knows the names of MathTrail alone. `tools/docs-check/citations.mjs` holds the names.
  - A register's opening is read in English and Russian — `Next number — R145`, `the next free number — Т-40`, `next — В34`, «Следующий номер — R32» —, and so are lists, with `and` or «и».
  - A range's last number is a section whatever follows it, `measurements 1.1–1.99 records`; a number after a comma or «и» and before a word is a count, `product 7, 12 модулей`, and so is a range there.
- **Comments of code** (R160). Each `R…` in a comment of Go, TypeScript and JavaScript — `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs` —, `.proto`, `.jsonc` and `devcontainer.json` files, and in the `#` comments of `.sh`, YAML, justfiles and Dockerfiles, names an entry of its log: without a suffix the repository's own, `R25 spec` `spec`'s; one with another repository's or MathTrail's suffix is not checked, and one in inline code is an example. Strings, literals of regular expressions and the bodies of heredocs are not comments, and code a generator wrote — a line of its own in its first lines in Go's form, `// Code generated … DO NOT EDIT.`, or `// @generated` — is not read: its comments come from the `.proto` files and schemas. `tools/docs-check/comments.mjs` reads the comments by a scanner of its own. In `spec` the switch `"comments": true` of the block `spec` of `tools/docs-check/budgets.json` turns it on; in another repository, the same key of its `docs-budgets.json`, which its task of epic E16 writes with `entry` 12 (R145), and the template carries from the start.
- **Citations** (R171). With the key `"citations": true` — in `spec`, of the block `spec` of `tools/docs-check/budgets.json`; in another repository, of its `docs-budgets.json`, which its own task of epic E22 sets and the template carries from the start — the check finds what R171 forbids mechanically: a task's number in a document outside RUN.md, `run/` and `docs/plan/` or in a comment of code, an amendment — dated, or to a decision — in a document outside the plan, and more than two citations in one parenthesis. A key of each repository, as `comments`, so that a move to the tag does not turn red before that task; the block `repository` holds none.
  - The plan is RUN.md and `run/`, in `spec` also COORDINATION.md and the template's RUN.md and `run/`. What R171 puts outside the rule — the archives `docs/plan/`, `spec`'s normative texts for authors, `.proto` files — is not read, and a number in inline code is an example.
  - A task's number is `T` and digits, MathTrail's with its subtask, `T105.10`, a heading's too. A dated amendment is the word «amendment» or «поправка» beside a date, before or after it, in any document outside the plan: in the log it is folded into its entry, elsewhere the entry is cited.
  - The citations of a parenthesis are the numbers of the registers and of the tables «В» and «Д», sections and tasks, a range one, counted in the parenthesis that holds them directly; the plan is held to it too. `tools/docs-check/citation-rule.mjs` holds the checks.
- **An example of a citation** — `R03`, `R19` — is written in inline code, in a document and in a comment alike: `docs-check` reads no number in code (RULES.md, Citations).
- **`just new-repo-check`** runs the same mode on a copy; links to `spec` are checked by its submodule, and for a draft by `spec`'s working tree.

— *Why:*
- The documents of the other repositories were checked by hand, and the one-off script of T05–T14 was lost with its session's folder; the check from the submodule needs nothing of the repository but `docs-budgets.json`.
- Reading the files git lists sees exactly the repository's documents, in any repository, the uncommitted ones too, and needs nothing on its side (`tutor` В29).
- The name as a suffix wherever a word boundary follows it: the trial of 2026-11-08 on `spec` and eleven repositories found 113 places where a citation of another log was checked against the own one because such a number existed at home too, and this reading changes none of their sentences (`sim` В5). Names of prose only at the end of a sentence caught natural sentences in every repository (`.github` В22).
- An anchor `(R25)` is the cheapest way from a line of code to its reason, and 2 of 8 numbers of decisions sampled in comments were wrong, which no check saw (measurements 1.14). The switch is a repository's own so that its move to the tag does not turn red before the task that fixes its comments.

— *Rejected:*
- a justfile of its own in the template — before code, against repositories 1;
- not checking the numbers in guillemets — the check would be blind to real citations in quotes;
- the tables «В» and «Д» checked only in the other repositories — one tool would hold two rules for identical tables;
- the path to the repository from the command line;
- `--exclude-standard` — the list would depend on the machine and the clone; parsing the repository's `.gitignore` by a rule of our own — a second rule beside git's; refusing a root without `.git` — `just new-repo-check` checks a draft, which has none;
- a sign after a repository's name to mark it a suffix — every author would have to remember it; a list of exceptions in `config.mjs` — a second rule beside the first; an error with a hint at each ambiguous place — 113 places, entries of logs and archives among them;
- a register of its own for the numbers of records of `docs/sources.md` — the check of sections already does it;
- a parser of each language for the comments — a dependency for each, where a scanner of comments and strings is enough; the comments checked in every repository from the tag on — red before its task.

— *Consequence:* `tools/docs-check/` — `main.mjs`, `config.mjs`, `citations.mjs`, `registers.mjs`, `budgets.mjs`, `comments.mjs`, `citation-rule.mjs` and their tests; `repo-template/files/docs-budgets.json`; repositories 2.2, 5; RULES.md, Citations.

## Analyzer findings

**R33. An analyzer's finding that a change cannot close stays open, and its reason is recorded here.** As R51 canvas-api. The findings of CodeQL and Scorecard come to the Security tab, those of SonarCloud to its project, and rule 12 of RUN.md closes them before a new task. The answer is given once, not on each scan, and the next reader tells an answered finding from a new one. The list was compared with the first runs of CodeQL and Scorecard on `main` on 2026-10-20: `spec` — commit f2769e1, Scorecard score 6.6; `module-kit` — 254452e, 6.3 (RUN.md, T17). It is shared by all repositories with the shared checks (R30): their template, devcontainer and author are the same.
- **Scorecard `Code-Review` and `Branch-Protection`** want approvals by a second person. The project has one author, and the ruleset of `main` does without approvals on purpose (R30). Setting up a second account for the sake of the score is worse than the score itself (R51 canvas-api).
- **Scorecard `Pinned-Dependencies`** is about the `npm install -g` of Claude Code in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`. The installation goes by exact version, and npm checks the archive against the hash that the registry publishes: that is the check available to a global installation (R51 canvas-api).
- **CodeQL in `draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`** — `js/xss-through-dom` (high) and four `js/cross-window-information-leak` (medium). This is the loader of a single-file prototype that a design tool built, not the platform's code. The prototype does not ship, and the documents override it ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)); SonarCloud no longer reads it. CodeQL will stop reading it when the shared `codeql.yml` gets an input for exclusions (Д8).
- **Pass with time or with tasks:**
  - `Maintained` — the repositories are younger than 90 days;
  - `SAST` — in `spec`, some of the commits were made before CodeQL;
  - `CI-Tests` — some pull requests were merged before CI: in `spec`, CI checked 11 of 13;
  - `CII-Best-Practices` — there is no OpenSSF Best Practices badge. The author gets it on bestpractices.dev, as canvas-api got it (R51 canvas-api), if the author finds it needed;
  - `Fuzzing` — there is no code yet that parses outside input: `docs-check` reads the documents of the repository itself. Fuzz tests come with such code.

`Signed-Releases` and `Packaging` (−1) and `Contributors` (3 — one organization) give no alerts.

— *Why:* rule 12 of RUN.md and the author's decision of 2026-10-20 to exclude `draft/` from CodeQL, as it is already excluded from SonarCloud. A check that will be red for the whole life of a one-person project is not a defect (R51 canvas-api).

— *Rejected:* closing such findings with the mark "false positive" or "won't fix" — then a new finding of the same rule would disappear silently; leaving the prototype's findings forever, or fixing the generated code — a new prototype would bring them again.

— *Consequence:* a finding not on this list is new, and it is closed by a change (rule 12 of RUN.md). Excluding `draft/` from CodeQL is Д8. — RUN.md, T17; R30.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* CodeQL no longer reads `draft/`, and Д8 is closed. The shared `codeql.yml` of `.github` got the input `paths-ignore` as early as v0.1.1 ("Paths CodeQL leaves out of the analysis of javascript-typescript — draft/**, say", the input's description at v0.1.10, read 2026-10-22), and the `codeql.yml` of `spec` is on v0.1.10 from this day and passes `draft/**`. The analysis of `actions` still reads all workflows. The item about the findings of CodeQL in `draft/NovaTrail Widget.html` above is now about the past: the five alerts are closed by the first analysis of `main` without `draft/`, and a new prototype will not bring them. The references to `.github` in the other shared checks — secrets, DCO and Scorecard — will be raised by Dependabot (RUN.md, Д10).

— *Amendment 2026-10-23:* the OpenSSF Best Practices badge is decided — R48. First `spec` gets it (RUN.md, T41), then each repository with code and automated tests. The item `CII-Best-Practices` above waits for this, not for the author's decision.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* `spec` has the OpenSSF Best Practices badge — project [15977](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15977) on bestpractices.dev, level passing since 2026-10-27 (`badge_level` and `achieved_passing_at` in `https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/15977.json`; RUN.md, T41). For `spec`, the item `CII-Best-Practices` leaves those that pass with time.
- Scorecard gives 5 of 10 for passing: "passing badge: 5" (ossf/scorecard, `docs/checks.md`, `main` 1e241c4). The alert threshold in the policy of scorecard-action is 5 too: `CII-Best-Practices: # passing score / score: 5` (ossf/scorecard-action, `policies/template.yml`, `main` 365df9f). Both read 2026-10-26.
- Scorecard looks up the project by the repository's address: `url := fmt.Sprintf("%s/projects.json?url=%s", client.baseURL, repoURI)`, where `repoURI` is `https://` and the address (ossf/scorecard, `clients/cii_http_client.go`, `main` 1e241c4, read 2026-10-27). `https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects.json?url=https://github.com/altnovatrail/spec` returns project 15977 (checked 2026-10-27).
- So alert #7 of `spec` will be closed by the next run of Scorecard on `main`, as in canvas-api and standalone. If it is not closed, the finding is new (rule 12 of RUN.md).

For the other repositories, the item waits for their badge (RUN.md, Д34). T41 does not take silver and gold: for them Scorecard gives "silver badge: 7" and "gold badge: 10" (`docs/checks.md`, the same place, read 2026-10-27), but passing closes the alert too, and silver also requires the criterion `access_continuity` (RUN.md, T41).

## The development environment

**R34. An archive that `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` downloads is checked against the sha256 checksum written beside its version.** The checksum is an `ARG` for each architecture, `amd64` and `arm64`, from the publisher's own list of checksums: `SHASUMS256.txt` of the Node release, `SHA256SUMS` of the releases of just and just-lsp, `gh_<version>_checksums.txt` of the gh release. The check runs before unpacking, and a wrong checksum stops the build. The checksum changes in the same change as the version: Dependabot does not see these versions, and they are raised by hand (R30; `.github/dependabot.yml`). — *Why:* the author's answer to В12 of `.github` — 2026-10-20, narrowed in planning epic E3 of `.github`. An exact version does not prevent substituting the archive at the same address, while a checksum in the file itself lets in no other archive once this one has been read; this is how `.github` already checks the CI tools (R08 .github). The stage `toolchain`, in which the CI checks of each repository run, needs it no less. The checksums were checked on 2026-10-20 against the publisher's list, for the releases on GitHub also against the field `digest` of their API, and against the downloaded archives themselves. — *Rejected:* `npm ci` for Claude Code — the answer to В12 dropped this part, and the Scorecard finding about `npm install -g` stays open with its reason (R33); an exact version without a checksum. — *Consequence:* the rule of exact versions in RULES.md names the checksum too; the repositories get the Dockerfile with checksums with their move to a tag of `spec`. — `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`; RULES.md, Hard rules.

— *Amendment 2026-11-08:* **a CI tool that a GitHub action or the runner image puts on the runner, and that there is nothing to pin with, is pinned as narrowly as its installer allows, and the run writes the exact version into its artifact or log.** The rule of exact versions (RULES.md, Hard rules) and the checksums of this decision are about what `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` and `devcontainer.json` install; the runner is outside them:
- the runner image is set by a label — so the jobs of `spec` run too, `runs-on: ubuntu-24.04` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `release.yml`);
- the Android system image in the workflow `emulators.yml` of `canvas` is installed by `sdkmanager`: the action `reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner` is pinned by SHA, the emulator build by number, the image by API level, target and architecture, `system-images;android-36;google_apis;x86_64`, and the run writes the revision into an artifact, `sdk-installed.txt` (R54 canvas). `sdkmanager` does not let one pin the revision: in the list of Google's repository this path has one entry — revision 7, the archive `x86_64-36_r07.zip` —, and its checksum is only SHA-1, `<checksum type="sha1">` ([sys-img2-4.xml](https://dl.google.com/android/repository/sys-img/google_apis/sys-img2-4.xml), read 2026-11-08). A new revision comes into CI by itself when Google releases it, and is visible in the run's artifact;
- the rule reads the same way for what comes with the macOS runner image — Xcode, which the job chooses by version, and the iOS simulator runtimes (T80 canvas).

The boundary is R12: such a tool only checks the platform, puts nothing of its own into a release file or an image, and NovaTrail does not distribute it. What goes into what ships is still pinned by exact version and checksum. *Why:* the author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В63 (RUN.md of `canvas`, `main` 316349d), by its recommendation — option (a) —, with the triage's refinement: the rule is general, not only about Android. The image changes only when Google releases a revision, and the run reads it every time. *Rejected:*
- the image archive by the address and checksum from `sys-img2-4.xml`, bypassing `sdkmanager`: the checksum there is SHA-1, weaker than this decision's sha256, and instead of the action, an installation step of our own. The archives of past revisions are still served at their addresses — r05 and r06 answered 200 on 2026-11-08 —, but Google has no list that names them, and the sha256 checksum would have to be computed by us, not taken from the publisher;
- our own cache of the image, raised by hand, like the snapshot of the Ubuntu archive (R40): the snapshots are a service of Ubuntu itself, while here NovaTrail would keep a copy of someone else's image itself, under terms about keeping a copy that nobody has read;
- an exception in the Hard rules of RULES.md: the rule there names where versions stand — an `ARG` of the Dockerfile and a literal of `devcontainer.json` —, and does not concern the runner, while each repository would take the exception with a new tag; R40 likewise rejected an exception for the packages of `apt`.

*Revisit* if a new revision brings down a run that passed on the previous one: then install the archive by a step of our own at the previous revision, with a sha256 checksum read once and checked against the SHA-1 of the list. — R11, R12, R40; R54 canvas; RUN.md, Д122.

— *Amendment 2026-11-15 (T168):* **where the publisher lists no checksums beside an archive, its `ARG` holds the sha256 of the archive as it was downloaded over HTTPS from the publisher's own address, for each architecture, with the date it was taken in the comment beside it; a raise of the version takes the new sums the same way, and the record in `docs/sources.md` that names the archive says the publisher has no list.** The first such archive is Docker's static archive of the stage `orchestrator`, `docker-<version>.tgz` of `download.docker.com/linux/static/stable/`, whose folders hold no file of checksums (sources 9.2). The sum still lets in no other archive once this one has been read, which is what this decision is for; it cannot say that the archive read was the one Docker built. *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-11-15 in T168, by the recommendation; R12 names the static archive, of which the stage takes the client alone. *Rejected:* the package `docker-ce-cli` of Docker's apt repository, whose sha256 its index `Packages` lists under the signed `InRelease` — an amendment to R12 for another source, for a list that the build would not check against its signature either. — R12, R156; RUN.md, T168.

## The task's review

**R35. A task's review is one round of `/code-review high`, and the executor may hand in a small change without a review.**
- Having fixed the round's findings, the executor does not repeat the review.
- Whether a change is small, the executor decides. The report says whether there was a review, and if not, why.
- The rule is written in rules 6 and 8 of the RUN.md of `spec`, of the template and of each repository, and for Codex in AGENTS.md.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-21: «теперь всегда только 1 код ревью. Если изменения небольшие то код ревью в этом случае не проводится - это решает сам агент». — *Rejected:* the former rule 6, «не больше двух кругов», where the second round ran if the first found something. — *Consequence:* the change in RUN.md and AGENTS.md of twelve repositories was made by the session of `.github` on the author's direct instruction, the same day. This is a one-off departure from R21, not an amendment to it. — RUN.md; `repo-template/`; AGENTS.md.

## UI packages and samples

**R36. UI packages enter their consumer as web components, and the data types that the repositories share are taken from the releases of `spec`. Each package names its own elements; `canvas` has one element, `<novatrail-canvas>`, for every canvas kind, and the members below are the agreement of `canvas` and `app`, whose types are `CanvasElement` of `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` (R74).**
- **The element** takes data by properties, gives the work by methods, and tells what the learner did by events: a `CustomEvent` from the host, `bubbles` and `composed`, with a frozen `detail`, sent on the learner's own action alone, never on the consumer's assignment. It needs no framework, and each consumer chooses its own. Its Shadow DOM is open.
- **What it shows** — one at a time, another given while it shows one a `TypeError`, and `app` gives each segment of a lesson a new element:
  - `task`, the open view of a task, given before `history` and `marks`; a slot bound `zone` is a `TypeError`;
  - `paper`, a task from the learner's paper: its crop, which the element lays over a sheet as tracing paper (R162);
  - `workedExample`, the open view of a lesson's segment `worked_example` (R58), on a sheet the learner does not write on: `history` only empty, `marks` a `TypeError`, `exportWork()` and `filled` `null`, the pen alone.
- **`manifest`**, the open view of the module manifest (R62): the element reads `module_format_version` — another version is a `TypeError` while the format is v0 (R44) —, `canvas.digit_height`, 32 without a manifest (R51), and `languages.explanation`, the language of the statement and of a workbook's lines; a canvas setting it does not know is a `TypeError`. **`media`**, a function that gives a promise of a `Blob` for a picture's reference, its path from `media/`, asked once: the canvas goes to no network, and `app` gives the files of the device part that `api` serves (repositories 2.1). Until a file comes, its frame shows its `alt`.
- **The writing history:** the property `history`, a frozen array of history events, which the consumer gives back to open the sheet as it was — one the sheet could not have written is a `TypeError`, and the sheet stays —; and the event `historychange`, synchronous after each stroke, erasure, clearing and undo, `detail` `{ events, from }`: a store whose length is not `from` has missed events and rereads `history`. `app` keeps the history and the submission context as they are, through JSON: rounded numbers break the digest and the crop's integers, and the element does not take the context back (R26, R27 canvas).
- **The work for checking**, `exportWork()`, a promise: on a sheet `{ png, submission }`, the crop and its context; on a workbook `{ cells, submission }`, `{ item, slot, png }` of each filled box in the task's order, each a crop by R25 canvas at the manifest's digit height; on a task from paper `{ statement, png, submission }`; and `null` where nothing is to check — no stroke, no box filled, a worked example. The submission context — where the crop lies on the sheet, the stroke groups and the table "group label → stroke IDs", the crop's integers and the submission digest; on a workbook the table "box → stroke IDs" and the digest of every box of the page; on a task from paper the tracing paper's state too — is `app`'s: it stays on the device, and only the crops with their places leave it (privacy 4; R53).
- **`filled`**, read-only: per item and slot, in the task's order, whether a slot holds a stroke `exportWork()` would take — a workbook's boxes, a sheet's one slot bound `anywhere` or `sheet`, a task from paper's one slot —, and `null` on a sheet of `choice` slots, with no task and for an example. An action changes it before its `historychange`, and a task or a history given changes it with no event. It is the exit condition `answer_slots_filled` (R57).
- **`marks`**, the tutor's marks of one submission with its context, given after `task` and `history`: a mark names a slot by its place `{ item, slot }`, from 1, and its kind and place are held to `Mark` of `novatrail.api.v1` (R74, R97).
- **The tools:** `tool`, `"pen" | "eraser" | "hand"` — the hand the element's own on every sheet the learner writes on, no tool of the format (R88 canvas) —, and `toolchange`, `{ tool }`. `undo()` and `clear()` are called by the element's own buttons, outside the agreement.
- **A task from paper's state:** `tracing`, `{ at, hidden }`, with `tracingchange`, and `grid`, `"dots" | "lines" | "blank" | "squares"`, dots as a task from paper comes, with `gridchange`, `{ grid }` (R88 canvas). `app` keeps both and gives them back, which tells nothing; how long it keeps the grid is R162.
- **A worked example's demo:** `demoState`, `{ opened, hidden }`, `{ opened: 0, hidden: false }` as an example starts, and `demochange` on the learner's press of the element's "Next" or "Demo". `app` keeps the state and gives it back after the example; one the example cannot have is a `TypeError`.
- **The picture of a work**, `exportPicture()`, a promise of a PNG `Blob` with no condition, which `app` puts as `StoredWork.picture` by `PutWork` ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15): the strokes the surface shows, black on white — the page, a sheet's or a workbook's with its draft, and the ink past it, right and down, the tracing paper where it lies counted whole —, a pixel a unit while it holds no more bytes than the page's 1000 × 1400, scaled down past that, its size in its PNG's header, within the limit of a stored work. A worked example's is its white page. Its size and colours are `canvas`'s (R83 canvas).
- **The language** of the element's labels is its own attribute `lang`, not an ancestor's (R91).
- **What `app` sets:** the style properties `--novatrail-canvas-accent`, the accent of the tool in use and of the focus ring; `--novatrail-canvas-glass`, the fill of the bar's glass; `--novatrail-canvas-top`, the offset, from the top of what scrolls the element, of the band in whose middle the bar stands; `--novatrail-canvas-pad-top` and `--novatrail-canvas-pad-bottom`, how far `app`'s own bars float over the element's top and bottom — the statement starts below the first, the sheet scrolls up past the second, and the bar's band ends above it (R73 canvas) —, each with the mockup's default (R148); the boolean attribute `tools-hidden`, which takes the bar, and an example's row, out of sight and out of the accessibility tree, on a phone while the tutor's sheet is open; `statement-hidden` (R161); and on a worked example its "Continue", a child `<button slot="actions">` in the named slot `actions`, after the element's "Next" and "Demo" in the element's row (R84 canvas): "Continue" and what it does stay `app`'s (R78; R06 app).
- **The consumer's CSP:** the element sets the styles of its Shadow DOM by `adoptedStyleSheets`, a `CSSStyleSheet` with `replaceSync()`, with no `<style>` element or `style` attribute, and needs of the consumer's CSP only `img-src blob:`.
- **The types** are in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas`, written by hand (R74); the package `canvas` registers the element in `HTMLElementTagNameMap` and its events in `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`.
- Later, with the text canvas, "Listen" on it is voiced by `app` on an event `speak`, by one speech synthesis for the whole app (Т-13). In the first slice there is no text canvas (R41).

— *Why:* the answer of `canvas` to Т-21, which the author took on 2026-10-21, and the author's answers since to the rows «в реестр spec» that brought each member (`canvas`: В37, В38, В40, В42, В46, В52–В54, В58, В82, В83, В85; `app`: В28, В66, В69), the hand, the grid and the padding by T251 (R88 canvas).
- The packages have several consumers — `app`, the samples page, the site, the card of the MCP channel —, each with the framework its repository chooses. React 19 and Preact take the element by themselves: «React 19 adds full support for custom elements and passes all tests on Custom Elements Everywhere» ([React 19](https://react.dev/blog/2024/12/05/react-19#support-for-custom-elements)), «Preact fully supports Web Components» ([Preact, Web Components](https://preactjs.com/guide/v10/web-components/)); both read 2026-10-21. A new canvas kind is the platform's code (R02): with one element for every kind, a new version of `canvas` brings it with no change to `app`.
- The Shadow DOM is open for the sake of styles: it isolates the styles and the DOM tree, not the code (R16; architecture 8); third-party code still runs only in a sandboxed iframe.
- Each member is named here because it is a contract: without it in `spec`, `app` would learn it only from the package, and the types could not hold it on both sides (R74). The events carry what is new, not the whole history; filling is a property, not a second event for one action (R27 canvas).
- The canvas has no data of its own (architecture 3.2): the submission context, derived from the learner's work, is `app`'s and stays on the device (privacy 4). The crop's integers make snapping exact (R26 canvas); the digest catches an accidental divergence, not a forgery.
- The labels are the package's own table, so that no consumer, the samples page among them, translates them.
- The CSP: `app` has `style-src 'self'` (R09 app), and a `<style>` in the Shadow DOM is connected to the document — «A node is connected if its shadow-including root is a document» ([DOM](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/), Last Updated 19 October 2026) — and blocked: «If the Should element's inline behavior be blocked by Content Security Policy? algorithm returns "Blocked" … then return» ([HTML](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/semantics.html), update a style block, Last Updated 30 October 2026); `replaceSync()` has no CSP step, «Let rules be the result of running parse a stylesheet's contents from text» (CSSOM, Editor's Draft 13 October 2026), held by a test of `canvas` under `default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; img-src blob:`. `ShadowRoot.adoptedStyleSheets` is in Chrome since 73, Firefox since 101, Safari since 16.4 (`mdn/browser-compat-data`, `api/ShadowRoot.json`, commit a8813fc). All read 2026-11-02.

— *Rejected:*
- components of `app`'s framework — they would decide for `app` and carry the framework into the samples page; a mount function — each consumer would write the mounting and cleanup, and each framework a wrapper;
- the canvas voicing by itself — the rules for voices would live in two packages;
- the submission context in the canvas's memory — the canvas would get data of its own;
- R36 naming only the gist, the names and the composition left to `canvas` — the contract would have no record in `spec`;
- the labels given by `app` — each consumer would translate them;
- the whole history in `historychange`; filling in its `detail` or as an event of its own;
- the module's settings in each task's open view (R51); `{ png, submission }` on a workbook, the boxes glued together (R53); `png: null` for an empty box;
- `filled` by slot with `null` for `choice`; an example through `task`, or an element of its own; a demo led by `app` alone or by the element alone (В52–В54 canvas);
- `undo()`, `clear()` and `media` all in the agreement, or none of them;
- a `sha256` of the canvas's styles in `app`'s `style-src`, which each change of them would change; `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`;
- the bar as `::part(tools)` for `app` to hide by its own CSS — `app` could break the bar's accessibility; `app`'s "Continue" in a row of its own, or "Next" and "Demo" drawn by `app`;
- `exportPicture()` the package's own, as `undo()` — `app` would take its type from `canvas` unchecked.

— Т-21; architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 6; repositories 8; privacy 4; R07, R26, R27, R28, R73, R83, R84 and R88 canvas; R06, R09 and R17 app; R44, R51, R53, R57, R58, R62, R74, R78, R90, R91, R97, R148, R161, R162; `types/canvas/index.d.ts`.

**R37. UI packages are published to npm, in the scope of the organization `@altnovatrail`; for `canvas`, `@altnovatrail/canvas`. The same file that is signed in the GitHub release goes to npm, by a step of the shared `release.yml` of `.github` — through trusted publishing, with no long-lived token.**
- The package is installed by an exact version and with no token, including by the authors of widgets from stage 4. Widget bundles are still pinned by hash in the module package (R16).
- The version in npm is tied to the signed release by a sum: the sha256 of its archive is in the signed `SHA256SUMS` of the GitHub release (R08 canvas). What checks the signature is Т-27.
- The publishing step is in the shared release of `.github`, not a job of its own in each repository with a package. How it is built is decided by `.github` with an amendment to its R18 .github: the shared workflows are its own (R30). What `canvas` asks of the step (В18 of `canvas`):
  - it runs on the runner, not in the `toolchain` stage of the caller: tokens do not go there (R18 .github);
  - Node and npm by an exact version and sum in the file itself, like cosign (R08 .github), no lower than npm 11.5.1 and Node 22.14.0;
  - it runs only if the caller named the package file: the author publishes the first version by hand, since a trusted publisher is configured for a package that is already in the registry;
  - `--access public` explicitly; with `publish: false` it publishes nothing;
  - on a rerun it takes the file from the release and checks the signature, does not publish a published version again but checks it by `integrity`; a version lower than the newest in npm it does not put under `latest`; on a refusal that `release-refusal` lets through, it publishes nothing.

  Whether the registry accepts provenance from a reusable workflow of another repository, the npm documentation does not say: the first publishing of `canvas` with this step will check it (T24 canvas).
- The types of `spec` are in `spec`'s own release (R31), and where their package is published is decided by RUN.md, T35. The recommendation of `canvas` is the same npm (В16 of `canvas`).

— *Why:* the answer of `canvas` to Т-26, В17 of `canvas`; Т-26 was closed by it, by the author's decision of 2026-10-21. The step of the shared release is the recommendation of В18 of `canvas`. The criterion of Т-26 — install by an exact version and with no token — is met only by npm. All read 2026-10-21:
- in npm anyone installs a public package in a scope: «Scoped public packages can be downloaded and installed by anyone», and a version does not change: «Registry data is immutable, meaning once published, a package cannot change» ([npm/documentation](https://github.com/npm/documentation/tree/4e8e03b978033529bf8f50d74305b29939eb022c), commit 4e8e03b, `downloading-and-installing-packages-locally.mdx` and `policies/unpublish.mdx`). An organization for public packages is free — «the "Unlimited public packages" free plan» (ibid., `creating-an-organization.mdx`). The author created the organization `altnovatrail` in npm on 2026-10-21 (architecture 4 canvas);
- from a reusable workflow npm checks the caller: «validation checks the calling workflow's name instead of the workflow that actually contains the publish command», and «The `id-token: write` permission must also be given to both parent and child workflows»; «Trusted publishing requires npm CLI version 11.5.1 or later and Node version 22.14.0 or higher» (ibid., `trusted-publishers.mdx`). OIDC needs no secret, so the step does not break the rule "shared workflows take no secrets" (the 2026-10-20 amendment to R24);
- the publishing code is one for all the repositories with packages on the shared release, and the provenance certificate, by the Fulcio rule, names the shared `release.yml` in its SAN, like the cosign signatures (Т-27).

— *Rejected:*
- GitHub Packages — a token is needed even to install a public package: «You need an access token to publish, install, and delete private, internal, and public packages» ([github/docs](https://github.com/github/docs/blob/cca0c9d7299f760587d6601bd96acfd2f5cb8929/data/reusables/package_registry/authenticate-packages.md), commit cca0c9d, read 2026-10-21);
- only GitHub releases — npm 12 closes installing by a link by default: «As of npm 12 the default is `none`» for `allow-remote` ([npm/cli](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/ae98c62586b6fea44114f72e249e246a2981de70/workspaces/config/lib/definitions/definitions.js), v12.2.1, commit ae98c62, read 2026-10-21), and each project would need `allow-remote=root`;
- a publishing job of its own in the `release.yml` of each repository — a copy for each repository with a package, and it needs a change to `.github` too: the shared `release.yml` has no outputs — neither the version nor a sign that the release came out;
- staged publishing — the author with 2FA approves each version, and the release again waits for a person, while it must come out by itself (R31; R18 .github);
- publishing each version by hand; a long-lived npm token in the secrets — a shared workflow takes no secrets (R05 .github).

— *Consequence:* Т-26 is closed. `.github` writes the amendment to R18 .github and the step, and T24 canvas waits for it. — architecture 3.2, 3.3, 3.11, 3.12, 6; repositories 8; R08 canvas.

— *Amendment 2026-10-29:* the package of `spec`, `@altnovatrail/spec`, is not published by a step of the shared `release.yml` of `.github`: that one cannot call `spec` (architecture 3.11). Its file is carried by `spec`'s own release, from line 0.4 (R73), the author publishes the first version in npm by hand, and the publishing step through trusted publishing is its own, in the `release.yml` of `spec`, by the steps of the shared `release.yml` of `.github` v0.1.10 — RUN.md, T51. Staged publishing is still rejected, and direct publishing for a trusted publisher is now turned on explicitly: «Configurations created after Sep 03, 2026 are automatically set to allow `npm stage publish`, and you can choose whether to also permit direct publishing with `npm publish`» ([npm Docs, Trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers), page updated 2026-10-06, read 2026-10-29). This is the flag `--allow-publish` of `npm trust` — RUN.md, T51. — R73; RUN.md, T49, T51.

— *Second amendment 2026-10-29:* `@altnovatrail/spec` is published by the `release.yml` of `spec`. The npm steps of the shared `release.yml` of `.github` v0.1.10 are carried into it word for word, except where `spec` is built otherwise, and one check beyond them (RUN.md, T51):
- the package name is a literal, not an input, and there is no step `npm-name`: the name of the package file is given by the output `npm` of the step "Build the files", and it also decides whether the npm steps run;
- cosign is a step before the signing: the rerun needs it too;
- Node is 24.22.1 with its npm 11.19.1, by the version and sum of the `.tar.xz` in the file itself, as in `.github`. This is not the Node of the `toolchain` stage, 24.21.0: that one came out before the security release 24.22.1 of 2026-10-20 ([nodejs.org/dist/index.json](https://nodejs.org/dist/index.json), read 2026-10-29). npm runs on the runner through the wrapper `npm-isolated` — without the user's and the project's settings and without scripts — and the OIDC token does not get into the container;
- the package check is before the signing and before the release: a bad package leaves no immutable release. The archive and its `package.json` are checked, then the package document from the registry by `?write=true`, then `npm publish --dry-run`. If the package is not in the registry, the run fails;
- publishing is after "Verify the release" and before the check of the Go module: `npm publish --access public` through trusted publishing. The outcome is decided by the registry, not by npm's exit code: npm may end successfully when the version is only prepared for publishing (staged), or fail on a version that came out ([npm/cli#9889](https://github.com/npm/cli/issues/9889), open as of 2026-10-29). So the step waits for the version in the registry and checks its `integrity` and the archive byte for byte against the release file;
- a version that is already in npm with the same `integrity` is skipped. With another one, the run fails. Beyond `.github`, the run fails the same way on a number that npm already gave out and that was unpublished — the `time` of the package document remembers it: «Once `package@version` has been used, you can never use it again» ([npm/documentation](https://github.com/npm/documentation/blob/514e6c9e84ef5b29dd8e11b7e743ab573ba10a0b/content/policies/unpublish.mdx), commit 514e6c9, read 2026-10-29). If the release has already come out, the package is published by the next release, with a new number, and the message says so. If not yet, all the releases of the line stop, since each would take the same number, until `RELEASE_LINE` is raised, and the message names this. A number in npm without a release of `spec` can come only from someone else's publishing;
- a version lower than the newest goes under the tag `previous`: without a tag npm 11 does not publish it — «Cannot implicitly apply the "latest" tag because previously published version … is higher than the new version» ([npm/cli v11.19.1](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.1/lib/commands/publish.js), `lib/commands/publish.js`, read 2026-10-29). The step counts the newest as npm does there: among the versions without a pre-release and without `deprecated`. So the placeholder `0.0.0-stage` that the registry set up with the package (RUN.md, В26) does not count;
- a refusal of the Releases API that `release-refusal` lets through publishes nothing in npm: there is no release, and the release of the tip covers it;
- a rerun of an already released commit publishes the file from the release, not one built anew. It is checked by `gh release verify-asset` — the attestation ties the file to the release and its commit — and by `cosign verify-blob`: the signature of the `release.yml` of `spec` on `main`, in this repository. `verify-blob` does not check the commit of the signing run: it is the tip of `main` at the start of that run, and a new run of the same commit — for example, CI run on it again — goes from a later tip;
- a commit that is no longer the tip of `main` goes to npm too. npm's provenance names as its commit `GITHUB_SHA` — `gitCommit: env.GITHUB_SHA` ([npm/cli v11.19.1](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/v11.19.1/workspaces/libnpmpublish/lib/provenance.js), read 2026-10-29) — that is, the tip, like the cosign certificate of its files, and its own commit is named by the release's attestation.

The package's trusted publisher is the repository `altnovatrail/spec`, the file `release.yml`, without an environment, with direct publishing: `npm trust github @altnovatrail/spec --file release.yml --repository altnovatrail/spec --allow-publish`. 0.4.0 has no provenance: the author published this version by hand.

*Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-29 in the planning of T51 — three, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T51, «Решено автором»):
- Node as in `.github`: the step stays a copy of the model, and the version is raised together with it;
- a version that is already in npm, and a refusal, as in `.github` and as `canvas` asked (В18 of `canvas`, above);
- a commit that is not the tip goes to npm: each version of line 0.4 is in npm, and the packages install the same version as the tag of the submodule `spec/` (R73).

*Rejected:*
- the Node of the `toolchain` stage — it came out before the security release;
- 24.22.1 in the Dockerfile as well — a change to all the checks for the sake of a release step;
- a warning instead of a failure when the `integrity` differs — the version in npm would silently diverge from the release file;
- only the release of the tip goes to npm: an earlier commit would have a tag, and its version would not be in npm.

— architecture 3.11, 3.12; repositories 5; RUN.md, T51.

The sum in `SHA256SUMS` is not needed for this, but stays a release file of `canvas` (R08 canvas). "What checks the signature is Т-27" above reads: R77. — R77; RUN.md, T37.

## The license check in other repositories

**R39. The other repositories take the list of licenses and the check of an npm lock file by recipes of `spec`: `licenses-allowed` and `licenses-check-repo`. The check rejects a lock file without `packages`.**
- **The list.** `just -f spec/justfile licenses-allowed` prints the list of category A from `tools/licenses/config.mjs` (R12), one SPDX identifier per line. This is an interface, like the release recipes (the 2026-10-20 amendment to R31): the layout of `config.mjs` can be changed without breaking the caller.
- **The check of an npm lock file** is `just -f spec/justfile licenses-check-repo <lock-file> [<exceptions file>]`, from the repository's root. The paths are its own: a path that leads out of it, the check rejects.
  - Each package of the lock file is checked against the same list and the same parsing of SPDX expressions as in `licenses-check` of `spec` itself.
  - The exceptions are the repository's own. This is JSON: an object of packages, each with `license` — what the lock file says of it, or `null` — and `reason`: why it is accepted and by which decision. There are no other fields, and a file of another form stops the check.
  - The exceptions of `spec` do not pass to another lock file. An exception that has nothing to accept in the lock file is an error, as in `spec`.
- **A lock file without `packages`** — lockfileVersion 1, such as npm 5 and 6 wrote — the check rejects, and so does `licenses-check` of `spec` itself. Before, it read such a file as empty and answered "ok". «1: The lockfile version used by npm v5 and v6», and `packages` is «an object that maps package locations to an object containing the information about that package» ([npm Docs, package-lock.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json), read 2026-10-21).
- **Who calls.** The recipes run in the `toolchain` stage of the caller: Node is there. How `go.yml`, `typescript.yml` and `self-ci.yml` call them is decided by `.github`: the shared workflows are its own (R30). The recommendation of `.github` is this:
  - `self-ci.yml` checks the copy of the list in `go.yml` against the output of `licenses-allowed`, not against a parsing of `config.mjs` as text;
  - the job `licenses` of the shared `typescript.yml` takes the submodule `spec` and calls `licenses-check-repo`. This is an exception to the checkout without a submodule (R16 .github): there the ban is held by the code that takes the files of `spec` from releases (R21), and here the submodule gives the check's tool.

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-10-21 to В19 and В20 of `.github`, by their recommendations; `.github` itself recommended recording them in one task.
- `go.yml` and `typescript.yml` of `.github` carry copies of the list, `ALLOWED_LICENSES`. The job "Workflows" of `self-ci.yml` checks them against `spec/tools/licenses/config.mjs`, reading the file as text, one quoted identifier per line (RUN.md of `.github`, commit b3ee1a8). This file had no interface, as `line.mjs` had none before the 2026-10-20 amendment to R31.
- The contract of the TypeScript wrapper has `ci-licenses` check each package of the lock file against this list, with exceptions by name (R19 .github). `spec` had such a check, but only for its own `tools/package-lock.json` and with its own exceptions. Without a recipe each TypeScript repository — `canvas`, `app`, `skill-map` — would write a script of its own, like canvas-api (R48 canvas-api), and the rule would diverge across the copies.

— *Rejected:*
- the list as a separate data file that `config.mjs` reads too: the caller would again read an internal file of `spec`, only another one;
- the check as a release file of `spec` or an npm package: the release of `spec` has no files (R31), and their path is decided by RUN.md, T35;
- leave it as it is.

— *Consequence:* `.github`, with its move to a tag, checks the copies of the list against `licenses-allowed` and calls `licenses-check-repo` from `typescript.yml`. `canvas`, `app` and `skill-map` move their `ci-licenses` and exceptions to the recipe with their move (RUN.md, Д15). — repositories 5; architecture 3.11; R12.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* an exception for a license outside the list in `licenses-check-repo` is only for a development tool, as in the check of `canvas` (R12 and R14 canvas). The author's answer, by the executor's recommendation: the divergence was found when the letter to `canvas` about its T08 was being written.
- **Only `dev`.** An exception that accepts a license outside the list — an SPDX expression or a text that does not parse as one — holds only a package that the lock file marks `dev`: «If the package is strictly part of the `devDependencies` tree, then `dev` will be true». Such a package without `dev` is an error: the exception is for a tool that never ships (R12; RULES.md, Licenses). `devOptional` is not `dev`: «If it is both a `dev` dependency _and_ an `optional` dependency of a non-dev dependency, then `devOptional` will be set» ([npm Docs, package-lock.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-lock-json), read 2026-10-22), and a dependency of a package that ships may go out together with it.
- **Builds for platforms.** The same exception covers the packages that the tool itself names in `optionalDependencies` — this is how its builds for platforms come — as long as they too are `dev` and under the same license. Such a build without `dev` is an error with a reason of its own, and a package under another license is checked like any other. In `canvas`, one exception `lightningcss` covers in this way its 11 builds under MPL-2.0 (R14 canvas): on the lock file of `canvas` 88492c4 the recipe with it answers "ok — 115 packages, 1 exceptions", and without it names 12 packages.
- **An exception for `null` or for `SEE LICENSE IN <file>`** corrects what the lock file says, rather than accepting a license outside the list. This is how a lock file says that it has no license, or that the license is in the package's own file: «If you are using a license that hasn't been assigned an SPDX identifier, or if you are using a custom license, use a string value like this one» ([npm Docs, package.json](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json), read 2026-10-22). What license the package actually has, the reason says, and a person reads it, as before the amendment. Such an exception has no condition of `dev`.
- **`licenses-check` of `spec` itself** does not carry this condition: its `tools/` does not ship at all, and the packages in it are `dependencies`, and the lock file marks none of them `dev`.

*Why:* the check of `canvas` is built this way and passes its CI (R12 and R14 canvas), and Д15 expects `canvas` to move to the recipe. Without the amendment it would lose the `dev` boundary in the move, and the exception `lightningcss` would become twelve names — R14 canvas rejected this. The `dev` boundary carries the condition of R12, "never ships", from the reason that a person reads into the check itself. *Rejected:* leave R39 as it is; an open question while `canvas` keeps its own script — the rule would again live in two copies; the condition of `dev` for the exceptions with `null` and `SEE LICENSE IN` as well — then a shipped package whose license from the list lies in its file, not in the lock file, could not be taken; any text that does not parse as an SPDX expression, without the condition of `dev` — then a typo in a license would get around the boundary. — `tools/licenses/main.mjs` and its tests; RUN.md, Д15, Д16.

— *Amendment 2026-11-02:* **an exception that accepts a license not from the list holds only a package of which nothing goes into any of the repository's deliverables — neither into an npm package, nor into a build, nor into a release file. A repository whose deliverable is a bundler's build keeps everything that the bundler embeds into it in `dependencies`, and `devDependencies` is for development and CI tools. Т-36 is closed.** The author's answer to Т-36, the first option, by the recommendation; T01 `app` came to the same by itself (R03 app; architecture 3.1 app, `main` of `app` 0849269).
- **What moved.** The mark `dev` says which tree the package came from: «If the package is strictly part of the `devDependencies` tree, then `dev` will be true» (the 2026-10-22 amendment above). Whether it goes into a deliverable, it does not say: `canvas` embeds the data of the icon set at build time from a package in `devDependencies` (R78). So the condition of R12, "never ships", is held not by the mark `dev` alone, but by it and the exception's reason together: the check compares `dev`, as before, and that nothing from the package goes into a deliverable is said by the reason and held by review. The amendment does not change the check's code.
- **An app** — `app`, later `site` — keeps in `dependencies` everything that its bundler embeds, and in `devDependencies` only tools. Then `dev` in it again means "never ships", and an exception under `dev` accepts nothing embedded. T01 `app` has already decided so: in `dependencies` are `react`, `react-dom`, `@altnovatrail/canvas`, later `skill-map`, and the package of the icon set, and its `ci-vuln` — `npm audit --omit=dev` — depends on the same boundary.
- **An npm package** — `canvas`, `skill-map` — keeps in `dependencies` what its consumer needs, and a package whose data it embeds at build time — the icon set — in `devDependencies`: the consumer does not need it. Such a package has no exception (R78). Where a package stands that only the repository's second build embeds — the samples page of `canvas` (R25) — is decided by `canvas` together with its build, by the same rule of exceptions.

*Why:* the author's answer of 2026-11-02 to Т-36, by the recommendation. The rule is for everyone, not only for `app`: for `site` and for the second build of a package (architecture 6) the deliverable is a build too. *Rejected:* close Т-36 with a rule of `app` alone, without a rule in `spec` — `site` and the samples page would decide anew; a check of the exceptions against the bundler's manifest in `licenses-check-repo` as well — new code in `tools/licenses`, and each bundler has an input of its own; `app` has no exceptions for licenses not from the list — it would lose `lightningcss`, a tool that R12 allows (R03 app). — repositories 8, Т-36; architecture 3.1 and 6; R78; RUN.md, Д61.

— *Amendment 2026-11-15:* **"the release of `spec` has no files (R31), and their path is decided by RUN.md, T35" in "Rejected" is no longer so: by R64 a release of `spec` carries files — each normative part with a version of its own as `<part>-<version>.tar.gz`, the Go module and the npm packages —, and the list of licenses and the check of the lock file stay recipes that the other repositories call from the submodule, since they are tools, not code.** The rejection holds. — R64; R143; RUN.md, T164.

## System packages in the devcontainer

**R40. A system package that `apt` installs in `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` is taken from the Ubuntu archive as of a date — by a snapshot. The snapshot ID is an `ARG` beside the list of packages, and it is raised by hand, like a version.**
- In one `RUN`: `apt-get update --snapshot "$UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT"`, then `apt-get install --snapshot "$UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT"` with the list of packages. Each package is then an exact version, the one that was in the archive at that moment, and the rule of exact versions (RULES.md, Hard rules) is met without a version for each package.
- `apt` checks the archive's signature itself, as on any update.
- The snapshot is raised by hand, like a version that Dependabot does not see (R30): when the list of packages changes and when the build fails after a new digest of the base image (R13 canvas).
- The rule is about the packages of the Ubuntu archive. A package from another `apt` archive, which has no snapshots, brings a decision of its own.
- The Dockerfile of `spec` has no `apt` packages. `canvas` was the first to need the rule: 21 Chromium libraries on Ubuntu 24.04 and fonts, in its T08 (R13 canvas).

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-10-21 to В21 of `.github`, by its recommendation.
- `apt` does not pin versions itself, and the Playwright image by digest gives the browsers but not their system libraries: in the image those lie outside `/ms-playwright` (architecture 4 .github).
- Snapshots are a service of Ubuntu itself: «The Ubuntu snapshot service makes it possible to see and use the Ubuntu archive as it was at any specified date and time», «Snapshots of the Ubuntu archive are available for any date and time after 1 March 2023» and «We intend to ensure snapshots are available for dates up to at least 2 years in the past, which we may extend if there is demand». Ubuntu 24.04 finds them by itself: «The apt included in Ubuntu 24.04 and later automatically detects when snapshots are supported for a repository». The order of the commands: «the apt update --snapshot [snapshot] command needs to be run immediately before the other apt commands», and «These commands will also fail if the snapshot format is incorrect or the snapshot does not exist» ([Ubuntu Snapshot Service](https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/), read 2026-10-21).
- Checked in a build. The Dockerfile of `canvas` on `main`, commit 88492c4 (pull request #18, T08 canvas), installs the packages with `ARG UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT=20261021T000000Z` and `--snapshot`. In CI run 39691386053 on this commit the `toolchain` stage built, and all 61 packages came from `https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/20261021T000000Z` (the log of the job "TypeScript / test", read 2026-10-21).

— *Rejected:*
- a version for each package, `package=version`: the Ubuntu archive does not keep all old versions, and the build will break when it removes them (the argument of В21 of `.github`);
- the `toolchain` stage from the Playwright image by tag and digest: it has the libraries, but its user is `pwuser`, while the `devcontainer` stage of the template comes from `vscode`;
- an exception in Hard rules for `apt` packages.

— *Cost:* snapshots are promised «up to at least 2 years in the past», not forever. A snapshot that is no longer there will stop the build — then it is raised, like a version. — *Consequence:* the rule of exact versions in RULES.md names the snapshot; `canvas` already installs its packages this way (R13 canvas), and the other repositories get the rule with their move to a tag (RUN.md, Д15). — RULES.md, Hard rules; R34.

— *Amendment 2026-11-16:* **`apt` reads the snapshot alone. The `RUN` writes a source of its own into a folder of its own — `URIs: https://snapshot.ubuntu.com/ubuntu/<ID>/`, the suites `noble noble-updates noble-backports noble-security` and the components `main universe restricted multiverse` of the base image's `ubuntu.sources`, `Signed-By: /usr/share/keyrings/ubuntu-archive-keyring.gpg` —, gives `apt-get update` and `apt-get install` that folder alone, `-o Dir::Etc::SourceList=/dev/null -o Dir::Etc::SourceParts=<folder>`, and removes it with the lists; `--snapshot` is no longer given. The ID is still the `ARG` `UBUNTU_SNAPSHOT` beside the list, raised by hand, and the list of packages is as it was. The base image's own sources stay as they are.** The author's decision of 2026-11-15 on the speed of CI (R76; RUN.md, T166). — *Why:* `apt-get update --snapshot` fetched 67.6 MB, the indexes of the live archive and of the snapshot both, and `snapshot.ubuntu.com` gave from 259 kB/s (measurements 3.1); the source of its own fetches 33.6 MB, and from an empty state of dpkg both resolve the same 431 packages at the same versions; the same URI serves `arm64` (measurements 3.2). — *Rejected:* `--snapshot` with the base image's sources, as before — the cost above; removing the base image's `ubuntu.sources` — a person's `apt` in the devcontainer would then read the snapshot alone; fewer suites or components — a smaller download, but then the resolution is no longer the base image's by construction. — *Consequence:* `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile`; `app`, `canvas` and `skill-map` take it with their moves to the tag, rows 7.22–7.24 of [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md), and `api` by row 7.15. — R79; RUN.md, T166; measurements 3.2.

— *Second amendment 2026-11-16:* **the rule of exact versions in RULES.md words the amendment above: a system package comes from a snapshot of the Ubuntu archive alone, from a source of its own whose URI names the snapshot by its ID, an `ARG` beside the list of packages, and not from the live archive; it no longer names `--snapshot`.** The answer to the row «в реестр spec» `canvas` В81, by its recommendation: RULES.md is loaded into every session of every repository, and a hard rule that the template's own `RUN` breaks invites a session to put the flags back. — *Rejected:* naming RULES.md in the amendment as not yet changed, until its next edit; leaving RULES.md to cite R40. — RUN.md, T172.

## The modules of the first slice

**R41. The first slice is three modules of two subjects: olympiad maths 1–6, school maths of grade 3 on a workbook, and short essays in English for any age.** О-1 is solved: instead of one second module, two.
- **Olympiad maths 1–6** is module 1 by R08: the learner is a child, the canvas is a handwriting sheet, the answer is a number or an option.
- **School maths of grade 3.** The learner is a child, the canvas is a workbook (concepts 8): the task's items stand on the non-erasable layer of the template, and the answer to each is a number or a fraction by hand in its answer slot. A verdict is given on each item (concepts 6, 9.2).
- **Short essays in English.** The canvas is a handwriting sheet, the essay is written by hand in free form. This is writing, not a language module: the explanations are in English, there is no target language (concepts 3).
  - AI reads the essay — reading of handwriting — and assesses it by the author's criteria — assessment by a rubric (concepts 10). The learner gets feedback by the rubric, not a verdict (R04).
  - Tasks with a key — for example, choosing the best first sentence — get a verdict.
  - The module is for any age, and the presentation style is by the learner's age (concepts 13). So an adult learner has a module of their own in the first slice, and the adult learner's account (R26) and the own key (О-4) stay in the slice.
- There are no third-party authors in the first slice (product 10), so all three modules are official. The canvases of the slice are the handwriting sheet and the workbook; there is no text canvas in it.
- The screens of the prototype — a page of ten examples on fractions and the essay «My best day» — are illustrations, not content: the solving steps, the traps and the topics are written by `modules` (R02).

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-22, by the screens of the prototype, which the author updated the same day ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)). The arguments are the plan's proposal:
- The main hypothesis — that AI understands the learner's free solution and reads the answer correctly (product 2) — all three modules test on handwriting: on a number on the sheet, on fractions in answer slots and on a whole text. The answers of Spanish — an edit and typing — a program would check without AI (architecture 4.2).
- The workbook brings what an olympiad task does not have: a task of many items with answer slots of their own on one sheet (concepts 6), the non-erasable layer of the template (concepts 8), the check kind "fraction and form" (concepts 9.2) and a series of items of one type that weighs less than the sum (concepts 11).
- Essays are the second subject and a path without a key: feedback by a rubric instead of a verdict (R04; product 4), the author's order for skills with a rubric (concepts 4, 5) and the learner's work as their artifact (concepts 8). One module serves both a child and an adult, with a different presentation style and different AI routes (R06, R07).
- The two maths give the first real reference between modules: the olympiad one rests on school skills only through the shared taxonomy (concepts 4; Т-14). In the prototype one module depends on another by package name, and the documents do not allow this ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)).

— *Rejected:*
- Spanish A1 for adults — the recommendation of О-1. Its answers do not test AI reading, it needs a text canvas of its own — a kind of its own on the page markup, not a sheet (R05 canvas) — and the step "pronounce" waits for voice input (О-6). It stays a module for later;
- olympiad maths and essays, without the workbook: format v0 would not meet tasks of many items with answer slots on one sheet;
- physics with a bench: it needs a widget, and widgets are stage 4 (architecture 3.4);
- school maths alone — a sheet with fractions, the third option of О-1: the format would be tested on one subject (R08).

— *Consequence:*
- R08 by an amendment: there are three modules, and still two subjects — maths and writing.
- The first slice has assessment by a rubric (architecture 3.6). What to measure it by is О-22. Whether feedback by a rubric affects the learner model is О-17, and it now concerns the first slice.
- An essay has no incorrect answers, and so no hint ladder (concepts 10): what a hint on request gives is О-21 and RUN.md, T30. The leak check has nothing to look for — there is no key — and the tutor must not write the essay for the learner (R05): how to hold this is decided by the detailing of assessment by a rubric (architecture 3.6).
- The path without AI — a typed answer or a choice (architecture 4.2; О-5) — the first slice tries only with tasks with a choice.
- An essay is the learner's free text: what the server keeps of an attempt is П-19, what a module may ask to write about is П-20, whether to keep the essays themselves is П-8.
- The text canvas, the check kinds "text" and "edit", and a language module where the target language is not the explanation language are not tested by the first slice. What happens to them in format v0 is decided by RUN.md, T29, and how a new canvas kind or check kind fits the format versions, by T23.
- The explanations of the essays module are in English. Translations in the module are RUN.md, T26, and the interface and explanation languages of the slice are О-2, which is open.
- The components that were planned for Spanish A1 get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д18.

— product 10, 13.1; architecture 3.2, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.10; repositories 2.1, 6.

## Normative texts

**R42. The normative texts for authors are in English and outside `docs/`. The module format lies in the folder `format/` at the root of `spec`: the schemas, the format text and the test vectors.** О-3 is solved.
- The normative texts are what an author writes a module by, and what the platform's code reads and checks it by: the module format, the widget protocol and the guides for authors.
- **The module format** is the schemas with descriptions (Т-7), the format text and the test vectors of the format.
  - **The format text** is the rules that a schema cannot express: a graph without cycles, the references and keys that `module-kit` checks (architecture 3.7), the meaning of the check kinds and of normalization (concepts 9.2), open fields (R05), the format versions (Т-11).
  - The test vectors are normative: an implementation that does not pass them does not conform to the format.
  - The examples show the format and test the schemas, but add no rules.
- The format is normative: what a module may and must contain and how the platform checks it is said by the schemas, the format text and the test vectors, and `docs/` describe it. A divergence is an error, and one change fixes it. The field names are the English terms of concepts 15, and a new or changed term goes there first; a decision changes only by an amendment (RULES.md, How we work).
- `docs/` stay descriptive and in Russian (R14).
- The layout inside `format/` and the file names are decided by RUN.md, T24. Where the random generator and its test vectors lie — they are shared by `module-kit`, `engine` and `sim` (R27) — is decided by T32, and where the widget protocol and the guides lie, by epic E5. The language of all of them is this one.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-22 by the recommendation of О-3: a standard that "any author" writes by cannot be in Russian only, and the descriptive documents stay in Russian. RULES.md already requires the descriptions of schemas in English, and the format text beside the schemas is changed by the same change as they are. The code of `module-kit`, which carries out the format, is in English too (R14). A separate folder is the plan's proposal: in `docs/` everything is in Russian (R14).

— *Rejected:*
- normative texts in Russian, like the documents (R14): an author who does not read Russian could not read the standard;
- only the descriptions in the schemas, without a format text: the rules that a schema does not express would live in the descriptive `docs/`, in Russian;
- the format text in English in `docs/`: the folder would mix language and role;
- two languages with a translation: at each divergence one would have to decide which of them is normative.

— *Consequence:* R14 by an amendment. The rule on language in RULES.md and rule 10 of RUN.md name the normative texts, repositories 5 the folder `format/`, and concepts 15 the terms "module format" and "format text". The folder appears with the first schema, and then CLAUDE.md names it too (RUN.md, T24). — repositories 5; RULES.md, Hard rules.

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* the format versions that the format text writes about were decided by R44 — the author's answer to Т-11. "The format versions (Т-11)" above reads "the format versions (R44)": the format text writes about them by R44, and its section on versions comes together with the folder `format/` (RUN.md, T24).

— *Amendment 2026-10-22:* the folder and its layout were decided by R45 — the author's answer to Т-7 and to the questions of T24.
- "The folder appears with the first schema" no longer holds: the folder `format/` appeared before the schemas, in RUN.md, T24, with the format text and the version number `format/VERSION`. The author agreed to this by approving the plan of T24.
- "The layout inside `format/` and the file names are decided by RUN.md, T24" is decided in R45.
- "The schemas with descriptions (Т-7)" in the item "The module format": Т-7 is closed by the same R45, and the schemas are JSON Schema 2020-12.

"`docs/` stay descriptive and in Russian (R14)" above reads "`docs/` stay descriptive (R14)". ## The first code of stage 2

**R43. The first code of stage 2 is the review board of `tutor`, and the large measurement of AI reading is put off until the author decides by the board's data.** The answer to the rows «в реестр spec» `tutor` В15 and В20 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 3660eac).
- **The review board** (R19 tutor). The author solves five fixed tasks by hand — sometimes with an error on purpose or illegibly. Two models of two providers read the solution and assess it themselves: correct, an error in line N, or cannot read. Under each answer the author marks whether the model is right, and the summary counts how often each is right. There is no program check on the board.
- **Where.** The command `tutor-eval board` — the eval CLI of `tutor` (R15) — listens only on the local address 127.0.0.1 in the devcontainer, and the page opens in the browser on the author's computer. This is not a service: `tutor` still has no process of its own (R15). The board has its own simple sheet, not the sheet of `canvas`.
- **Data.** The handwriting and the marks are only the author's own, an adult's. The pictures and the log lie with the author, outside git (R05 tutor), and the models are called with keys for eval only (R24).
- **The model's assessment on the board is what the board measures, not a verdict for a learner.** For the product, R03 and R04 stand: a program delivers the verdict. Whether to revisit them, the author decides by the board's data.
- **The large measurement** — about 110 sheets and statistics (architecture 3.1 tutor) — is put off: it will be returned to if the board shows that it is needed. What waits with it, rather than being cancelled: the release of `tutor` with the open views of the measurement's tasks for CI of `canvas` (R25), the check of the synthetic samples of `canvas` in CI of `tutor` (R38), and the measurement's conclusions, by which Т-23 and О-8 are decided.

Иногда специально ошибаться или писать неразборчиво. ИИ будет пытаться понять что я написал и выдавать свою оценку — решил правильно или с ошибкой. Далее я жму кнопку ИИ был прав или нет. Всё. Никаких проверок с твоей стороны не нужно вообще». The record in `spec` follows the recommendations of `tutor` in В15 and В20: the card and repositories 6 named as the first code of the stage what is put off, and `canvas` would build the samples page for a release of `tutor` that will not come for now.
