## Shared taxonomy

**R50. The shared taxonomy is a dictionary of anchor skills in the module format: the schema `format/schemas/shared-taxonomy.schema.json`, where each anchor skill is a branch of `oneOf` with the ID `core.<name>`, a title and a description. A module's skill rests on an anchor skill as a prerequisite and teaches it with the field `teaches`, and the manifest names the anchor skills on which the module's skills rest in `dependencies`. The dictionary is part of the format version.** The author's answers when planning RUN.md, T27, and the task T42 recorded them; Т-14 is closed. Normatively it is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), section 13, and in sections 2, 11 and 12, and in the schemas `shared-taxonomy.schema.json`, `skill-graph.schema.json` and `manifest.schema.json`; here is what was decided, why, and what was rejected.
- **The dictionary** is the format's schema `shared-taxonomy.schema.json`. Its instance is the ID of an anchor skill: at the root a string and the form of the ID, and each anchor skill is a branch of `oneOf`, where the ID is `const`, the title `title`, the description `description`. An ID that is not in the dictionary the schema itself rejects. It describes no part of a module and is never a module's file: it is referred to by the parts that name anchor skills. The platform curates the dictionary, in `spec`.
- **The ID** is `core.<name>`, where the name is in kebab-case starting with a letter: `core.multiplication-table`.
  - The dot separates the namespace: the ID of an anchor skill cannot be confused with a local ID or with a module ID, which have no dots.
  - The ID has no subject: a module of any subject may rest on an anchor skill.
  - The ID is the same in a module and outside it. An anchor skill has no full ID: it is not part of a module, and the learner model, the engine and progress know it by this ID.
- **The title and the description** are English text of the schema, not text of a module: an anchor skill has no explanation language. The description says what a learner who knows the skill can do, and it is normative: it is the meaning of the anchor skill.
- **Where a module names anchor skills:**
  - in a skill's prerequisites — what it needs. A prerequisite is a skill of the module by its local ID or an anchor skill by its own ID: in the schema this is an `anyOf` of the two;
  - in a skill's `teaches` — what it teaches: a learner who knows the skill can do what the description of each anchor skill says. One anchor skill may be taught by several skills of one module or of different ones;
  - in the manifest's `dependencies` — what the module's skills rest on. A module whose skills need no anchor skills does not write the field. So one manifest shows what the module rests on.
- **Rules:**
  - `skill-graph.own-anchors` — a skill does not name as a prerequisite an anchor skill that a skill of the same module teaches, itself included. A skill that needs what its own module teaches names the module's skill: so the module's graph holds this link, and the tiers and the check of cycles see it;
  - `manifest.dependencies` — `dependencies` names exactly the anchor skills that the prerequisites of the module's skill graph name: each, and no other. The rule links two files, and its vectors are folders laid out as a module.

  `module-kit` checks them, and `spec`'s CI checks the YAML and the schemas of their vectors ([format text](../format/README.md), section 9). Anchor skills do not count toward the tier: they are not skills of the module, and a skill all of whose prerequisites are anchor skills stands in tier 1.
- **Versions.** The dictionary is part of the format version (R44):
  - a new anchor skill and the mark `"deprecated": true` are a minor version: a module may name a marked anchor skill until a major version removes it;
  - the removal of an anchor skill and a change of its meaning are a major one. The meaning under the same ID does not change: a skill with a new meaning comes under a new ID, and the earlier ID is removed;
  - other words of the same meaning in the description are an editorial change, without a new version;
  - the ID of an anchor skill is not reused;
  - v1 holds only the anchor skills that a module of the first slice names.
- **The learner model and the engine.** Whether a learner knows an anchor skill `learner-model` decides by the skills that teach it, in the learner's modules (architecture 3.8). An anchor skill that no module of the learner teaches does not hold back a skill that needs it: the engine counts it as unknown (concepts 4). The format checks each module separately, so it does not see a cycle of prerequisites between modules through anchor skills.
- **The first anchor skills** are `core.multiplication-table`, `core.division-with-remainder`, `core.fractions-of-a-whole` and `core.linear-equations`. In the format's examples the first three are taught by the school mathematics of grade 3, and the olympiad one rests on division with remainder and fractions of a whole. The fourth is taken by no module of the slice: it is for the third-party module of concepts 16.3, and it will not enter v1 unless a module of the slice takes it (R44).
- **What R50 does not decide:**
  - how a third-party author proposes an anchor skill of their own — that is the publication rules (О-9);
  - the index of the modules that teach an anchor skill — RUN.md, T34;
  - whether a supporting skill of a task may be an anchor skill, as in concepts 16.3 — RUN.md, T28;
  - how `learner-model` derives knowledge of an anchor skill from the skills that teach it — and from skills with `rubric` or `none`, which have no verdict (О-17) — and what the engine does with a cycle between modules: that is their detailing (architecture 3.8);
  - which version part of a module an edit of `teaches` or `dependencies` raises — the semver rules of `module-kit` (T04 module-kit). To remove `teaches` is to take an anchor skill away from the modules that rest on it;
  - translations of the titles and descriptions of anchor skills: there are no translations in format v0 (R46).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-26 when planning T27, by the plan's recommendations: the dictionary as a schema of the format, an anchor skill as a branch of `oneOf`, the ID `core.<name>`, the dictionary in the format version, the prerequisite and `teaches` on the skill, `dependencies` in the manifest and the first four anchor skills (RUN.md, T42, «Решено автором»). The rest — the rules `skill-graph.own-anchors` and `manifest.dependencies`, the meaning of `teaches`, the tier without anchor skills and what an anchor skill means for the learner model and the engine — is the proposal of the plan of T27, which the author approved. All was read 2026-10-26.
- **A schema, not a data file.** An unknown anchor skill the schema itself rejects, and no format rule of its own is needed for it. `const` "is functionally equivalent to an "enum" … with a single value" ([JSON Schema 2020-12 validation](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-validation), §6.1.3), and a branch of `oneOf` carries a title and a description besides: "A title will preferably be short, whereas a description will provide explanation about the purpose of the instance described by this schema" (ibid., §9.1). The mark `deprecated` in a branch concerns only its own anchor skill: it "applies to each instance location to which the schema object containing the keyword successfully applies", and it means that "applications SHOULD refrain from usage of the declared property. It MAY mean the property is going to be removed in the future" (ibid., §9.3). The dictionary goes into the releases as one more schema, together with the others.
- **The prerequisite and `teaches`** are as in schema.org. `teaches` — "The item being described is intended to help a person learn the competency or learning outcome defined by the referenced term", and `competencyRequired` — "Knowledge, skill, ability or personal attribute that must be demonstrated by a person or other entity in order to do something such as earn an Educational Occupational Credential or understand a LearningResource". Among the values of both is `DefinedTerm`, a term of a vocabulary ([schema.org, teaches](https://schema.org/teaches) and [competencyRequired](https://schema.org/competencyRequired), V30.1 of 2026-09-16). So both what a skill needs and what it teaches are linked to an anchor skill.
- **Modules only through the dictionary**, as Т-14 recommended (concepts 4). In the prototype a module rests on another module by the package name and a range of versions — `math-g3 ^1.5` ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)) —, and then renaming or retiring a skill in one module would break another. An anchor skill a module will neither rename nor retire.
- **`dependencies` is exactly the anchor skills of the graph's prerequisites.** A list that the author writes by hand beside the graph would drift from it, as tiers typed by hand would drift (R49). The rule holds them together, and the manifest shows what the module rests on, without the graph.
- **The tier is without anchor skills.** The tier is difficulty within a module (R49), and an anchor skill from another module would shift the tiers, though nothing changed in the module itself.
- **A new meaning is a new ID**, as for a module's skill (R49). The learner model knows an anchor skill only by its ID, and from v1 the platform reads two major format versions at once (R44): if the meaning changed under the same ID, the evidence of the earlier meaning would count toward the new one. This reading of the author's answer «удаление и смена смысла — мажорная, ID не переиспользуется» was proposed by the review of T42.

— *Rejected:*
- the ID `core.<subject>.<name>`, as in the illustration of concepts 16.3: the subject would bind the anchor skill to itself forever;
- a data file `format/shared-taxonomy.yaml` with a schema of its own: it needs code of `format-check`, a rule for an unknown anchor skill and a second file in the release;
- the shared taxonomy as one task with the skill graph — by rule 11 of RUN.md;
- dependencies without a field in the manifest, which `module-kit` computes into the package, like the tier. The field in the manifest the author decided (R46; RUN.md, T42, «Решено автором»): the manifest shows what the module rests on, without the graph, and the rule `manifest.dependencies` — the plan's proposal — does not let the field drift from the graph.

— *Consequence:*
- Т-14 is closed (repositories 8). Amendments to R44 — the dictionary in the format version —, to R45 — the dictionary's schema describes no parts, and `teaches` is a link named by a verb —, to R46 — the field `dependencies` and the ID of an anchor skill — and to R49 — a prerequisite may be an anchor skill.
- concepts 3, 4, 11, 15 and 16.3 — the anchor skill, module dependencies, the prerequisite and the shared taxonomy; architecture 3.7 and 3.8; repositories 5 — the dictionary in `format/`.
- RUN.md, T34 — the index of the modules that teach an anchor skill (the record at table 1). The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д31.

— concepts 3, 4, 11, 15, 16.3; architecture 3.7, 3.8; repositories 5, 8; [format/README.md](../format/README.md), sections 2, 3, 5, 10–13; RUN.md, T42, Д31.

— *Amendment 2026-10-26:* a supporting skill of a task may be an anchor skill, and the primary one only a skill of the module (R51; RUN.md, T28). An anchor skill that a skill of the same module teaches the task does not name; it names that skill — the rule `task.own-anchors`, like `skill-graph.own-anchors` for prerequisites. A supporting anchor skill does not enter `dependencies`: it still holds what the graph's prerequisites name.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* the index of the modules that teach an anchor skill was decided by R63: each record of the index has `teaches`, the anchor skills that the skills of its graph teach. "RUN.md, T34" about the index in "What R50 does not decide" and in "Consequence" reads as RUN.md, T44 and R63. — R63; RUN.md, T44.

## Task

**R51. A task is a file `tasks/<id>.yaml`: the task statement, the canvas, the items with their answer slots, the skills, the band and the difficulty, and where needed the age categories it suits. A module's difficulty scale is the bands in the module manifest, and the digit height on a crop is there too. An item's key is RUN.md, T29. The rule `module.media` checks the media files, and `spec` builds the open view itself.** The author's answers in planning RUN.md, T28. Normatively this is written in English in the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 6, 9, 10, 11 and 14, and in the schemas `task.schema.json`, `manifest.schema.json` and `common.schema.json`; here is what is decided, why, and what is rejected.
- **A task** is `tasks/<id>.yaml` by the schema `task.schema.json`, and its `id` is the file's name without `.yaml`: the rule `module.file-ids`. An item's key or predicate — the check kind — RUN.md, T29 will add, and until it the tasks of the examples have no keys: version 0.1 is a draft (R44).
- **The task statement** is parts in order: a paragraph `text` or a picture.
  - A paragraph is plain text in the module's explanation language. There are no formulas and no sound in a statement in v0: each will come with a minor version.
  - A picture has `picture`, a path in `media/` to a PNG, JPEG or WebP file; `alt`, what is on it in words: a screen reader reads it, and it stands in the picture's place until the picture has arrived, and it is empty only for a decoration; `width` and `height`, the size in CSS px.
  - The statement is part of the author's template, which the learner neither erases nor changes. Whether it is above the canvas or on it, the canvas kind decides: the handwriting sheet shows it above the sheet (R23 canvas). This answers В34 `canvas`, and concepts 6 and 8 are amended.
- **The canvas belongs to the task,** one for all the items. `kind` is `handwriting_sheet` or `workbook`.
  - The handwriting sheet is 1000 × 1400 units from the top left corner, and the size is a constant of the kind (R06 canvas). The task gives it a grid `grid` — `squares`, `lines` or `dots`, without the field squares — and its step `grid_step` from 20 to 500 units, without the field 50.
  - The workbook is a page of lines, a line per item, and how the lines lie on the page is decided by `canvas`.
  - Every task has a pen and an eraser. There is no field of tools in v0: it will come with a minor version, with the first module that needs a ruler or a calculator.
- **Items and answer slots.** An item is named by its place in the task, from 1, and an answer slot by its place among the item's slots.
  - On the sheet, an item has slots `answer_slots` and, where needed, `text`: what it asks, "a)".
  - In the workbook, an item is a line `line`: pieces of text and boxes in order, at least one box, and a box anywhere — "7 × [ ] = 56", "56 [ ] 65", "[ ] apples". The line's boxes are its answer slots. A two-storey fraction and column arithmetic will come later, and what cannot be written so, RUN.md, T38 will gather.
- **The bindings of v0** are what the three modules of the slice need:
  - `anywhere` — anywhere on the sheet: AI finds the final answer (R61 canvas-api);
  - `sheet` — the whole sheet, the work as a whole, like an essay;
  - `zone` — in a zone: a rectangle of the sheet, `left` and `top` from the left and top edges, `width` and `height`, in units of the sheet. The names are not `x` and `y`: a plain `y` breaks `yaml.plain-strings`;
  - `choice` — a choice among the options `options`: two or more, without repeats, in order;
  - `box` — a box of a workbook line.

  On the sheet, `anywhere`, `sheet`, `zone` and `choice`; in the workbook, `box`. A slot `anywhere` or `sheet` is the only one in its task: AI would not tell two final answers "anywhere" apart. Keyboard input, an edit in a text and a widget's state will come later, with a minor version, and v1 will take in only what a module of the slice took (R44): nobody takes `zone` yet.
- **Skills** — `primary`: the module's skills by local ID that the task trains, and a wrong answer is evidence against them; `supporting`: the skills the answer needs and that a wrong answer does not lower — skills of the module or anchor skills. An item's own `skills` replace the task's skills for it.
- **The difficulty scale is bands and a difficulty inside a band, as in standalone.** The module manifest lists the bands `bands` in order, from the easiest: `id`, `title` and, for a module with grades, `grades`. A task names its band `band` and its difficulty `difficulty` from 1 to 5 inside it. A learner of a grade starts in the band of their grade; where a learner outside the bands starts and how far apart the bands are, `learner-model` decides.
- **The digit height on a crop** is `canvas.digit_height` in the module manifest: whole px from 1 to 256, without the field 32. The setting is one per module, and how the app gets it with a task RUN.md, T34 decides. This answers В38 `canvas` in its part on the digit height.
- **A task's age categories** are `age_categories`: fewer than the module's, and the platform gives the task only to learners of those categories. This is the mark that П-20 awaited: a module can give a topic about the learner's life to adults alone.
- **There is no provenance in a module:** everything in a module comes from the author, and a task has no field for it. A key from the solver will come with the templates (RUN.md, T33), and "entered by an adult" and "derived by AI" are the provenance of tasks from paper (О-11), which modules do not have.
- **standalone's pictures** are files in `media/`: in the port, `modules` draws them into files with a description (RUN.md of `modules`, T03). Kinds of pictures that `canvas` draws will come later, with a minor version.
- **Open and closed.** Open are `id`, the statement, the canvas and the items with all their fields: the app shows them. Closed are the skills, the band, the difficulty and the age categories: the server reads them. Opening a field later is a major version (R44).
- **Rules:**
  - of the module manifest — `manifest.bands`: if bands are written, their IDs differ; in a module with grades each band names its grades, and each grade of `audience.grades` is in exactly one; in a module without grades the bands name no grades;
  - of a task — `task.known-skills`, `task.skill-roles`, `task.own-anchors`, `task.known-band`, `task.known-pictures`, `task.age-categories` and `task.zones`; zones touching at their edges is not an overlap. `module-kit` checks them, and the CI of `spec` checks their vectors' YAML and schemas;
  - of the whole module — `module.file-ids` and `module.media`. These, like `module.manifest` and `module.layout`, `format-check` checks itself.
- **Media files** go by the signatures of [WHATWG MIME Sniffing](https://mimesniff.spec.whatwg.org/), "Last Updated 19 October 2026", read 2026-10-26: PNG — `89 50 4E 47 0D 0A 1A 0A`, JPEG — `FF D8 FF`, WebP — "RIFF", four bytes and "WEBPVP" (§6.1); MP3 — "ID3" or a frame header of layer III (§6.2). The signature is what `module.media` reads: the rest of the file is the author's concern.
- **The open view** `spec` builds itself: the vectors `format/vectors/open-view/` and their check in `format-check` (the amendment to R45).
- **What R51 does not decide:**
  - the key, the check kinds, and whether a skill's assessability matches how its items are checked — RUN.md, T29;
  - traps, the solution, hints, the givens and the unknown — RUN.md, T30;
  - templates and the key from the solver — RUN.md, T33;
  - how the app gets the digit height and the explanation language with a task — RUN.md, T34;
  - sound and formulas in the statement, the field of tools, styling for the learner's interests and kinds of pictures that `canvas` draws — with minor versions, with the module that needs them;
  - what a module may ask a learner under 18 to write about — П-20 and epic E4.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-26 in planning T28 — sixteen, all by the plan's recommendations but the first: the author kept the task as one (RUN.md, T28, «Решено автором»). The rest — the rules, the forms of the schema, the names of the fields, the check of the media and of the open view — is the plan's proposal after an independent agent checked the draft. All read 2026-10-26.
- **Bands and difficulty are as in standalone,** commit c6cbeb2: "a task has a level — the band of grades it is written for — and a difficulty inside that level" ([SPEC.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/mathtrail-standalone/blob/c6cbeb2/SPEC.md), section 1.1), and the starting point is the band of the grade: `Start(grade)` in `internal/domain/rating/ladder.go` returns the offset of the band the grade falls in. The bands are 2.5 apart and overlap: a task's hardness there is its band's offset plus the difficulty minus 3. One scale of rungs would not express the overlap, and the numbers are the model's business, not the format's.
- **The term is "difficulty band":** "level" in concepts 11 already means the learner's level, and a term means one thing.
- **The bindings follow the slice.** Anywhere on the sheet is as in canvas-api: «Поля ответа нет: ребёнок решает и пишет итоговый ответ где угодно на листе … а итог находит модель» ("There is no answer field: the child solves and writes the final answer anywhere on the sheet … and the model finds the final answer") ([docs/decisions.md](https://github.com/mathtrail/canvas-api/blob/0901af0/docs/decisions.md), R61 canvas-api). The box is for the workbook, the whole sheet for an essay, and the choice for the assignments with a key among the essays and for standalone's tasks: there an answer is always a choice among five options. What the slice does not take will not enter v1 (R44), and so it is not in v0 either.
- **The workbook line** is the author's answer: a box in a workbook example happens both at the start and in the middle, and text and boxes in order write any such example without a markup language.
- **The statement above the sheet** is how `canvas` shows it (R23 canvas), and, by В34 `canvas` (RUN.md of `canvas`, commit 5feb06f), so do the others: "So in canvas-api — «текст над листом, а не часть листа» ("the text above the sheet, not a part of the sheet"), — on the review board of `tutor` and in the prototype of `spec`". The picture's description and size are also by В34: without a description a picture that has not arrived cannot be read, and without a size the sheet shifts under the pen when it arrives.
- **The skills are closed:** a skill's title — "gaps and posts" on a task about a staircase — hints at the way to solve it, and R05 closes what gives that away. Opening it later is a major version, and then it will also be decided what to show before the solution.
- **There is no provenance:** standalone has none either — "Nobody else's wording, anywhere. The ideas come from open sources; the text is ours" (SPEC 1.5 standalone) —, and the tasks that AI helped to write the author checks before publication (concepts 9.3).
- **Pictures are files:** standalone's 13 kinds of pictures are drawn by its card — "an object of one of thirteen kinds, which the card draws as SVG" (SPEC 4.4 standalone). Taking them into the format would mean 13 schemas and 13 drawers in `canvas` for the sake of one module, while a file with a description any browser shows.
- **The open view goes by the annotations of 2020-12:** the definition "a mark counts only where the subschema passes" is exactly the collection of annotations by the 2020-12 core, §7.7.1.2, and the two implementations — `format-check` and `module-kit` — are compared by the vectors.
- **Two bugs of `ajv` 8.20.0** were found in this task. `unevaluatedProperties` counts a place's fields as unevaluated when beside it stands `dependentSchemas` without its own key, or `$ref` together with `oneOf` or `anyOf` whose passing branch is not the first. By 2020-12 such a part is valid, while `format-check` would reject it. The format's schemas take neither, and a test of `format-check` pins the behaviour of `ajv`: if it changes, the test will say so. What to do about this further is the question В25 of RUN.md.

— *Rejected:*
- three tasks — T28, media and pictures, the open view — or two, T28 and media: the author kept one;
- a stub of the check field with the kinds "number" and "choice" in T28 — T29 decides the kinds;
- one scale of rungs with a starting rung for each grade; one number of difficulty for a task;
- a picture's size from its file; the statement on the template layer, as was said in concepts 6 and 8;
- a zone in cells of the grid — it would shift when the step changes;
- a canvas for each item;
- the bindings "keyboard input", "edit" and "widget state" in v0;
- the age mark later; styling for interests in v0;
- a field of provenance in a task;
- standalone's kinds of pictures in v0;
- the digit height in each task, as `canvas.digit` in the temporary type of `canvas`;
- only the module's skills among the supporting skills;
- the text of a workbook item, and the boxes after it;
- a field of tools of the pen and the eraser;
- "difficulty level", `level`;
- the task's skills open.

— *Consequence:*
- concepts 3, 4, 6, 8, 9.4, 11, 12, 13, 15 and 16 — the task statement, items, slots and bindings, bands and difficulty, the canvas, the age mark; privacy 9 — П-20 added to; architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.4, 3.5, 3.7, 3.8 and 3.10; repositories 3, 4 and 5; README.md and CLAUDE.md.
- Amendments to R25, R45, R46, R49 and R50.
- What R51 changes in the tasks of epic E2 is said by «Решено автором (2026-10-26, T28)» at table 1 of RUN.md. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д32.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **the default digit height is 24 px, from format version 0.2.** The author's decision on the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В39 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), its third option. It differs both from the recommendation of `tutor` and from the rule that `tutor` wrote down before the run: that gave 16 px (R48 tutor).
- **The measurement of E4 `tutor`** (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера чтения» and «Итог замера тетради»; R37 and R42 tutor). The heights 16, 24 and 48 px were compared with 32 px in pairs, by sheets, without the key, on Haiku 5.5 · `low` and Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking:
  - on 68 test sheets, 16 and 24 px are no worse than 32 px on both. 48 px on Haiku · `low` is worse: 12 extra "unreadable" against 5, p 0.033. There were no other errors at the heights;
  - on 15 test workbook pages, 16, 24 and 48 px are also no worse than 32 px on both, and there are no new false "correct";
  - a sheet's picture at 16 px is about 90 tokens against about 200 at 32 px. The crop of a workbook box at 16, 24 and 32 px is one and the same: 200 × 200, 64 tokens.
- **Why 24 and not 16.** The handwriting of the measurement is synthetic data, even and large, while live handwriting is smaller and less even: 24 px leave a margin. The gain in price at 16 px is small — the whole input about 1,300 tokens against 1,400. On sheets with lowercase letters the digits on a crop are, besides, larger than the height from the module manifest (RUN.md, epic E3, the crop rule).
- **When this enters the format.** A new default value changes the behaviour of a module without the field, and that is a new format version. "A minor version only adds", and of default values the text puts among the patch changes only "a parameter whose default keeps the previous behaviour" ([format text](../format/README.md), section 2; R44). So 24 px come with version 0.2, in a new line of `spec`, and a task of its own makes it — RUN.md, T48. Until then a module of format 0.1 without the field is read at 32 px, and `canvas` without a module manifest draws the crop at 32 (R36).
- **Recheck** on the handwriting of adult volunteers (П-16) before the modules of the slice come out without the field (R48 tutor).

*Why:* the author's decision: the middle between the rule's advice and the former height (R48 tutor). To record the decision now and to make format 0.2 task T48 is also the author's decision: the format version is in about 140 examples and vectors of `format/`, and the digests of the package and index vectors depend on it.

*Rejected:*
- 16 px — the advice by the rule, but checked only on synthetic data;
- keep 32 px — 24 px is no worse on both parts of the measurement;
- 24 px in format 0.1, without a new version: R44 does not allow it;
- format 0.2 in the same change as this amendment.

*Consequence:* RUN.md, T48 — format 0.2. `canvas` takes 24 px with format 0.2, `tutor` closes В39 — RUN.md, Д47.

## The course of writing and AI

**R52. Nothing of the learner's writing history goes to AI — neither the order of writing, nor the action log, nor the frames before erasure, neither into reading nor into analysis: what goes to the check is an image or a crop, as by R09. So it stays until a measurement on live handwriting and free notation shows that the course of writing helps.** П-21 is closed. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В30 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its first option.
- **What the measurement of `tutor` measured**, 2026-10-26 (R24 and R27 `tutor`; architecture 3.1 tutor, «Итог замера»). The model assessed the finished sheet — `correct`, `error` or `unreadable` — and placed the box of the first error. This went in one call: the model saw the key and the reference solution, as on the review board (R43). By the vocabulary of `spec` this is reading and analysis in one call (architecture 3.6; Т-23), and there was no reading without the key in the measurement. What П-21 calls the course of solution is the course of writing: the order of writing, the pauses and the erasures, what is not on the final image (R55). The forms are the four options of П-21:
  - (A) only the final image;
  - (B) the image and the action log: the lines in the order of writing, pauses from 6 s, erasures and returns to a line — without time, pressure, coordinates and what was erased;
  - (C) the image and up to two frames before erasure: on a frame is what was erased itself;
  - (D) both.

  There are 40 sheets, 30 of them test sheets, with 3 repeats per form. The judges are Opus 5.5 · `high`, Haiku 5.5 · `low` and Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking. The criterion was written down before the first run: form D against form A by sheets, the exact sign test, the threshold p < 0.05. Forms B and C against A the measurement counted without a threshold.
- **The answer by the criterion is "not shown" for all three judges.** On 30 test sheets, 90 answers per form, A → D:
  - Opus 5.5 · `high` — correct 90 and 90, false alarms 0 and 0;
  - Haiku 5.5 · `low` — correct 84 and 72, false alarms 3 and 9, p "harms" 0.10;
  - Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking — correct 65 and 77, false alarms 14 and 8, p "helps" 0.061.

  There is no false "correct" in any answer. Of the comparisons without a threshold, «Итог замера» names one thing for forms B and C: the log without frames gave a false alarm less often for Haiku without thinking — 14 in A, 5 in B and 8 in D. But even in D this judge is right less often than Haiku · `low` by the image alone: 77 against 84.
- **The measurement's caveats.** 39 sheets of the 40 were drawn by code (R26 tutor): the handwriting is even, without blots, and the erasures are exactly to plan. The solutions are written in lines from top to bottom, and there is no free notation — a number line, a drawing, a note at the side — on the sheets. Opus is right already by the image alone, and a help from the course of writing is not visible for it on these sheets by construction. The call "analysis of the course of solution and the hint" with a trap and a rung (architecture 4.1) the measurement did not measure: the model only assessed the sheet and looked for the first error.
- **So** the rule of the recommendation of П-21 applies: of the kinds that give the same benefit, take the one poorest in data. The benefit of the course of writing is not shown: form D, which has both the log and the frames, gave it to no judge, and the log and the frames separately were not measured by the criterion. So one image goes to AI — both into reading and into analysis. R09 and privacy 4 do not change. The check request in the contract `app` ↔ `api` (RUN.md, epic E3) carries the work as an image or a crop, without fields of the course of writing. `tutor` already reads the work by one final image (R27 tutor), and nothing changes in the code.
- **A measurement is not a check of a learner.** The measurement samples from adults carry a writing history (П-18), and the next measurement of `tutor` sends the model the forms with the course of writing — that is how it measures. R52 is about a learner's work that the platform checks.
- **When to return** — with the measurement of `tutor` on the live handwriting of adult volunteers (П-16) and on free notation: it is the first item of epic E4 of RUN.md of `tutor`, and there the answer "not shown" may become another. If a kind beyond the image shows a benefit, it will come with a new decision. As before, it needs an amendment to R09 and privacy 4 and the lawyer's answer: how to count «процесс картинками» and a trace without time and pressure (the recommendation of П-21).

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26 — option (a) of `tutor` in В30. The argument of `tutor`: the recommendation of П-21 came true in its part on reading, while nobody has yet measured the benefit of the course of writing in analysis. A frame before erasure carries what was erased itself, and the log the order and the pauses of the learner's writing: without a shown benefit there is no reason for them to go to the provider (privacy 1).

What the measured call is named is the executor's proposal, named in the question to the author. R27 `tutor` and the row В30 call this call reading. But the model in it saw the key and the task's solution and looked for the first error, and by architecture 3.6 that is the work of analysis, only in one call with reading (Т-23). So the argument of `tutor` holds for the call of analysis and hint (architecture 4.1): its measurement did not measure that. And for the search for the first error with the key there are data, and they did not show a benefit of the course of writing.

— *Rejected:*
- the image in reading, and into analysis the log without what was erased, as the former recommendation of П-21. The log without frames against the image alone the measurement counted only without a threshold, and one thing is visible from it: fewer false alarms for the weakest judge. Opus, though, is right by the image alone, and no help is visible for it on these sheets by construction. To let the log go to the provider without a shown benefit is against the rule of П-21, and it would need an amendment to R09 and the lawyer's answer anyway;
- to wait with the answer for the measurement on live handwriting, option (c) of `tutor`: epic E3 would plan the contract with the question open, while the answer of this measurement is already there — "not shown";
- the course of writing into reading for Haiku without thinking: its gain is not significant (p = 0.061), and in form D it is still below Haiku · `low` by the image alone (R27 tutor);
- the conclusion "the course of writing does not help": the measurement does not prove it — the handwriting is synthetic, there is no free notation, and Opus is faultless on these sheets even without the course of writing.

— *Consequence:*
- П-21 is closed (privacy 9); R09, privacy 1 and 4 do not change.
- Epic E3 of RUN.md writes the contract `app` ↔ `api` without fields of the course of writing.
- `tutor` gets the answer with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

R27 `tutor` also stays — by the author's decision (R27 tutor, amendment 2026-10-28).

## The place on the canvas

**R53. A place on the canvas in the observation and in the contract `app` ↔ `api` is fractions 0–1000 of the crop that the device sent: `[ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]`, integers. Into fractions the adapter of `tutor` converts from the units of its provider, into units of the sheet `canvas` does, and `sheet_box` does not leave the device.** Т-32 is closed. The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В31 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), by the first option of Т-32.
- **The Anthropic adapter** takes pixels from the model and converts them into fractions itself. All read 2026-10-26:
  - the model names a place in pixels of the image it processed: "The coordinates Claude returns are pixel positions in the image Claude processes: your image after Claude resizes it to fit the model's native resolution". And in the same place: "Always ask for pixel coordinates and normalize in your own code if you need to" ([Coordinates and bounding boxes](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision-coordinates));
  - the adapter allows no resizing at the provider. It sends the image with `"oversized_image": "error"` (architecture 3.1 tutor), and "No image that sets "error" reaches the model resized" (ibid.). An image larger than the model's limit it scales down itself and knows its size;
  - it divides by the size of the image it sent, not by the size with padding. The model pads every image to a multiple of 28 px on the right and at the bottom, and "Always normalize or rescale by the resized dimensions, not the padded dimensions" (ibid.). A box that went out onto the padding it first clamps to the image: "Clamp returned coordinates to the resized dimensions before rescaling" (ibid.).

  OpenAI has no box format, and Google's models, whose place is fractions 0–1000, are closed (Т-32; R47).
- **The data of the measurement of `tutor`** (R27 tutor; architecture 3.1 tutor, «Итог замера»). A sheet is the whole image 1000 × 600, without a crop, and the model does not scale it down. In the table of sizes, the row "1000x1000 px (1 megapixel)" has "Not resized" at both resolution levels ([Vision](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/vision), read 2026-10-26). For 1000 × 600 both the side and the number of visual tokens, 792, are below both limits. On sheets with an error, the box of the first error in pixels hit its line:
  - for Opus 5.5 · `high` — in 114 answers of 114;
  - for Haiku 5.5 · `low` — in 100;
  - for Haiku 5.5 · `low` without thinking — in 95.

  As a hit the measurement counted the line that has the most visible pixels in the box with a margin of 8 px: this is precision to the line, not finer.
- **The rest is as in the recommendation of Т-32.** Into the same fractions are converted:
  - the tutor's marks in the answer of `api` — a group label, an answer slot or a box;
  - the group boxes, if Т-31 accepts them;
  - the zone of an answer slot, if it has to be shown to reading: `canvas` converts the zone, and the crop stays one.

  A box's validity — integers 0–1000 and min < max — the adapter checks, and an invalid box has no place. How the observation chooses a place — a slot, a label or a box — Т-32 left to the question В12 `tutor`, and that one is recorded as Т-32: now this is decided by epic E3, where the observation is written (R11).

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26: the first option of Т-32, as Т-32 and `tutor` in В31 recommended it, and `canvas` decided so for itself as early as 2026-10-21 (R06 canvas). The observation depends neither on the canvas kind nor on the provider. Only the adapter sees the image's resizing, and only it can recompute a place, while the server does not need the sheet's geometry (R09). The measurement showed that Claude's pixels on an image not resized fall into the right line, and converting them into fractions is the adapter's arithmetic, as Anthropic advises.

— *Rejected:*
- units of the sheet: the adapter would need `sheet_box` from the device, and the sheet's geometry would go to the server;
- fractions, with `api` converting into units of the sheet by `sheet_box` from `app`: the same, and `api` would know the canvas's geometry;
- fractions that the model itself gives: "Claude does not work well when you ask for normalized coordinates" (Coordinates and bounding boxes, ibid.).

— *Consequence:*
- Т-32 is closed (repositories 8). The field of the place in the observation and in the contract is written by epic E3 of RUN.md (R11), and the types for `canvas` come out by the path of T35 (R36).
- architecture 3.2 and 3.6 name the place by R53.
- `tutor` and `canvas` get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

— repositories 8; architecture 3.2, 3.6; RUN.md, table 2, Д33.

"The crop stays one" above is about the sheet's zones.

## The tutor's words

**R54. The tutor's words go to the device whole: `api` gives them when the whole text has passed the leak check, and otherwise the fallback text. Nobody gives them out as a stream; a stream is only for the reading call, whose answer a program reads.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В23 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its first option.
- **Why not a stream.** The leak check looks in the model's text for the key and the leak phrases that the author gave, and a text that did not pass it the fallback text replaces (concepts 10). It runs before any text of the tutor goes to the device (architecture 3.5). A hint that is shown in parts cannot be checked whole before it is shown: the beginning, already shown to the learner, cannot be replaced with the fallback text if the leak is further on.
- **What we pay.** A stream would show the first words earlier. On the review board, where the answer goes as a stream, the first token of Opus 5.5 · `high` came after 1.6 s of 2.5 s (architecture 2.6 tutor, series T45). The learner will see the tutor's words when the model has finished writing them whole.
- **Where the stream stays.** The reading call may stream: its answer a program reads — `module-kit` gives the verdict by the observation (architecture 4.1) —, and the learner sees the verdict, not the model's text. Whether to give the verdict by lines while they arrive — the early verdict, В24 `tutor` — R54 does not decide.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26 by the recommendation of `tutor` in В23. The leak check is a safeguard, not a proof (concepts 10), but there is no other between the model's text and the learner, and what is shown before it bypasses it.

— *Rejected:*
- a stream after the check of the whole text: there is no gain — the first words come at the same time as the whole text;
- a leak check by sentences: the beginning, already shown to the learner, cannot be recalled if the continuation does not pass.

— *Consequence:* architecture 3.5 and 3.6. A real-time channel is still not needed (Т-25). `tutor`, `api` and `app` get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

— architecture 3.5, 3.6; RUN.md, Д33.

A key that already stands in the statement or in the text of its own item is not looked for: there the author's leak phrases guard the answer.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **there is no early verdict by lines in format v0: `module-kit` gives the verdict by the observation whole, when the reading has ended. The early verdict waits for a check kind by steps in a new format version.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В24 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), by the recommendation of `tutor`. - Return with a check kind by steps, if the stream shows that the lines arrive noticeably before the end of the answer.

## The term "solution"

**R55. "Solution" («решение») is the task's solution or the learner's solution, and where the context does not show whose, it is written in full. "Analysis of the course of solution" stays the name of an AI capability, and the order of writing, the pauses and the erasures are the course of writing, not the course of solution.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В25 (RUN.md of `tutor`, commit 7efa0f8), its second option.
- **The task's solution** is its course of solution, the field `solution`: it is shown after the correct answer, and before it does not enter the open view (concepts 15; R05). In a module it is from the author, and for a task from paper AI may derive it, and then it is marked so (concepts 9.4). In code and schemas `solution` is only this.
- **The learner's solution** is how the learner solves the task on the canvas: lines, a drawing, a note at the side. It is part of their work, which goes to the check (concepts 9). Reading reads it, and the analysis of the course of solution looks for the first error in it (architecture 3.6).
- **Where to write it in full** — where both meanings occur side by side: "the model sees the key and the task's solution and looks for the first error in the learner's solution". Where it is clear whose solution is meant, just "solution": "showing the solution" (О-7) is always the task's solution, and "the learner's free solution" (product 2) is already named in full.
- **The course of solution** is the steps of a solution, the task's or the learner's, as they are seen in the notation: "analysis of the course of solution" analyses the steps of the learner's solution in the image.
- **The course of writing** is the order of writing, the pauses and the erasures: what the writing history carries beyond the final image (concepts 15). П-21 and the measurement of `tutor` called it the course of solution, and R52 and onward the course of writing.

— *Why:* the author's decision of 2026-10-26 by the recommendation of `tutor` in В25: it needs the fewest changes both in `spec` and in the components, and "analysis of the course of solution" stays the capability's name. A term means one thing (RULES.md, The bar), and each meaning now has its own full name. The names are the executor's proposal after review. «Решение автора» ("the author's solution"), as in the option of `tutor`, in this log already means a decision of the project's author — "*Why:* the author's decision …" stands at almost every entry —, while the solution of a task from paper is not always from the author (concepts 9.4). "Course of writing" is the word of R26 tutor: it separates what the writing history carries from the steps of a solution, which "analysis of the course of solution" analyses.

— *Rejected:*
- "solution" only for the task's solution, and for the learner "work": work is wider — it is also a text, a typed answer and a widget's state (privacy 4) —, and the capability "analysis of the course of solution" would have to be renamed in the documents of all the components;
- «решение автора» ("the author's solution") — it already means a decision of the project's author, and the solution of a task from paper may be from AI;
- leave it as it is: one term with two meanings is against RULES.md, The bar.

— *Consequence:* concepts 6, 9.4 and 15, architecture 3.6 and 4.1 and privacy 5.1 name the solution in full where the other meaning is beside it, and R52, П-21 and the records of the measurement of `tutor` say "course of writing". `tutor` corrects its documents with its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д33.

— concepts 6, 9.4, 15; architecture 3.6, 4.1; privacy 5.1; RUN.md, Д33.

— *Amendment 2026-11-15:* **"it is shown after the correct answer" above reads so: the task's solution is shown when the attempt is closed — by a correct answer, or by the button that shows it, to a learner of the category `adult` from the start of the attempt and to a child from the fourth wrong answer (R82), and for a task with a rubric by the learner's "Done" (R87).** — R82, R87; R143; RUN.md, T164.

## Slot check

**R56. The check belongs to each answer slot: the field `check` with the check kind and its parameters, closed whole, together with the kind. The kinds of format v0 are `number`, `fraction`, `choice`, `predicate` and `rubric`. How each reads the value and gives the slot's verdict, and how the item's verdict is made up of the slots' verdicts, the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15 says. The verdict vectors are `format/vectors/verdicts/`, and `spec` computes them itself, but for what Starlark gives a predicate.** The author's answers in planning T29 (RUN.md), 2026-10-27.
- **The check is at the slot** — at a slot of the sheet and at a box of a workbook line. The kind and the key stand beside what they check, and the kinds in one line may differ. Which kinds suit which binding, the schema says: `sheet` only a rubric, `choice` a tapped choice, `anywhere`, `zone` and `box` a number, a fraction, a choice by hand and a predicate. An item's "own key" in concepts 6 and 15 reads as the keys of its slots.
- **The kinds of v0** are what the three modules of the slice need: numbers and fractions for the workbooks of school maths, numbers and choice for olympiad maths, rubric and choice for short essays (R41). And the predicate: it will enter v1 only if a module of the slice takes it (the amendment to R44).
  - `number` — an integer, a decimal with a point or a simple fraction; the comparison is by value, in rational numbers, exact. `units` are the words after the number that the check discards.
  - `fraction` — a simple fraction. `form`: `any` — any fraction of the same value, `reduced` — only an irreducible one, and a reducible one of the same value is "not yet".
  - `choice` — by tap, from the options of a slot with the binding `choice`, or by hand, and then the options are in the check itself. So the signs <, > and = in a workbook box are checked: what is read not from the options is "unreadable", not "not yet".
  - `predicate` — a Starlark expression of the read integer `value`, no longer than 1000 characters. `True` is "correct", `False` is "not yet"; an error, a result that is not a `bool`, more than 1,000,000 steps in the count of go.starlark.net, or the clock of `module-kit` — "unchecked".
  - `rubric` — the criteria `criteria`, only on the whole sheet; the result is feedback, not a verdict (R04).
- **The key is a string,** `key: "7"`: a plain `0.1` in YAML is a binary fraction, and an exact comparison with it would give a false "not yet".
- **Value and normalization.** The reader gives a slot's value as it is written, and the check kind normalizes it: NFKC, minus signs and dashes into `-`, the slashes of a fraction and of division into `/`, White_Space spaces one at a time.
  - For numbers, `=` at the start and `.!?` at the end are discarded, the units too, and a superscript or subscript digit is "not in notation".
  - For a choice, also a plain lowercase letter, and nothing is discarded.
  - A notation is up to 16 characters.
- **A slot's verdict:** empty — "unreadable" with the reason `blank`; not in a notation — with the reason `notation`; matched — "correct"; otherwise "not yet". **An item's verdict:** all slots correct — "correct"; at least one "not yet" — "not yet"; otherwise "unreadable", and if there is no such either, "unchecked".
- **Closed whole.** The app gets neither the key, nor the options of a choice by hand, nor the predicate, nor the rubric's criteria, nor the kind. What the learner is to know — which signs the box awaits, by which criteria the essay is judged — the author writes in the task statement (the amendment to R51).
- **Assessability is a rule,** `task.assessability`: the primary skill of an item with a key or a predicate is `verdict`, of an item with a rubric `rubric`, and a skill `none` is only supporting (the amendment to R49).
- **The task's rules** are `task.choice-key`, `task.choice-options`, `task.fraction-key`, `task.predicate-expression` and `task.assessability`. `module-kit` checks them, and their vectors the CI of `spec` checks by the schema and the YAML rules, like the vectors of the other rules of a task (R45).
- **The verdict vectors** are `format/vectors/verdicts/<kind>/<case>.yaml` by the schema `verdict-vector.schema.json`: an item with its checks and its readings — the value of each slot with the verdict of the slot and of the item.
  - `format-check` computes the verdicts as a second implementation, as it builds the open view, and the CI of `module-kit` passes the same vectors.
  - The predicate is an exception: `spec` has no Starlark, and it computes only "blank" and "not in notation" (the amendment to R45).
  - The rest of an observation — whether it is legible, whether it is unambiguous, how many final answers — the vectors do not hold: that is the observation's type, epic E3.
- **The predicate's step limit is in the format:** the same expression on the same value makes the same steps on any machine, and the verdict repeats by the stored value (R03). The clock, its figure and concurrent runs are T03 of `module-kit`.
- **What v0 does not have:** text, edit, quantity, order and set, widget state and "steps" — a check of each line of the course of solution. Each will come as a new kind, with a minor version. This answers В10 `tutor`.

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 14 and 15.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T29 — eight, all by the plan's recommendations but the first: the author kept the task one, together with the predicate and its limits (RUN.md, T29, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Normalization follows canvas-api,** `docs/spec.md`, commit 0901af0, read 2026-10-27: «Unicode NFKC; юникодные минусы и тире заменяются на `-`; пробелы по краям убираются», «Знак `=` в начале и знаки `.`, `!`, `?` в конце отбрасываются: «= 7» и «7.» — это 7», «Слово единицы в конце отбрасывается», and the whitelist of notations comes before parsing (spec 5.2 canvas-api); the comparison is `big.Rat`, and «`3/6` и `0.5` равны» (spec 5.3 canvas-api). The differences:
  - a decimal and a common fraction are in one kind, `number`, like `number` of canvas-api, and an integer is in it too;
  - a superscript digit is "not in notation": NFKC makes `7²` the number 72 (Node 24.21, ICU 78.3, Unicode 17.0);
  - for a choice, `=` and a period are not dropped: they can be the answer.
- **In doubt, "unreadable", not "not yet"** (R04), as in R38 canvas-api: «`INCORRECT` получает только разборчивый, однозначный ответ правильной формы». So a read value that is not among the options of a choice is "unreadable" too: `7` in a box for a sign is a doubt in the reading, not the learner's error. But an answer slot read confidently and wrong is no longer a doubt, and the item with it is "not yet".
- **A reducible fraction where an irreducible one is needed is "not yet",** as `tutor` plans: «несокращённая дробь там, где нужна сокращённая, — «пока нет»» (RUN.md `tutor`, T79, commit 49f4c6a).
- **The predicate is an expression,** not a program: a short check is visible in the task itself, and it needs neither a line of the layout nor a rule about files. standalone's solver programs — the files `content/examples/solvers/<id>.star` (SPEC 1.5 and 6 standalone, commit 99d8a65) — are needed by the keys of templates, RUN.md, T33. The step limit is as in standalone, `thread.SetMaxExecutionSteps`, but smaller: an expression of one number does not need 25,000,000 steps.
- **The predicate's vectors are a part:** there is no mature Starlark in JavaScript. `starlark-webasm` 1.0.3 is Apache-2.0, about 5 MB of WASM, published 2022-04-11 (the npm registry, read 2026-10-27), and its go.starlark.net is older than the one `module-kit` will take.
- **Without "steps":** no module of the slice takes them, the measurement did not return a verdict by lines (the 2026-10-26 amendment to R43), and canvas-api removed the exact equivalence of steps from the product (R37 canvas-api).

— *Rejected:*
- the predicate and Starlark as a separate task after T03 `module-kit`, and the verdict vectors as one more: the author kept one task;
- the check on the item, with keys by the place of the answer slots: there would be one kind in a line, and the number of keys would need one more rule;
- a kind "text" with options and normalization for signs and words by hand — its defaults would freeze from v1, and for signs a choice by hand is enough; a separate kind "sign"; a workbook page without signs;
- open criteria of a rubric: then the kind by which the schema branches would be open too;
- assessability without a rule or only for items with a key;
- vectors only by the schema, without a second implementation; `starlark-webasm` in `tools/`;
- the predicate as a file `predicates/<id>.star` in the module layout;
- the key as a YAML number; a decimal comma and digit group separators in v0;
- "steps" in v0.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* trap values (R57). The checks `number`, `fraction` and `choice` have `trap_values`: a trap value is compared like the key, with the same normalization, and at "not yet" it names the trap. The verdict vectors name it, and `format-check` computes it; the rule `task.trap-values` is among the rules of the answer slot that `spec` checks at a vector's item. The short key in the leak check, which T29 handed to T30, is decided: a key that already stands in the text of its own item is not searched for. Step 1 of the normalization of numbers now also replaces a fraction like `½` that a number adjoins. Otherwise NFKC would make `1½` the notation `11⁄2`, eleven halves, and a mixed number would get "not yet" rather than "unreadable" (R04). The error was found by the review in the planning of T30, in the code of `format-check` on Node 24.21.

— *Amendment 2026-10-27:* placeholders in the key (R60). In the key and the trap value of `number` and `fraction` of a template, a placeholder stands in the place of the integer, the numerator or the denominator, and outside a template a placeholder in them breaks `task.placeholders`. Solver programs for the keys of templates are no longer T33 but T43: the key of a template in format v0 is computed by an expression. Template expressions are a narrow subset of the same Starlark as the predicate's, but without a step limit of their own: they have no more steps than characters.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* the template's solver (R61). A Starlark program in the format is only a template's solver, the field `template.solver`, and its limit is in the format too: 100,000,000 steps in the count of go.starlark.net for all instances of the template together. The check's predicate stays an expression no longer than 1000 characters.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* the slot checks lie in the canonical view — the server part —, and the open view does not have them (R62). — R62; RUN.md, T34.

— *Amendment 2026-10-28:* **how a reader gives a fraction written vertically and a mirrored digit: the fraction in a line, "numerator/denominator", and the mirrored digit as the digit itself.** The author's answers to the `tutor` rows «в реестр spec» В46 and В48 (RUN.md `tutor`, commit a5a78c8), their first options, by the recommendations of `tutor`. Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 15, "The value read".
- **A vertical fraction.** The notation of a fraction is only in a line, `3/4`, and a two-storey fraction in an item line will come to the format later (R51). But in a box of the workbook the learner writes a fraction vertically too. It is the same fraction, and the notation in a line is the only one the kind `fraction` takes. Without the rule one reader would write `3/4`, another "3 over 4", and the verdict would depend on the reader.
  - The measurement T80 of `tutor` (architecture 3.4 tutor, «Итог замера тетради»): with such a rule of the prompt, Opus 5.5 · `high` gets 27 readings out of 33 correct for vertical fractions and 29 out of 33 for fractions in a line. Haiku 5.5 · `low` has three times more extra "unreadable" for vertical ones — 16 out of 99 against 5 out of 99.
- **A mirrored digit.** A child who wrote 5 mirrored has solved correctly, and "not yet" for them is a false alarm. So the truth of a mirrored digit is the digit itself. "Unreadable" on it is an acceptable outcome, and the false alarm is in the target of the first slice (product 10). The rule does not concern letters: a mirrored b is a d.
  - The measurement T80 on the workbook's synthetic data, without a caption, at 32 px: mirrored boxes were read correctly in 0 out of 15 by Opus, in 8 out of 45 by Haiku · `low` and in 5 out of 45 by Haiku without thinking. False alarms on them — 8 out of 15, 9 out of 45 and 14 out of 45: the models read a mirrored 5 as 2, and a 2 as 5. On boxes without peculiarities nobody has false alarms.
  - The workbook's eval set measures mirrored digits as a separate row.
- **The module format version** does not change: the rule is about the reader, not the module, and with the same read value the verdict is the same ([format text](../format/README.md), section 2).

*Why:* the recommendations of `tutor`. The rule about letters is the executor's proposal.

*Rejected:*
- a vertical fraction as "unreadable" until the format takes a two-storey fraction, or deciding it together with that: a correct fraction would wait for a format version;
- a mirrored digit as "unreadable", and the learner rewrites it: a correct solution would get a request to rewrite;
- not measuring mirrored digits.

*Consequence:* product 10. `tutor` closes В46 and В48 by its move to a tag — RUN.md, Д47.

## Traps, techniques, solving steps and hints

**R57. The trap and technique catalogs and the solving steps are files at the root of the module: `traps.yaml`, `techniques.yaml` and `solving-steps.yaml`. A trap by a wrong value is in the slot check, and the traps that AI may suppose are named by the task. The task carries the "givens and unknown", the techniques, the solution, the leak phrases, and its item the simpler case. The fallback texts of the ladder are the trap text, the trap advice and the module's rung template from the manifest. How the leak check searches is said normatively by the [format text](../format/README.md), section 20, and its vectors are `format/vectors/leaks/`, and `spec` computes them itself.** The author's answers in the planning of T30 (RUN.md), 2026-10-27.
- **The catalogs are files at the root,** dictionaries by local ID, like the skills in the skill graph (R46):
  - the trap catalog `traps.yaml` — the description, the skills and the advice `trap_advice` of each trap;
  - the technique catalog `techniques.yaml` — the name and the description of each technique;
  - the solving steps `solving-steps.yaml` — the steps in order.

  Each of them is optional. A published trap ID names no other trap (the amendment to R46).
- **A trap by a wrong value is in the slot check,** `trap_values`: the value, the trap and, optionally, the trap text — what the learner will read at this error.
  - The value is compared by the check like the key, with the same normalization, and names the trap only when the verdict is "not yet".
  - Such traps exist for `number`, `fraction` and `choice`: a predicate has no key, and a rubric has no verdict.
  - The rule `task.trap-values`: a trap value gets "not yet", for a choice it is an option as written, and no two values of one check are equal by its comparison.
  - The verdict vectors name the matched trap, and `format-check` computes it (the amendment to R56).
- **The traps that AI supposes** by the kind of error in the work are the task's field `traps`; their provenance is "derived by AI" (concepts 9.4). Traps of both kinds come only from the catalog (`task.known-traps`).
- **The trap advice is `trap_advice`,** as the term of concepts 15 and the example of R45: what to suggest to an adult or the learner at this error. Progress shows it, and it is also the fallback text when a trap value has no text of its own. The skills of a trap are the IDs of the module's skills (`traps.known-skills`; R49).
- **The fields of a task** (the amendment to R51):
  - `givens` and `unknown` — the "givens and unknown", open;
  - `techniques` — techniques from the catalog (`task.known-techniques`), closed;
  - `solution` — texts and pictures, as in the task statement, closed. The schema requires it of a task that has an item with a verdict: a format rule is only what the schema does not express;
  - `leak_phrases` — leak phrases, closed;
  - for an item, `simpler_case`, the simpler case, closed.
- **Open** is what the learner sees before the answer and what does not suggest the method: the solving steps with exit conditions, the "givens and unknown" and the technique catalog, like the skills in the skill map. **Closed** are the task's techniques — their name suggests the method of solution, like the names of a task's skills (R51) — and also the trap catalog, the traps and texts of the task, the simpler case, the leak phrases and the solution. `api` gives a task's technique at the step that gives it, or at the learner's request, and records this.
- **A solving step** is a name `title`, `gives` — what the step gives, `givens` or `techniques`, — and an exit condition `exit_condition`: `givens_ticked`, `answer_slots_filled` or `none`. A step with `givens_ticked` gives `givens`, and the widget's state will come with stage 4.
- **Fallback texts** (concepts 10):
  - at rungs 1–2 — the text of the trap value, without it the advice of its trap, and without that the rung template;
  - at the third rung — the item's simpler case, and without it the same as at the second.

  The rung templates belong to the module: two different texts `rung_templates` in the manifest, in the explanation language. A module with an item with a verdict cannot do without them (`manifest.rung-templates`).
- **О-21 as far as the format goes:** before the first submission a request gives the "givens and unknown" and the task's technique — without AI and without reading the work. There is no sketch "how to start" in v0: it will come as a minor version when `canvas` learns to draw it. The rest of О-21 — what a request gives after a wrong answer and "explain differently" — is decided by the detailing of `api`, and О-21 stays open.
- **The leak check** — normatively, the [format text](../format/README.md), section 20:
  - searched for are the keys `number`, `fraction` and `choice` of all items of the task and all its leak phrases;
  - a key that itself is found in the text of the task statement and in the `alt` of its pictures, in the text and line of its own item and in the options of its answer slots `choice` is not searched for: the leak phrases hold it. So the key of a tapped choice is never searched for. So the short key that T29 handed to T30 is decided (the amendment to R56);
  - the normal form is step 1 of the normalization of numbers and the normalization of a choice ([format text](../format/README.md), section 15); the letters of a word are the categories L, M and N;
  - a string is found whole, with a boundary where its edge is a letter of a word; a number by value and by absolute value;
  - numbers in words and notations that the check does not read as a number are caught only by leak phrases;
  - the rule `task.no-leaks` checks the author's texts that the learner sees before solving.
- **Leak vectors** — `format/vectors/leaks/<case>.yaml` by the schema `leak-vector.schema.json`, the fourth schema without a part. `format-check` computes them with a second implementation, `leaks.mjs`, and CI of `module-kit` passes the same vectors (the amendment to R45).
- **Step 1 of normalization** also replaces a fraction like `½` that a number adjoins: otherwise NFKC makes `1½` the notation `11⁄2`, and the learner would get a false "not yet" (the amendment to R56).

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), sections 10, 11 and 14–20.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T30 — eight, all by the plan's recommendations (RUN.md, T30, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **Traps follow standalone:** "The catalog stays closed for the same reason the topic catalog does: `trap_hit` is what makes a wrong answer a diagnosis, and free-form trap names cannot be counted" and "Each trap carries its advice" (SPEC 1.3 standalone, commit 99d8a65, read 2026-10-27). The differences: a task's trap is found by the value, not by the letter of an option, and a trap has skills, as concepts 7 requires.
- **A trap by value and the fallback texts follow canvas-api** (commit 0901af0, read 2026-10-27): the task has `traps: {"6": "…"}`, and «Ответ совпадает с ловушкой по тем же правилам» (spec 8.6 and 5.3 canvas-api); «на ступенях 1–2 — текст ловушки, который автор задачи написал для этого неверного ответа, а если такого нет — шаблон ступени; на ступени 3 — случай попроще от автора задачи» (R24 canvas-api). The difference is that the rung template belongs to the module, not the service: a module has one explanation language (R46), and the platform does not need to translate templates into the language of each module.
- **A key from the text of its own item is not searched for** — this is a departure from R24 canvas-api, where «Ключ запрещён всегда — даже если это слово есть в самом условии». Because of this rule R40 canvas-api removed a task in which the leak check «пришлось бы запрещать «no», «never», «cannot»», and `tutor` keeps open how not to take for a leak «законную цифру ключа — «2 ноги»» (RUN.md `tutor`, T75, commit 8451728). standalone did not count as giving away what is said in the task statement either (SPEC 5.4 standalone).
- **Numbers in words are leak phrases,** not tables of the platform. canvas-api translated "seven" into 7, but such a table is needed for each language, and modules are written in any. In the measurement bank of `tutor` the leak phrases are «сверх самого ключа» (architecture 3.1 tutor, commit 8451728).
- **What is open follows the prototype:** "Understand: tap what we know and what we need to find", "Plan: a technique card" ([draft/README.md](../draft/README.md)). standalone's hint "arrives with the task and is revealed locally, and the fact that it was opened travels with the answer" (SPEC 8.3 standalone). A technique, though, is closed, like a task's skills (R51), and `api` gives it.
- **The solution is by the schema:** a format rule is what the schema does not express ([format text](../format/README.md), section 7; concepts 15), and "has an item with a verdict" the schema expresses by open fields.
- **`gives` of a step:** physics has no step "plan" (concepts 7), so the step itself says what it gives.

- T30 as two or three tasks: the author kept one;
- catalogs as folders, a file per trap, and one file of all catalogs;

## Lessons

**R58. A lesson is a file `lessons/<id>.yaml`: the module's skills it teaches, and segments in the author's order — explanations, worked examples and the module's tasks by ID. The demo is parts of a worked example on the handwriting sheet. The order of lessons is set by the skill graph, and О-19 is decided: there is no separate field of order.**
- **The lesson's skills** are `skills`, the module's skills by local ID (`lesson.known-skills`). They are closed, like a task's skills (R51): the app needs only the lesson's title, and the engine reads the skills. Each task of the lesson trains at least one of them as primary — its item's skill or, without one, the task's skill (`lesson.task-skills`).
- **The lesson's segments** are `segments`, in order and without repeats. A segment is an object with exactly one field:
  - `explanation` — an explanation, paragraphs and pictures, like the parts of a task statement;
  - `worked_example` — a worked example;
  - `task` — a task of the module by its ID (`lesson.known-tasks`). The next segment comes when the task has ended.

  There is no special check segment at the end: the check is the last tasks of the lesson, and the format does not mark them.
- **A worked example** is not a task: no answer slots, no key, and it does not serve as evidence.
  - It has a task statement, a handwriting sheet and `demo` — the demo: parts of the example's solution, which the learner opens one at a time and can hide all at once. A part is a paragraph, a picture beside the sheet or a picture on a sheet area.
  - The area `area` is a rectangle of the sheet in its units, like a zone, and it lies on the sheet (`lesson.areas`). A picture on an area stands on the layer of the demo, at the size of the area (concepts 8).
  - A worked example has no workbook in v0. The learner does not write on the example's sheet: there is no work of the learner there.
  - The example is open: R05 guards the key and the solution of a task, and an example is not a task. So its parts are `demo`, not `solution`: a task's solution is never opened ([format text](../format/README.md), section 6).
- **The order of lessons follows the skill graph** (О-19).
  - Lesson A comes after lesson B when a skill of A needs, through the module's prerequisites, a skill of B that is not among the skills of A. Anchor skills give no order.
  - A graph without cycles does not guarantee an order without a cycle: a lesson [a, c] and a lesson [b], where b requires a and c requires b, each come after the other. Hence the rule `lesson.order`.
  - Where the graph gives no order — two lessons of one skill, skills without a link — the engine's rule chooses.
  - For a sequential module the graph is a chain, and the app infers the mark "sequential" from the graph.
- **Adaptation.** The segments go in the author's order, and the engine does not reorder them.
  - In a lesson whose skills are not all with a verdict, the engine adds nothing and skips nothing: the lesson goes in the author's order, without adaptation (concepts 4, 5). So "the skills of essays with a rubric go in the author's order" of the record of T22 at table 1 of RUN.md: in the order of the graph and of the lesson.
  - Whether the engine adds consolidation to a lesson whose skills are all with a verdict, and whether it ends it early, is decided by the detailing of `engine`.
- **Age** is the lesson's `age_categories`, as for a task, closed. A lesson is given only to a learner whom both the lesson and each of its tasks suit. Otherwise a task only for adults (П-20) would reach a child in a lesson where nothing is skipped. The rule `lesson.age-categories`: the lesson's categories are from the manifest, and at least one category suits both the lesson and each of its tasks: a lesson that no learner will get is an error.
- **Open** are `id`, `title` and the segments with all their fields: the app runs the lesson. **Closed** are the skills and the age categories.
- **The leak check in a lesson** is the rule `lesson.no-leaks`: neither the lesson's title, nor its explanations, nor the task statement and demo of its examples contain the keys and leak phrases of its tasks ([format text](../format/README.md), section 20). All texts are searched, after the task too: the open view of a lesson goes to the device whole, and the key does not go there before solving (R05). So the author decided by a finding of the review, instead of searching only before the task's segment. `format-check` computes the rule itself, like `task.no-leaks` (the amendments to R45 and R57).
- **The lesson's pictures** are files of the module (`lesson.known-pictures`).
- **Common definitions.** The parts of a task statement, the canvas and the rectangle of a sheet moved to `common.schema.json`, so that the lesson does not refer to the task's schema (the amendment to R51).

Normative: the [format text](../format/README.md), section 21, and edits of sections 6, 9, 10, 12, 14 and 20.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-10-27 in the planning of T31 — six, all by the plan's recommendations, and a seventh by a finding of the review, about the leak check in a lesson (RUN.md, T31, «Решено автором»). The rest here is the plan's proposal, which the author approved.
- **The order through the graph** is the recommendation of О-19 (product 13): "A sequential module's graph is a chain, and the engine goes along it as along any graph", and "the next lesson is still chosen by the engine" (R03).
  - In the prototype the mark *Sequential* cannot move the package: "Next in a sequential module" is only a line (`draft/NovaTrail Widget.html`, commit 4846d00, read 2026-10-27).
  - In standalone the author does not set the order either: "those never handed out come first, in catalog order", and "Nor does the rule read the links between topics" (SPEC 3.1 and 3.2 standalone, commit 4dece74, read 2026-10-27).
  - The difference is that here the rule reads the graph, as concepts 12 requires.
- **A worked example on the sheet** follows the demo layer of concepts 8 and `canvas`: it has the layer `show`, «HTML и SVG; в первом коде пуст», and HTML on the sheet is «блок 1000 × 1400 единиц с матрицей» (architecture `canvas`, commit f162153, read 2026-10-27). A picture on a sheet area is what this layer will draw without a new format of strokes.
  - Closest to a lesson in MathTrail is the topic page of standalone's site: "how such tasks are solved: the steps of the move, then examples worked through to their answers" (SPEC 8.12.2 standalone, R172 standalone). Its examples are `examples[]` with `question`, `steps` and `answer` in `site/content/en/topics/gaps-and-boundaries.yaml`.
- **The lesson's skills are closed** — by the same argument as a task's skills in R51: the name of a skill suggests the method of solving the lesson's tasks.
- **A segment is one field with `minProperties` and `maxProperties`,** not `oneOf`. In ajv 8.20.0 a `oneOf` of three `required` gives four errors for one breakage, and an invalid example names one ([format text](../format/README.md), section 8). В25 — `$ref` beside `oneOf` — is still open.
- **Names.** «Шаг» (step) is already taken by the solving step, «решение» (solution) is closed, «разбор» is the short name of the review of the course of solution (R55), and «место» and «область» are the place of a schema, a place on the canvas (R53) and the area of an item (concepts 6). Hence «звено урока | segment», «показ автора | demo» and «участок листа | area».

— *Rejected:*
- a mark "sequential" in the manifest with a list of lessons; a lesson that names the lesson before it as the default path;
- a lesson without a rule about the skills of its tasks; the lesson's skills inferred from its tasks — then there is no lesson without tasks, like a lesson of reading sample essays;
- a worked example outside the canvas, with the demo layer as a minor version; the demo over a lesson's task too;
- a check segment at the end, without hints and with the solution after the whole check;
- a lesson in which the engine never adds or skips anything, and consolidation with an early end, allowed by the format itself;
- the leak check in a lesson's text only as SHOULD advice, and only before the task's segment: the text after the task is already on the device;
- a segment through `oneOf`; a reference of the lesson's schema to the task's schema; a field `solution` of an example; the names `place`, `working` and `steps`.
