## Interface icons

**R78. The icons of the UI packages are one set of the Iconify catalog, Material Symbols, in the style Rounded: outlined, and what is selected — filled. Each UI package takes the set's package `@iconify-json/material-symbols` itself, by exact version, and builds in at build time only its own icons: the device does not call the Iconify API. Which icon has which value is said by the table of architecture 6.** The author's answers in planning T47 (RUN.md), 2026-11-02.
- **The set** — Material Symbols, the prefix `material-symbols`, the author Google, the license Apache-2.0 from the list of R12. The set is one, without a fallback. A button for a value that the set lacks holds by its caption alone until an amendment to this entry names an icon; a second set also comes only by an amendment. So it is now with the protractor (architecture 1 canvas): it is in none of the four candidates of T47.
- **The style** — Rounded. A button's icon is the outline, `<base>-outline-rounded`. The selected option of a choice — "Pen" or "Eraser" — and a mode turned on are the same icon with a fill, `<base>-rounded`. The fill does not replace the state: a screen reader is still told it by ARIA — `aria-checked` on "Pen" and "Eraser", `aria-expanded` on "Demo" (R36; R42 canvas). For line icons — arrows, "Undo" — the outline and the fill are the same.
- **How the icons get into the build:**
  - the set's package `@iconify-json/material-symbols` a UI package takes by exact version. In a package that comes out in npm — `canvas` and `skill-map` — it stands in `devDependencies`: the consumer does not need the set's data, since the icons are already built in. In `app` — where the answer to Т-36 says. Dependabot and the license check see the set as any dependency;
  - each package raises its version of the set itself, and a new version may draw an icon differently. So that one value looks the same on one screen, `app` keeps the same version of the set as the versions of `canvas` and `skill-map` in its lock file have; how it compares this is decided by its T01 (RUN.md, Д61);
  - the build builds in only the icons that the package takes. By what — the package decides: by a plugin of its bundler, for example unplugin-icons, or by a script on `@iconify/utils` if there is no bundler, as with `canvas`, which only `tsc` builds (R12 canvas). The package does not turn on unplugin-icons' auto-install of sets, `autoInstall`: the set comes from the lock file, not by an import;
  - at run time — not one request to `api.iconify.design` or to another Iconify API. Iconify's components that go there for icons — `@iconify/react`, `iconify-icon` and the like — the packages do not take.
- **The license.** The check of the lock file by `spec`'s list (R39) reads the license of the set's package — `Apache-2.0`, from the list. The set's icons go into the build even when the set's package stands in `devDependencies`. So no exception is written for it in `licenses-check-repo`, not even under `dev`: the boundary `dev` of the 2026-10-22 amendment to R39 is for tools that never ship anywhere (R12). If a new version of the set changes the license to one not from the list, the check will reject it, while an exception under `dev` the check would let through: this rule is held by review, not by code. What is built in from `devDependencies` in general is decided by Т-36.
- **The notice:**
  - Apache-2.0 requires giving the recipient a copy of the license: "You must give any other recipients of the Work or Derivative Works a copy of this License" ([the set's LICENSE](https://github.com/google/material-design-icons/blob/10ecc14/LICENSE), section 4(a)), as in R46. It is carried by the `LICENSE` of the NovaTrail package itself: it is the same text of Apache-2.0 (R20). The set has no `NOTICE` file, so there are no notices from it to carry, and there is no copyright line of Google in the license text either;
  - beyond that, the package names the set in its `NOTICE`: Material Symbols, Google, Apache-2.0, the address `google/material-design-icons` and the version of the set's package. The packages `@iconify-json/*` have neither `LICENSE` nor `NOTICE`, and without this line one cannot learn from the build where the icons come from. `NOTICE` goes into the package's npm archive, and in `app` into its build, together with the notices of everything else built into it.
- **Accessibility:**
  - an icon's SVG is with `aria-hidden="true"` and without `<title>`. The button's name is the caption from the package's table of captions (R36): if the caption beside the icon is visible, it is the button's text; if only the icon is visible, the caption goes into `aria-label`;
  - an icon's color is `currentColor`: in forced colors mode it takes the system color of the button (R36);
  - whether the caption beside an icon is visible is decided by the accessibility standard of T07 of `app` (О-24), and the translations of captions go by its shared scheme (О-2). Until then a button's caption is visible.
- **The table of values** — architecture 6:
  - one value is one icon, and one icon is one value, like a term in concepts 15. Buttons with one value in different packages look the same, and an icon from the table does not stand on a button with another value;
  - the first rows are the buttons of the row of `canvas` (`src/element/labels.ts` of `canvas`, `main` e90e210): the task screen of `app` shows them. "Next" will be taken by the lesson player of `app` too (R42 canvas);
  - a value that a second package needs enters the table as a row «в реестр spec» (RULES.md, Across repositories). An icon for a value that only it has a package chooses from the set itself — not from those in the table — and records it in its `docs/architecture.md`. If it already stands at another package for another value, both values enter the table by the same route;
  - an icon whose direction goes along the line — "Next", "Undo", the hidden "Demo" — is mirrored in a right-to-left line. Which icons are so, the table says.
- **What the entry does not concern:** the pictures of content — these are the module's media files, and their rule is the module format; the icons of widgets — a widget is foreign code in the iframe sandbox (architecture 3.4).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-02 in planning T47: the set and the style — by their look in the catalog, the rest — by the plan's recommendations. The line in `NOTICE`, the visible caption until the standard of T07 of `app`, and the rule of direction are the plan's proposal, which the author approved. All read 2026-11-02.
- **The author's request of 2026-10-28.** The set is shared: otherwise one button would look different in `app` and in the canvas, and each package would decide the license and the way of delivery itself.
- **No requests at run time.** "Iconify icon components do not bundle icon data. They load only data for icons used on currently viewed page at run time", "Component requests data for icons from Iconify API", and among the drawbacks — "Requires access to Iconify API, making it unusable for offline applications" ([Iconify, Icons on Demand](https://iconify.design/docs/icon-components/)). A request from the learner's device would give its IP address to a third party that is not in architecture 3.12, and an IP address is personal information under COPPA ([16 CFR 312.2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/16/312.2); privacy 10). The UI packages themselves are not loaded at run time either (R16).
- **Building in without the network.** "Not using any frameworks, but want to automate the build process? Iconify Utils offers easy to use functions that generate SVG", and "All icons in Iconify packages pass very strict validation, so they do not contain any potentially harmful content, such as scripts and external resources" ([Iconify, SVG](https://iconify.design/docs/usage/svg/)). unplugin-icons has "On-demand - Only bundle the icons you really use, while having all the options", and the auto-install is "Option C: Auto Install (Experimental)", by default `autoInstall: false` ([README](https://github.com/unplugin/unplugin-icons/blob/v24.0.0/README.md), tag v24.0.0). The licenses of unplugin-icons 24.0.0 and `@iconify/utils` 3.1.7 are MIT (the npm registry).
- **The set and its license.** `@iconify-json/material-symbols` 1.2.97 of 2026-10-28 has `license` — `Apache-2.0`, and `info.json` names 15,761 icons, the author — Google — and the license. There are nine files in the package, and neither `LICENSE` nor `NOTICE` is among them (the npm registry and jsDelivr). `google/material-design-icons`, commit 10ecc14, has at its root a `LICENSE` with Apache-2.0 and no `NOTICE`, and the README says: "We have made these icons available for you to incorporate into your products under the Apache License Version 2.0" and "We'd love attribution in your app's *about* screen, but it's not required".
- **Coverage.** The set has icons for the canvas tools (architecture 1 canvas) — the pen `ink-pen`, the eraser `ink-eraser`, the ruler `straighten`, the calculator `calculate`, the keyboard `keyboard`, the microphone `mic` — and for all the buttons of the row of `canvas`, each in all six styles. A protractor is in no candidate — neither in Material Symbols nor in Lucide, Tabler and Phosphor. The catalog's search finds this tool only in small sets: iconoven, iconmind, matita and energy-icons (`api.iconify.design/search?query=protractor`).
- **Each package — itself.** The set's package gives data, not code, and a copy of its own in each package ties nothing. A shared package of icons would require a new repository, and a new icon its release and the consumers' move to a version. The table in `spec` gives the same unity without this.
- **The set's package, not copies of SVG.** Its version is raised by Dependabot, and its license compared by the check of the lock file; neither of them sees copies of SVG.

— *Rejected:*
- Lucide (ISC), Tabler (MIT) and Phosphor (MIT) — the other candidates of T47; the choice is by look;
- the styles Outlined and Sharp; always the outline; always the fill;
- a main set with a fallback;
- Iconify's components and its API at run time, including an instance of the API of our own;
- SVG copied into the package's repository together with the set's license;
- a shared package `@altnovatrail/icons` — a new repository, an amendment to R18 and a release of its own;
- an export `./icons` in `@altnovatrail/spec`: the package would stop carrying declarations alone (R73), and a new icon would wait for a release of `spec` and for the packages' move to a tag;
- only the set and the rules, without the table of values: the packages would draw one button with different icons;
- a guard in the code of `licenses-check-repo` that would reject an exception for `@iconify-json/*`: it would close one set of icons, and the general case would stay without a record. It is now Т-36.

— *Consequence:*
- architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.12 and 6; concepts 15 — "icon" and "icon set"; repositories 8 — Т-36;
- RUN.md — T47 and Д61. `canvas` by its move to a tag puts icons on the buttons of the row and revisits the "badges" in R28 and R33 canvas, `app` chooses in T01 what to build icons in with, and `skill-map` takes the set with its first code.

## The template's kind `typescript`

**R79. The template's kind `typescript` carries a stage with a browser for tests and the Biome extension. A copy of this kind gets, at the end of the stage `toolchain`, Chrome Headless Shell from the Playwright image by tag and digest and its system libraries from a snapshot of Ubuntu, and in VS Code the extension `biomejs.biome` and Biome as the default TypeScript formatter.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В4 (RUN.md of `app`, commit 0849269), by its recommendation. Д17 is closed.
- **How it is built:**
  - a kind in `repo-template/kinds.json` is an object with three keys: `extensions` — VS Code extensions, `settings` — VS Code settings, `toolchain` — a file in `repo-template/kinds/` whose lines go at the end of the stage `toolchain` of the Dockerfile, before the heading of the stage `devcontainer` and its `FROM`. The recipe stops at a key it does not know, at a value of the wrong type, at a file outside `kinds/`, at a setting that `spec`'s devcontainer already has, and at a place in `spec`'s devcontainer that it did not find exactly once (repositories 2.2). A kind written as a list of extensions, as before this entry, the recipe still reads: `just new-repo` builds a copy from the template of the latest tag, and at `v0.6.2` the kind is still a list;
  - the kind `typescript` has `biomejs.biome@3.8.1`, the setting `"[typescript]": { "editor.defaultFormatter": "biomejs.biome" }` and the file `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile`. The kinds `go` and `docs` have no stage, and `go` still has the Go extension;
  - the file's lines are the same as R13 canvas on `main` of `canvas` e90e210: Chrome Headless Shell of revision 1248 from `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.64.1-noble` by digest `sha256:7852dc5a7d72f5fe458a597d690f6c42fbc8e9e26ddfa95f8e6ef552558d9bbf`, `ENV PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/ms-playwright`, 24 `apt` packages — Chromium's libraries for Ubuntu 24.04 and fonts — from the snapshot `20261021T000000Z` (R40). The image's version is the same as `playwright` in `canvas` and in the plan of `app`: 1.64.1 (architecture 3.1 app). The stage of a copy of the kind `typescript` matches the stage of `canvas` line for line, and only the comments differ;
  - the decisions the file cites are `spec`'s decisions, and the recipe adds the suffix to them, as to the whole Dockerfile: `(R79 spec)`, `(R40 spec)`.
- **Who raises the versions.** `spec` raises the image, the revision and the snapshot in the template, and a copy gets them by its move to a tag. Dependabot does not see them: the image stands in `COPY --from`, not in a `FROM` line (R13 canvas). A repository that needs a new `playwright` sooner raises all three in its Dockerfile — in the pull request that raises the package, as R13 canvas does — and writes a row «в реестр spec». Until its move to a tag with the new template, its Dockerfile is no longer the recipe's output, and its decision names this.
- **The browser's terms.** Chrome Headless Shell is a build of Google Chrome for Testing under Google's free terms. This entry is the decision that brings it into a copy of the kind `typescript`, and so names it an exception within the two bounds of R12: NovaTrail does not distribute the browser — the stage `toolchain` is built on each run and is published nowhere — and the platform is built, run and deployed without it. A repository of the kind `typescript` names it, citing this entry (Д16).
- **The default formatter** is the executor's proposal. The formatter setting exists in `canvas` and in the plan of `app` ("the stage `devcontainer` — the extension `biomejs.biome` and the default TypeScript formatter", architecture 3.1 app). Without it in the template, each repository would again add it by hand.

— *Why:* the author's answer of 2026-11-02, by the recommendation of `app` in В4. Д17 said to return "when a second repository on TypeScript takes up tests in the browser". `app` is the second: its screens with the element `<novatrail-canvas>` run in Chromium (R03 app), and the canvas element does not work in DOM emulators. Without a shared stage the same lines — the image, the revision, 24 `apt` packages and the snapshot — would live in two copies, and each move to a tag would carry the recipe's edits into the Dockerfile by hand: in `canvas` it is already so (R13 canvas). Biome was chosen by both repositories on TypeScript that have a decision on the linter: `canvas` (R12 canvas) and `app` (R03 app). The extension's version is the latest stable, 3.8.1 of 2026-10-24: `canvas` has 3.7.1, and `app` in its plan 3.8.1. Later versions in the gallery are pre-releases, with numbers of the form `2026.10.241124` (the VS Code Marketplace gallery API, `extensionquery` for `biomejs.biome`, read 2026-11-02). The image's digest was compared with the registry 2026-11-02: `https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/playwright/manifests/sha256:7852dc5a…` answers with an image index. Microsoft has since re-published the tag `v1.64.1-noble` itself, and it now points to the index `sha256:2f05f8a7…`. The template takes the digest of `canvas`: its CI has already built this stage.

— *Cost:* the stage with the browser also goes to a copy that does not test in a browser. The step "Toolchain image" of `canvas` took 57–67 seconds in each of five jobs, and without the browser 18 (R13 canvas). All the required checks of such a copy also depend on MCR and on `snapshot.ubuntu.com`. `skill-map` gets Biome before its decision on the linter, as Д17 warned. If it chooses another linter, its decision will remove the extension and the setting and name this a difference from the recipe.

— *Rejected:*
- each repository keeps its own copy of the stage, like `canvas` (option (b) of В4): two copies and two raises by hand;
- only the Biome extension, and the stage when a third repository takes up the browser (option (c) of В4): Д17 waited for the second;
- a shared image with the browser for all repositories: it would have to be published, and NovaTrail does not publish an image with Chrome for Testing (R12; Д17);
- the image by the new digest of the tag `v1.64.1-noble`: a copy's stage would diverge from the stage of `canvas` that its CI built, while the Playwright version and the browser's revision are the same in both indexes.

— *Consequence:*
- `repo-template/kinds.json`, `repo-template/kinds/typescript.Dockerfile` and the recipe `new-repo` — `tools/new-repo/devcontainer.mjs`, its functions `readKind` and `editDevcontainer`, with tests in `just new-repo-test`; repositories 2.2, the template's README and the list of what is raised by hand, in `.github/dependabot.yml`;
- `canvas` and `app` take the stage from the recipe by their move to a tag, and the Dockerfile of `canvas` becomes the recipe's output again: R13 canvas then says that the lines came from the template. `skill-map` gets the stage and Biome by the same route, at its move to a tag (RUN.md, Д63).

## The learner model on the server

**R80. The learner model lives in the platform's database — the database of `api`. What is stored is an append-only log of evidence, and it is the source of truth, while the skills' state is a cache marked with the version of `learner-model` and the release of `modules`. The engine choice also stores the release of `modules` and the number of the log's last evidence by which it was made. П-7 and Т-22 are closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В4 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` d563af3), by its recommendation: to close both questions now. What `api` decided is R06 api, the details are architecture 3.2 api.
- **Where the model lives** — in the database of `api` (П-7). Several devices and several learners of the account and a subscription work with it, and the engine computes on the server, as Т-10 recommends. The export is in an open format (R09); its format is decided by epic E4 (R76).
- **What is stored** (Т-22):
  - evidence — one per finished attempt (concepts 11); an attempt of a task with a rubric gives none in the first slice (О-17). What is in it and how much it weighs is decided by `learner-model` (architecture 3.8), and `api` stores it as it is;
  - the log is only appended to. The recomputation cuts off evidence on a version that the index marked `wrong_key` (R63), and the rows remain. The log is deleted only whole — with the profile or by the time limit (П-9);
  - the skills' state is a cache marked with the version of `learner-model` and the release of `modules`. It is recomputed from the log when one of them changes or a version is withdrawn because of `wrong_key`. New evidence is appended to the cache without recomputing the whole log.
- **The condition for `learner-model`** is one: the state appended by new evidence matches the one recomputed from the log. If it does not match, the cache is recomputed whole. If T04 of `learner-model` decides otherwise, Т-22 returns.
- **The engine choice** stores what architecture 1 names, and also the release of `modules` and the number of the log's last evidence. Without them a repetition from the log does not know which prefix of the log to take and which withdrawal marks were in force then.

— *Why:* the author's answer by the recommendation of `api`; the recommendations of П-7 and Т-22 are the same. A change of algorithm recomputes the state from the log rather than carrying over the old one. The engine choice is repeated from the log (architecture 1), and by it too the model is recomputed without the evidence of `wrong_key` (R63). The cache is needed so that the engine choice after each attempt does not recompute the whole log.

— *Rejected:*
- a family's file — for example, in Google Drive, as in standalone. There the file was the truth, but writes went without a condition — "Whoever uploads last wins, silently" — and an emptied Drive trash erased a profile without a copy (`05-storage.md` of standalone, by architecture 4 api);
- the device: the engine computes on the server (Т-10), and each device would have a model of its own;
- closing only П-7, and Т-22 after T04 of `learner-model`: the condition for `learner-model` is one, and with another decision of T04 the question returns anyway.

— privacy 4, 9; architecture 1; repositories 8; RUN.md, Д67; R06 api.

To the appending condition of T04 of `learner-model` the conditions of the transfer are added (architecture 3.8):
- a module's skill that is neither in `skills` nor in `retired_skills` of the current version goes to no skill, without an error;
- an anchor skill `core.<name>` goes as it is if the vocabulary of some format version in the window of `api` knows it, and otherwise to no skill; the trap's skills, if the evidence carries them, go by the same rules;

## The inbox of `spec`

**R81. The session of `spec` finds the rows «в реестр spec» of the other repositories itself: before each task the recipe `just inbox` reads on GitHub the tables 3 of their RUN.md and compares them with table 5 of the RUN.md of `spec` — which rows are already recorded and where. A row counts as arrived when it is on `main` of its repository, while the rows of open pull requests are "on the way", and they are recorded only on the author's word. There is no new channel, and the author no longer carries rows.** The author's decision of 2026-11-02 in planning T66 (RUN.md), both answers by the plan's recommendations.
- **How it works.**
  - A repository's session writes a row as it did — into table 3 of its RUN.md — and its question opens with the mark «В реестр spec» (RULES.md, Across repositories). The recipe recognizes the mark regardless of case and only at the start of the question: the same words further in the text are not the mark.
  - `just inbox` reads through `gh` the RUN.md of each repository from `tools/release/repositories.mjs` except `spec`: on the commit of `main` and in each open pull request. It prints three lists: new rows on `main`; "on the way" — rows that a pull request adds to its base; rows of table 5 that the source no longer carries — they may leave it.
  - The session of `spec` triages the new rows before the task by rule 13 of RUN.md: what the author has already decided it records, and the rest it brings to the author with options and a recommendation. A recorded row goes into table 5.
  - The answer reaches the repository, as before, with its move to a tag (the «Д» rows of table 4).
  - What is not a question needs no route of its own: what a repository took by a move to a tag is seen by its submodule (rule 3 of COORDINATION.md), and its tasks by its RUN.md.
- **The first run**, 2026-11-02. 12 repositories were read: 40 rows on `main`, 0 on the way. 29 of them had been recorded, and they went into table 5 — by the «Д» rows and the start of table 3. There were 11 new: `api` В6–В9, `app` В11–В16, `canvas` В58. While the task ran, one more came to `main` of `.github`, В35, and the next run found it. The errors of the trials that the recipe no longer makes:
  - without the condition "at the start of the question" it took the row `module-kit` В1 — a question about the order of its tasks, where «в реестр spec» stands in the recommendation;
  - without comparison with the pull request's base — 38 rows from old branches of Dependabot, recorded long ago. The base is the common ancestor of the branch with `main`, not the pull request's `base.sha`: otherwise an old branch would bring back rows that `main` has closed since;
  - a row recorded from a pull request on the author's word it does not name as gone while the pull request is open; a failure of one repository or pull request does not stop the run, and it reads the lists page by page.

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-02 in planning T66. The rows already lie in the tables 3 of the other repositories (RULES.md, Across repositories), and the coordinator already reads their RUN.md on GitHub (R76): all that was missing was that the session of `spec` read them itself. Nothing changes for the other repositories — neither rule 4 nor the order of their move to a tag — and the recipe works at once, on any tag of theirs. The record is one, in the repository's file, as the rule "Project context lives in the repository's files" requires. A row on `main` the author has already reviewed, while before the merge it may change, so the rows of pull requests are only "on the way".

— *Rejected:*
- issues in `spec` that the sessions of other repositories open: the rule would reach them only with a move to a tag, the row's text would live in two places, rule 4 would need an exception, and issues are public. The inbox would be only the issues of the author's account, and the author's answer by that account cannot be told apart from a session's record;
- Discussions in `spec`: the same, and the `gh` commands for them in version 2.101 are in preview, and a pull request does not close a discussion;
- messages between sessions of Claude Code: two sessions are needed at once, a message is not kept and does not get into files, and an exchange between different devcontainers is not verified. On 2026-11-02 `ListAgents` did not see other sessions;
- an inbox file in `spec` that the other repositories add to by pull requests: a session would change `spec` not from within it (RULES.md, Across repositories);
- only `main`, without the rows of pull requests: the author would wait for the merge where the answer can be prepared earlier, as with the `.github` rows В32 and В33 (Д64);
- `main` and pull requests on an equal footing: a row recorded from a branch could diverge from the one that gets merged.

— *Consequence:* `tools/inbox/` and the recipes `just inbox` and `just inbox-test`; rule 13 and table 5 of RUN.md; rule 3 of COORDINATION.md; RULES.md, Across repositories; the template of RUN.md, `repo-template/files/RUN.md`; CLAUDE.md, Environment; repositories 5. The edit of RULES.md reaches the other repositories with their move to a tag, but the recipe does not wait for it.

— RUN.md, T66; R19, R76.

— *Amendment 2026-11-04:* **table 5 keeps a fingerprint of the rows it names, and `just inbox` also prints the rows of table 5 whose rows on `main` of the source have changed since.** The author's answer of 2026-11-04 to the question В28 of RUN.md, by its recommendation. The recipe compared rows only by their numbers and did not see additions to recorded ones: so the addenda of T12 and T13 of `api` to its В3, В4, В11 and В14 and the edit of `modules` В3 in its T08 went through, and only the third inbox triage of 2026-11-02 found them, by reading the rows whole.
- **The fingerprint** is the first 12 hexadecimal digits of the SHA-256 of the rows of the source's table 3 in the order of their numbers: a row's cells, each with its whitespace collapsed, joined by " | ", and the rows joined by a line break (`fingerprintOf` in `tools/inbox/inbox.mjs`). An edit of any word of a row — the question, the options, the recommendation — changes it, while the row's place in the file and Markdown marks do not. The fingerprint is one per row of table 5, not per number: a row of table 5 names several rows of the source, and the column stays short.
- **What the recipe prints** — a row of table 5 at least one of whose rows is on `main` while their fingerprint is not the one recorded, or is not recorded at all, "—", — with the new fingerprint and the place of the rows at the source. The session rereads them, records what was added as a new row, and puts the fingerprint into table 5 (rule 13 of RUN.md). When some of the rows have left the source, the fingerprint of the remaining ones is different too, and the recipe names the row both among the changed and among the gone. A changed row is not an error, and the recipe ends with code 0; a fingerprint that is not 12 hexadecimal digits is an error of table 5, like an unread row. The rows "on the way" have no fingerprint: they go into table 5 only on the author's word.
- **The first fingerprints** were taken 2026-11-04 from `main` of the sources. Since the commits at which `spec` recorded the rows, `api` В15, В16 and В18, `module-kit` В15, and `modules` В3 and В12 have changed, and the same day they were compared: there are no new requests to `spec` in them.

— *Rejected:* a rule in RULES.md and in the template of RUN.md that an addition to a recorded row goes as a new row with its own number — it would be held by hand in twelve repositories, while the recipe sees the edit itself; changing nothing — the triage would reread each recorded row whole at each run.

— *Consequence:* `tools/inbox/` and its tests; rule 13, «Как устроен план» and table 5 of RUN.md; CLAUDE.md, Environment.

It reads the working tree, not GitHub.** The author's decision of 2026-11-12 in planning T126: the recipe runs before every task anyway. — *Consequence:* `tools/inbox/due.mjs`, `main.mjs` and tests; rule 13 of RUN.md. — R145; RUN.md, T126.

## Showing the solution and a hint on request

**R82. On a task of a module the solution is shown by a button: to a learner of the category `adult` from the start of the attempt, to a child from the fourth wrong answer, once the hint ladder is passed, and with the adult's setting "ask before showing", on by default, by an adult action; showing closes the attempt with the outcome "solution shown". A task from paper never shows its solution. "Hint" before the first wrong answer gives "givens and unknown", the task's technique and its leading question, and on a task from paper the tutor's opening question by AI; after it the words of the current rung once more, without AI; "explain differently" gives the same rung in other words, one AI call per rung, without the work. An attempt left or abandoned with wrong answers has the outcome "left unfinished". О-7 and О-21 are closed.** The author's answers to the rows «в реестр spec» of `api`, `learner-model`, `engine` and `modules`, by their recommendations, and for a task from paper the author's decisions of epic E11 (R162) and of 2026-11-20 in the planning of T230: the opening question by AI from the task's crop, and the cascade of R164 for every call of the words. What `api` decided is R09 and R10 api, the details architecture 3.5 api.
- **The ladder** (concepts 10):
  - a wrong answer is a submission in which at least one answer slot got "not yet". "Unreadable" and "unchecked" give no rung: they are not the learner's mistake (R04);
  - the k-th wrong answer gives rung k while k is at most three, whether the tutor's panel is open or not (R148). From the fourth there is no new rung and no AI call for a rung's words: the words of rung 3 stay, and Hint and "explain differently" work as below. To a child the program offers to call an adult, or to show the solution of a task of a module; to an adult learner, to show the solution of a task of a module, and on a task from paper nothing more. "Call an adult" is the interface of `app`: `api` notifies no one (architecture 7). Whether a child who solves with the panel closed has passed the ladder is О-26;
  - the rung's answer slot is the first "not yet" slot in order in the submission that gave the rung — items by place, slots by order in the item —, chosen by the program (R03); the rung's words, "explain differently" and the fallback text speak of it (R57). From the fourth wrong answer it stays rung 3's;
  - the ladder is per task, not per item: on a page of a workbook four submissions with a mistake offer to show the solution of the whole page.
- **Showing the solution** (О-7), on a task of a module:
  - a child is a learner of any age category but `adult` (concepts 13); to a child showing comes only from the fourth wrong answer, whatever kind of action asks for it;
  - "ask before showing" is a setting of the child's profile, on by default, which an adult changes. On, showing is an adult action, behind the PIN of the section for adults, and `api` refuses a learning request for it with "an adult is needed"; off, showing is a learning action. The server tells kinds of actions apart, not people (R04 api): the refusal is no security boundary, only the one place that enforces the setting on all the account's devices;
  - a learner of the category `adult` shows the solution from the start of the attempt, with no setting;
  - showing closes the attempt with the outcome "solution shown" and adds no trap of its own; the traps the program found earlier stay in the evidence;
  - the key and the task's solution go to the device only once the attempt is closed by a correct answer or by showing. A left, an abandoned and an "unchecked" attempt give no key (R05).
- **A task from paper** has no "Show the solution", at any rung, with the solver's key or the AI's, for every age category: its key and any solution never go to the device, and the app does nothing for the learner (R05; R162).
- **A hint on request** (О-21) sends no work (R69), and the rung grows only with wrong answers (R03):
  - before the first wrong answer — "givens and unknown", which `app` shows from the task's open view, and the task's technique and its leading question, when it has one, which `api` gives; without AI (R57; R108). The leading question is no rung and changes no fallback text;
  - before the first wrong answer on a task from paper, which has no module and so none of the three — the tutor's opening question: one AI call per attempt, with `hint`, from the task's crop as printed, without the learner's strokes, and the statements and keys of the frame's tasks once a Check derived them. The attempt keeps the model's words, and Hint gives them again without AI. Before a key exists the leak check takes the model's own answer of each task, which the call returns for that alone and nobody keeps; words that do not pass, or do not come, give the platform's opening question, "What do you already know here, and what do you need to find?", in the language of the interface, which is kept nowhere. It is no rung, and "explain differently" is not offered on it;
  - after a wrong answer — the current rung's words that the attempt keeps, without AI, or the rung's fallback text when there are none. Words not asked because the tutor's panel was closed are asked once, by AI and with the work, when "Hint" opens the panel (R148);
  - the rung's words on a task from paper come with `solution_analysis`, from the crop of the work, with every task of the frame — its statement, its key and the value read — and the rung's task by its number, in the language of the interface; the rung's task is the first "not yet" slot, as above. Their fallback text, which no module gives, is the platform's template of the rung, in English and Russian (R57; R139 tutor). Every call of the words of a task from paper — the opening question, a rung's, "explain differently" — is the cascade of R164, admitted by the author's word until 2027-01-17;
  - on a task with a rubric, an essay, which has no wrong answers and no ladder — what it gives before the first wrong answer: the techniques and the leading question, without AI and without the work. A task that names neither gets the empty answer, and `app` says there is nothing to hint; the button stays, since the techniques are closed and the device does not know them before it asks (R87; [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15);
  - "explain differently" — the same rung in other words: one AI call per rung, within the quota; the model gets what it gets for the rung's words (architecture 4.1), except the work. Words that did not come or did not pass the leak check and the form check (R70) become the rung's fallback text. In the mode without AI (О-5) it is not offered;
  - every call for the attempt's words, of a rung and of "differently", gets the previous questions of the task, so as not to repeat them (privacy 4);
  - the mode "self" gives the same: a hint exists in both modes, from the start of the task (concepts 10).
- **"Show where"** is the profile's hint mode (R162). With it on, after "Not yet" on a task from paper the tutor's mark is a wavy line under the place of the first mistake, drawn from the frame `tutor` returns with the rung's words of a model; with "Questions only", and with a fallback text, the words alone. The line stands beside the words in the tutor's panel, and goes with other work, the tracing paper moved, or another Check. A task of a module keeps its frame in either mode.
- **Evidence** (concepts 11) is the facts of the attempt, not the model's conclusions; what it carries is `learner-model`'s (R80; R08 learner-model), and an attempt of a task from paper gives none (R162). The outcome goes by the wrong answers; the request and "explain differently" do not change it. "Left unfinished" is the outcome of an attempt the learner left by beginning another, or abandoned, with wrong answers; without them it gives no evidence (R80). Beyond the outcome the evidence carries:
  - the traps the program found by the trap values, not the candidate traps of reading (R57);
  - for each item, those correct to the end too: whether it was submitted, the reasons of its submissions without a verdict, the first verdict and the number of wrong answers before the submission that gave it, the verdict at the end and the number of wrong answers before the first "correct";
  - the task's technique, at a step or on request, and the leading question on request in its own field of the schema of `learner-model`, apart from the technique (R21 learner-model);
  - how many times the learner asked "explain differently";
  - whether the solution of this task went to the profile's device earlier, after a correct answer or showing. A template has no such fact: a new attempt gives new numbers (R60). The solution of a task with a rubric, open after "Done" (R87), is a sample, not a key: it counts neither here nor in the summary of issues (R104);
  - everything else the model reads, and not the lesson's segment.

  That the learner saw "givens and unknown" is not recorded. The weights of the outcome and of each fact are `learner-model`'s (architecture 3.8).
- **The engine** does not give as the next task a task with a key — not a template — whose solution has gone to the learner's device; how long after it may, `engine` decides, and a task with a rubric it reads by its own rule (R03 engine; R107; architecture 3.8).

— *Why:*
- the recommendations of `api`, which repeat those of О-7 and О-21;
- the fourth wrong answer, as in canvas-api, where the ladder came from: there the analysis went on for at most three wrong answers (R39 canvas-api), and from the fourth came an offer of help (R09 api). So the child first tries the simpler case of rung 3;
- the setting on by default: in MathTrail a child never saw the solution before a correct answer (R39 canvas-api); this way an adult sees it first and may turn the setting off;
- showing closes the attempt: an answer after the shown solution checks nothing, and "solution shown" is an unsolved task, like "I don't know" in standalone (R93 standalone; R09 api);
- "differently" once per rung and without the work: at most three calls per attempt beyond the rungs' words, and of what is kept privacy 4 lets only the previous questions go to the AI;
- "left unfinished", not "not solved": that is what О-7 calls "solution shown", and one term means one thing. Leaving without wrong answers does not move the model, like a skip in R98 standalone, where punishing a skip punished an accidental tap;
- the evidence holds facts, not conclusions: "the item is blank" or "not solved" would be read by one version of the weight rule, submissions, verdicts and wrong answers by the next too (R08 learner-model). Without the first verdicts the model would not tell a page nine items of ten correct at the first submission from one correct only after hints (R06 learner-model). `api`'s attempt stores the verdicts, traps and wrong answers anyway (architecture 3.2 api): no new data of the learner. The lesson's segment changes no weight and has no reader (R06, R08 learner-model);
- the technique at a step or on request: for this distinction the contract keeps two requests, `BeginStep` and `GetHint`. The learner sees the solution after a correct answer too (concepts 6), so the fact covers both. "Givens and unknown" are open, since they do not hint at the way (R57), and in the mode "by steps" `app` shows them at a step without asking `api`: a record would mean something else;
- the leading question suggests the way, so it is closed and recorded (R57). Its own field: the log is append-only (R80), and a question in the technique's field would mix two facts for good, beyond recomputation;
- "Hint" on an essay: no new AI call and no new data; an essay is helped by the technique — the plan of a text from the module's author —, and the rubric's feedback comes after the submission anyway;
- a sample, not a key: the learner saw no key that a repeat would give away;
- a task from paper: the key never leaves the server, and the learner solves it themselves; the wavy line shows where without touching the learner's strokes (R05; R162). Its opening question is the AI's, by the author's word: a page has no author's question, and one question of the program for every task says little; kept, so Hint again costs nothing. The model's own answers guard it as a key guards a rung's words — a guard, not a proof, as R57's leak check is.

— *Rejected:*
- never showing the solution to a child, as R39 canvas-api, and "skipped, the rating does not change", as the prototype: О-7 recommends neither;
- showing from the third rung: the child would skip the simpler case;
- showing without closing the attempt: the key would be on the device while the attempt is open (R05);
- every request raising the rung, as the author's analysis in О-21: the learner would reach the solution without trying (R03);
- "explain differently" without a limit and with the work of the last submission: the quota would go on presses, and the device would keep the work to send again;
- closing О-7 alone, and О-21 after a measurement of "differently" in `tutor`: that is an eval of the hint, not a condition of the decision;
- a left or abandoned attempt "unchecked", as the attempts of R07 api: if `learner-model` weighs "unchecked" zero, the wrong answers before leaving are lost to the model;
- leaving without wrong answers as "left unfinished" too: R98 standalone rejected the same;
- recording that the learner saw "givens and unknown", or that they asked "Hint" before the first wrong answer: the first is wrong in the mode "by steps", the second has no reader until `learner-model` asks for it;
- the model's conclusions in the evidence, "which items were blank" or "not solved", instead of "whether the item was submitted" (R08 learner-model); the lesson's segment in the evidence;
- the leading question in the technique's field; a field of it in a contract of `spec`: the evidence is no contract of `spec` (architecture 3.8);
- on an essay, no "Hint", only "Done"; the tutor's question by the rubric's criteria — an AI call with the work, a new capability and its eval set; no button where the task names no technique — a new open field of the format or the contract to say whether a hint exists;
- a day's pause of the engine after "Done" with a solution;
- "Show the solution" of a task from paper with the solver's key or the AI's (R162);
- before the first wrong answer on a task from paper, a question of the program without AI, alike for every task, and an empty answer, "nothing to hint"; the words of a task from paper by Opus 5.5 · `high` alone, as the hint of a module, or by Haiku alone (the author's decisions of 2026-11-20);
- the wavy line in the mode "Questions only", or kept across other work, whose strokes it may no longer underline.

— product 13, О-7, О-21 and О-26; concepts 6, 10, 11 and 15; architecture 3.5, 3.7, 3.8 and 4.1; privacy 1 and 4; dpia 6; [the format text](../format/README.md), section 19; [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15; R05, R57, R80, R87, R108, R148, R162, R164; R09, R10 and R100 api, R139 tutor, R76 app, R87 canvas.

## Contracts: protobuf, buf and Connect

**R83. `spec`'s contracts are proto3 files in `contracts/`, packages `novatrail.<part>.v1`, by buf's rules `STANDARD`, `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC` and with the compatibility `FILE` against the previous release of `spec`. A field's name in JSON is its proto name, snake_case. A contract's version is the package's suffix and the tag of `spec`, and a breaking change is a new package and a new line of `spec`. The code from the contracts is generated by `spec`: in Go, the nested module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts`, in TypeScript, the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`. `app` and `api` talk over Connect.** The author's answers of 2026-11-02 in the planning of T54 (RUN.md), all by the plan's recommendations. The primary sources were read the same day.
- **Layout.**
  - The folder `contracts/` at the root of `spec`, as `format/`. The normative text is `contracts/README.md`, in English, as are the comments in the `.proto` files (R14, R42).
  - A file is `contracts/novatrail/<part>/v1/<name>.proto`, its package `novatrail.<part>.v1`: the path from `contracts/` repeats the package's name, as buf's rule `PACKAGE_DIRECTORY_MATCH` requires. The prefix `novatrail` makes the packages' names unique in the world, and the Go FAQ requires that of every declaration that gets into a Go binary.
  - `buf.yaml` of version 2 is at the root of `spec`, with one module, `contracts`, and without `deps`: buf takes dependencies only from the Buf Schema Registry, and the build must not depend on a service outside the repository.
- **buf's rules.**
  - `buf lint`: the categories `STANDARD`, `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC`, without `except` and with `disallow_comment_ignores: true`, so a comment in a file does not lift a rule. `COMMENTS` requires a comment on every element, as R45 requires a `description` on every property of a schema. `UNARY_RPC` forbids streams: the tutor's words go whole (R54), and there is no real-time channel in the first slice (Т-25). The rule `PROTOVALIDATE` is empty: protovalidate's constraints need the module `buf.validate` from the BSR, and the contracts do not take them.
  - `buf breaking`: the category `FILE`, against the previous release of `spec`; the first release with a package has nothing to compare with. How buf takes the previous release — by a git tag or by a release file checked by `release-verify` (R77) — is decided by T55.
- **Fields.**
  - Names are the terms of concepts 15 in English, in snake_case, and a repeated field is in the plural (protobuf's style).
  - Integer places and crops are `int32` (R53): an `int64` is a string in JSON and a `bigint` in TypeScript. There are no unsigned ones. `int64` is only for a value that can be greater than 2³¹ − 1, the greatest `int32`.
  - An enum's zero value is `<NAME>_UNSPECIFIED`, and it has no meaning. A field and an enum value are not removed from a package (version, below): what is not needed stays, with a comment saying so, and the next major package does not take it.
  - The values and IDs of the module format — `handwriting_sheet`, a task's ID — stay `string`, not a proto enum: otherwise one value would have two spellings.
  - `optional` is on a simple field where "none" and zero differ, as absence in R72. "One of" is `oneof`. PNG is `bytes`, and in JSON it is a base64 string.
  - How the format's open view, a JSON Schema value, goes into protobuf is decided by T64.
- **Names in JSON.** A field's name in JSON is its proto name, snake_case, as in the format (R45).
  - A JSON writer — of a sample file, of a file of `spec`, of the Connect codec — turns on `UseProtoNames` in Go (`protojson`) or `useProtoFieldName` in TypeScript (protobuf-es).
  - The option `json_name` is forbidden in the contracts. A reader accepts both spellings, as ProtoJSON requires.
- **Syntax** is `syntax = "proto3"`, and simple fields where presence matters are `optional`. The Go code is the Open API, the default for proto3. Moving to editions is possible later, by a decision of its own: the wire and JSON do not change by it.
- **Version.**
  - A contract has no MAJOR.MINOR version of its own. The version is the package's suffix, `v1`, and the tag of `spec` in which the file came out. buf's rule `PACKAGE_VERSION_SUFFIX` does not let a package `v0` through.
  - Within a package a change only adds, and `buf breaking` `FILE` holds this. Such a change comes out in any release of the line.
  - A breaking change is a new package, `v2`, beside `v1`. A package `vN` with N from 2, beside `v(N−1)`, opens a new line of `spec`, and `release-version` holds this, as with the format (R44); the code of the check is T55. The first package `v1` of a new part does not open a line.
  - `api` keeps two major packages, the current and the previous, as the window of R44, and `app` reads the package of its build. Within a major package an old build of `app` works with a new `api`: both sides of Connect skip unknown fields. This is the answer to the question of RUN.md, Д20: which versions of the contract `api` and `app` read when the build of `app` is older than the service.
- **The Go code** is the nested module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts`, with its own `go.mod` in `contracts/`.
  - The generated `.pb.go` and `.connect.go` lie in the repository beside their `.proto`. Whether they match what buf generates is checked by T55, as `just types-check` checks the format's types (R72).
  - The module's tag is `contracts/vX.Y.Z`, with the number of the tag of `spec`. The module requires `google.golang.org/protobuf` and `connectrpc.com/connect/v2` at exact versions.
  - The root module of `spec` still requires nothing (R64): with the `go.mod` in `contracts/` that T55 brings, the nested module is not in its zip. Until then `contracts/README.md` lies in the root's zip, as the repository's other texts do.
- **The TypeScript code** is the npm package `@altnovatrail/contracts`: JavaScript code and declarations, `target=js+dts`, and JSON types, `json_types=true`.
  - Its dependency is `@bufbuild/protobuf` at an exact version.
  - The package comes out as a release file of its own, with a trusted publisher in npm, and a consumer checks it with `release-verify-npm`, as `@altnovatrail/spec` (R73, R77). The path is T57, and setting up the publisher is the author's step.
  - `@altnovatrail/spec` stays declarations only (R73). The mark's type in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` is written by hand, as the element's types are, and `tools/types/canvas.check.ts` compares it with the mark's type of the contract (R74; RUN.md, T62).
- **The transport** `app` ↔ `api` is Connect, and the contract chooses it: the services' stubs are born in `spec`, and the client must match the server.
  - The server is connect-go v2 in `api`, the client connect-es in `app`.
  - Calls are unary only.
  - JSON or binary protobuf on the wire is a choice of the transport, and T07 `api` decides it. A Connect server accepts both, and gRPC and gRPC-Web too.
- **The plugins** of buf are local, at exact versions; there are no remote BSR plugins, whose version may be "latest". How the devcontainer installs them is decided by T55:
  - `protoc-gen-go` and `protoc-gen-connect-go` by the `tool` directive of the Go module in `tools/`;
  - `protoc-gen-es` at an exact version in `tools/package.json`;
  - `buf` itself as an `ARG` of the Dockerfile, with a checksum for each architecture from its release's `sha256.txt` (R34).

  As of 2026-11-02 the newest versions are: buf v1.75.0 (Apache-2.0), `google.golang.org/protobuf` v1.36.12 (BSD-3-Clause), `connectrpc.com/connect/v2` v2.0.2 (Apache-2.0), `@bufbuild/protobuf` and `@bufbuild/protoc-gen-es` 2.16.0 (Apache-2.0 and BSD-3-Clause), `@connectrpc/connect` 2.3.0 (Apache-2.0). All the licenses are of category A (R12).

— *Why:*
- **One type per process.** `tutor`, `module-kit` and `api` exchange the observation in one process (R15), and it must have one type. The Go FAQ: "When a single .proto file is generated into two or more Go packages and linked into the same Go binary, it conflicts on every Protobuf declaration in the generated Go packages", and "Starting with v1.26.0 of the google.golang.org/protobuf module, a hard error will be reported when a Go program starts up that has multiple conflicting Protobuf names linked into it" (protobuf.dev/reference/go/faq, read 2026-11-02). Code generated at each consumer would not start this binary. `api` too expects the contract "as generated packages from the releases of `spec`" (architecture 1 api).
- **A nested module.** The generated code imports the protobuf runtime (`protoreflect`, `protoimpl`), and the root module of `spec` requires nothing (R64). The nested module's tag: "each tag name must be prefixed with the module subdirectory, followed by a slash" (go.dev/ref/mod, read 2026-11-02). R64 has two arguments against a subfolder: a second kind of tags — its cost is accepted — and a copy of `format/` inside; here nothing needs copying: the `.proto` files lie in the module itself.
- **An npm package of its own.** protobuf-es code takes a runtime too: `import { fileDesc, messageDesc } from "@bufbuild/protobuf/codegenv2"` (`packages/protobuf-example/src/gen/example_pb.ts` @v2.16.0). And `@altnovatrail/spec` is declarations only, without dependencies (R73). connect-es does not work without the descriptors, so types alone are not enough.
- **The rules.** The version suffix: "The last component of a package must be a version of the form v\d+ … where the numeric parts are at least 1" (buf.build/docs/lint/rules, read 2026-11-02). Compatibility: "If you don't know which to pick, start with FILE (the default)", and "you should use FILE to protect all generated languages" (buf.build/docs/breaking/rules, read 2026-11-02): the contracts generate code in two languages.
- **Names in JSON.** "Parsers accept both the lowerCamelCase name (or the one specified by the json_name option) and the original proto field name. This allows for a serializer option to choose to print using the original field name … and have the resulting output still be parsed back by all spec parsers" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json, read 2026-11-02). So a field has one spelling — in the format, in `.proto` and in JSON —, and a sample file is of the same style as the module (RUN.md, Д21).
- **`optional`.** "We recommend adding the optional label for proto3 basic types by default" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/field_presence, read 2026-11-02).
- **Integers.** "ProtoJSON serializers emit int64s as strings to ensure no precision loss will occur on large int64s by any implementation" (protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json). The fractions 0–1000 and the integer crops (R53) fit in `int32`, and in JSON they are numbers.
- **Connect.** "Connect also offers direct support for the gRPC-Web protocol used by grpc/grpc-web, without relying on a translating proxy like Envoy", and Connect's own protocol "works over HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3" (connectrpc.com/docs/introduction, read 2026-11-02). Both sides skip unknown fields: connect-go v2.0.2 — `DiscardUnknown: true, // Ensure difference schema versions unmarshal.` (`connectproto/connectproto.go`), connect-es 2.3.0 — "In connect-es, unknown JSON fields are ignored by default" (`packages/connect/src/protocol/serialization.ts`).

— *Rejected:*
- a folder `proto/`: a name by the technology, not by the role; the contracts inside `format/`: two normative parts with different versions in one folder and one archive;
- `STANDARD` without `COMMENTS` and `UNARY_RPC`, and the soft `BASIC`, `WIRE_JSON` and `PACKAGE`: without a version in the package's name, without `_UNSPECIFIED`, and `WIRE_JSON` does not protect the generated code;
- lowerCamelCase names in JSON, ProtoJSON's default: a field has two spellings; `json_name` on every field: a duplicate of the name, easy to forget;
- Edition 2023 and 2024: 2024 gives the Opaque API in Go by default, while publishers of generated Go code are advised the Hybrid one (go.dev/blog/protobuf-opaque, 16.12.2024), protoc-gen-go v1.36.12 goes no further than 2024, and every generator knows proto3;
- a MAJOR.MINOR version of its own, as the format has: a new line for each task of E3, and STANDARD does not let a package `v0` through; `v1alpha1` until the first app: buf would not catch the renaming of a field, and sample files are kept long;
- the code in the root module of `spec`: it breaks R64 and R72, and every consumer of `spec` in Go would get the protobuf runtime; the code at each consumer: a conflict of the protobuf registry in the binary of `api`; a generator of our own without a runtime, as `tools/types`: our own implementation of ProtoJSON and no Connect stubs, while connect-go requires `proto.Message`;
- the TypeScript code in `@altnovatrail/spec`: it breaks R73; generation at `app` and `canvas`: two generators whose versions may diverge; declarations only: connect-es does not work without descriptors;
- gRPC-Web: the browser needs a proxy, Envoy by default; HTTP of our own with protobuf bodies, as R67 canvas-api: there are no stubs, and the contract does not check the transport; choosing the transport in the detailing of `api`: the stubs are born in `spec`, and the client must match the server.

— *Consequence:* [contracts/README.md](../contracts/README.md); the 2026-11-02 amendments to R11, R21, R44, R64, R72 and R73; concepts 1 and 15; repositories 1 and 5; architecture 1 and 3.5; CLAUDE.md, Documents; RUN.md: T55 and T57 take the files, checks, tags and package, and Д20 and Д21 are added to.

## Own key

**R84. An own key lies on the device only if the key's owner decided so on this device — in the database of their profile —, and otherwise only in the tab's memory while their profile is open; on the server, only in the request's memory. The key and its provider come with every request of the owner profile that calls AI, and `api` accepts them only with a profile of the category `adult`. The owner profile on an account that has a profile of another category is opened by the same PIN as the section for adults. The providers' terms allow giving the key to `api`. Т-9 and П-17 are closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-02 to the rows «в реестр spec» `app` В20–В23 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 14f5a54): В20–В22 by their recommendations, and В23 not by its recommendation. What `app` and `api` decided is R08 app and R04 api.
- **Where the key lies** (Т-9). On the device, only by the key's owner's mark "Keep on this device", separate for each device: only they know whether the device is shared. Without the mark the key lives in the tab's memory while the owner profile is open. There is no encryption in the browser: whoever holds the device can get at a key saved on the device, and `app` says so plainly, and the damage is held by the key's limit and lifetime at the provider (R55 tutor; concepts 14). On the server, only in the request's memory, not in the database and not in the logs (privacy 5.2). The key is not in the export: the export is the learners' data, and the key is a secret of the key's owner (architecture 4.5).
- **With which request.** With every request of the owner profile that calls AI: with the work for reading, with the rung's words and with "explain differently", which sends no work (R82). `app` names the provider without the key at the start of the attempt (RUN.md, Д66). With a request of a profile of a category other than `adult`, `api` does not accept a key, and checks this itself (R04 api; О-4). A provider's refusal by a limit is the outcome "limit reached" with a cause (R55 tutor), a refusal of the key itself — wrong or revoked — is an outcome of its own, and neither moves the call to platform AI without an action of the key's owner (R08 app).
- **Connecting.** `api` checks the key through `tutor` — it does not go to providers bypassing `tutor` (architecture 3.5) — by a request without the learner's content, on behalf of the owner profile: the key is accepted, wrong, the key has no rights, or the provider is closed for the profile. The providers open to an own key for the profile are named by `api` by the admission function (Т-20), and `app` does not build them in.
- **The owner profile on a shared device** (П-17) is behind the same PIN as the section for adults, at every opening, if the account holds a profile of a category other than `adult`. It closes by itself: by "Switch learner", on reload and after 5 minutes of a hidden page. Without such profiles, without a PIN (R08 app). The PIN is a barrier of the interface, and `api` holds its hash and counter (R04 api).
- **The providers' terms** (В23). They allow giving an own key to `api`: so the author decided, without a lawyer. At Anthropic, API keys of individuals too go by the Commercial Terms, there is no clause about passing a key in them, and the help page directly describes a key in third-party tools: "when you upload your API key to third-party tools … you are giving the developer of that tool access to your Claude Console account". At OpenAI, the Services Agreement is a contract "between the organization agreeing to these terms", §3.1 says "Customer will not share Account access credentials or individual login credentials between multiple users", by §3.3(g) one may not "buy, sell, or transfer API keys from, to, or with a third party", and an End User is also the one "who accesses the Services under Customer’s Account". There is no direct ban on a key in a third-party service in it. The sources and dates are privacy 10.

— *Why:* the author's answer. The providers advise keeping a key on the server: OpenAI, "Don’t share it with others or expose it in any client-side code such as browsers or apps", Anthropic's SDK for the browser, "Any user with access to the browser can potentially inspect, extract, and misuse these credentials" (architecture 4 app; checked 2026-11-02). But there are no own keys on the server (architecture 7), so the key is on the device, by default only in memory, and in the database where an adult learns alone and decided so themselves. The key comes with every AI call: otherwise "explain differently" of the key's owner would go through platform AI, at its quota and under its contracts, not under the terms the key's owner accepted with the provider (privacy 5.1, 5.2). The check at connecting is so that a typo in the key is found on the page where the key is entered, not at the first hint. Both sides decided П-17, while О-4 and П-4 decide who gets an own key, not how it lies on a shared device: a key is only ever on a profile `adult` anyway.

— *Rejected:*
- the key always on the device, as Т-9 recommended: on a shared tablet it would always lie there, against the providers' advice;
- the key on the server, encrypted: the server would hold a secret of every key's owner, and architecture 7 does not allow it;
- the key only with the work, as architecture 3.9 tutor and T07 `api` wrote: "explain differently" of the key's owner would go through platform AI;
- no check of the key: a wrong key would be found at the first call;
- П-17 open until О-4: О-4 decides who gets a key;
- the providers' terms as a question to a lawyer in epic E4 before the code of the own key, as `app` recommended, as a question of its own or an addition to П-4; the own OpenAI key closed until the lawyer answers. The author chose to count the passing as allowed: Anthropic directly describes such a path, and OpenAI does not directly forbid it.

— *Does not decide:* for whom the own key is, О-4 and П-4; the admission table, Т-20 (RUN.md, T61); how `tutor` checks the key.

— *Consequence:* Т-9 and П-17 are closed; privacy 2, 4, 5.2 and 10; architecture 3.1, 3.5, 3.6, 4.3, 4.5, 5 and 7; concepts 14; product 12; RUN.md: «Свой ключ в контракте `app` ↔ `api`» at table 1 and T62–T64. The components get the answer with their move to a tag — RUN.md, Д78.

— repositories 8; privacy 5.2, 9, 10; architecture 4.3; R08 app, R04 api.

There is no "Do not close" among the periods.** Closing for protection is a time limit by WCAG 2.2, 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable, level A: "if a time limit is included in order to address security concerns, it would be considered to have been set by the content" ([Understanding 2.2.1](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/timing-adjustable.html)). Until then the format is R09 app, and its rules are the schema `deployment.schema.json` and the CSP template `csp.json` in the signed build of `app`: by them the rollout and a self-hosting operator check the file.** The author's answer of 2026-11-02 to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В24 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 14f5a54), with the triage's clarification about the timing.
- The file is written not by those who read it: on the platform, by the rollout of `infra` from the rollout list (Т-19), in a self-hosting copy, by its operator, and `app` reads it. Format 1 is `format`, `api` and `signIn` (R09 app).
- The part's path is the same as that of the AI admission table (RUN.md, T61; Т-20): a version of its own, a release file and an `fs.FS` in the Go module (R64), types in `@altnovatrail/spec` (R73), test vectors. It is not in `format/`: there is one normative part with a version of its own there (R83). The build of `app` then carries a copy of the schema from the release of `spec` it stands on.

## Observation

**R86. The observation is the contract `novatrail.observation.v1`. For each answer slot whose answer AI reads, it carries the value as written, or why there is no value, and for a slot `anywhere` also the box of the final answer. `module-kit` joins two readings into one, by the slot check, and gives the verdict by the joined observation. The module format does not change by this. The reading request and the analysis response are types of `tutor`, and a change of the contract's meaning is a new package.** The author's answers of 2026-11-02 in the planning of T56 (RUN.md), all by the plan's recommendations. Normatively, [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, and `contracts/novatrail/observation/v1/observation.proto`.
- **What is in the observation.** The message `Observation` is the slots whose answer AI reads, each once, in the task's order. On a handwriting sheet these are the slots `anywhere`, `zone` and `sheet`, on a workbook every box. `tutor` takes the boxes from the open view, and gives an empty one as empty without calling the model: the work holds only the filled ones (the 2026-10-27 amendment to R53). A slot has its place, `{ item, slot }` from 1, and one of two: `value`, as written, or `unreadable`: blank, illegible, ambiguous, no final answer, several final answers. AI does not read a tapped choice, and it is not in the observation: `api` gives `module-kit` the option the learner chose beside the observation.
- **What the reader gives.**
  - A value only if it is visible in the writing itself (R62 canvas-api), and as written: the check kind normalizes it (R56). A vertical fraction is written in a line.
  - "Ambiguous" is a mirrored digit (the 2026-10-29 amendment to R56), a value of which the reader sees another reading, and a value that it cannot show in the writing.
  - The reader knows nothing of the slot check: neither the kind nor the options of a handwritten choice. This is the answer to the question Д37. The answer's form is named by the task statement ([the format text](../format/README.md), section 15), and options among which the key stands would hint at the answer, as the key would (R67).
- **The place** is the answer to "how the observation chooses a place" (R53):
  - for a slot `anywhere`, the box of the final answer on the crop in whole thousandths, `CropBox`, if the reader named it and it is valid;
  - for a zone and a box, the slot itself;
  - a group label only if group boxes go with the work (Т-31).
- **Joining.** Slots with a verdict have two readers (R68), and `tutor` gives the observations of both or a call outcome, never one. `module-kit` joins them slot by slot:
  - values agree when the slot check compares them as equal, as a value with a trap, and gives them one verdict; then the value is that of the pair's first reader. A predicate compares the integers read;
  - equal reasons give the same reason, and everything else gives "ambiguous";
  - a value that the check kind normalizes to empty is joined as "blank", and a joined reason has no box;
  - an invalid observation is as an AI failure: there is no joined one, and every slot that AI reads is "unchecked". A reason that the release of `module-kit` reading the observation does not know is invalid too.

  An essay is read by one reader, and there is nothing to join (the second 2026-11-01 amendment to R68).
- **The verdict** is by the joined observation as a whole (the 2026-10-28 amendment to R54).
  - A value gets the format's verdict, with a reason and a trap ([the format text](../format/README.md), section 15).
  - A reason without a value gives `unreadable` with the reason of its name: `blank`, `illegible`, `ambiguous`, `no_final_answer` or `several_final_answers`. The reason `notation` remains the format's.
- **The call outcomes are not an observation.** An AI failure, a limit, "not admitted" and a refusal of the own key (R84) give the slots that AI reads "unchecked". If one reader failed, there is no observation at all.
- **What `api` stores** is the joined observation and the tapped choice: by them the same release of `module-kit` repeats the verdict (R03). The readers' observations, the writing parts and other readings are not stored, and what is stored for an essay is П-19.
- **The format does not change.** It judges the read value, and what makes a slot "unreadable" before the check kind its text already assigns to the observation. [The format text](../format/README.md), section 15, now refers to the contract: this is an editorial change. So too the rules about a vertical fraction and about a mirrored digit did not change the format's version: they are rules about the reader (the 2026-10-28 and 2026-10-29 amendments to R56).
- **The reading request and the analysis response are types of `tutor`.** Only `api` and `tutor` exchange them, and `api` calls its library anyway.
  - The open view in the request is the format's type `open.Task` (R72), and how it goes into protobuf is decided by T64.
  - The analysis gives the box of the first error or nothing, and a trap from the block or nothing. The box is the same message `CropBox`, and in T62 `api` gives it as a mark without conversion.
  - The candidate trap and the place of the first error were put by concepts 9.1 in the observation, but this is the response of the analysis, which sees the key (R67).
- **The version of the meaning.**
  - A new value of a reason or a new field is an addition to `v1`.
  - A change of the meaning of a field, a value or a rule of [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10 — whatever gives another result on the same message — breaks the package: a `v2` and a new line are needed, as with a major change of the format (R44).
  - `buf breaking` does not see this, and review holds it (the second 2026-11-02 amendment to R83).
- **The vectors** of the joining and of the verdict by the observation are a separate task, T68: with the code of `tools/`, T56 would be more than one check (rule 11 of RUN.md).

— *Why:* the author's answers of 2026-11-02 while T56 was planned, all by the plan's recommendations.
- **The join is `module-kit`'s.** Normalization is its own (R56), and comparing by verdict is possible only with the key. In `tutor`, the reading path would get the slot checks together with the keys, and R67 keeps reading without the key. The join is a rule, not perception, and its place is in the deterministic core (R03). The eval of `tutor` compares the same way: "their values, read as the check of the kind number reads them, and their verdicts are one" (`internal/report/reading.go` of `tutor`, `main` be607e5, read 2026-11-02).
- **Comparing by the check, not by the text.** "0.5" and "1/2" under `number` are one value, and "3 / 4" and "3/4" are one notation: by the text they would go to "unreadable" with no gain. One verdict is needed because the check compares "2/4" and "1/2" equal, while under `form: reduced` their verdicts differ.
- **Without the writing parts and the other readings.** The check needs only the values, and the analysis does not get the observation (architecture 3.10 tutor). With the parts, `api` would keep the learner's writing of the solution whole, "while the profile lives" (architecture 3.2 api), and minimization does not allow this (privacy 1). The other readings are already expressed by the reason "ambiguous" (R34 tutor).
- **The format is not touched.** The type of the observation is described once — in `.proto`, while in the format's vectors it would have to be described by JSON Schema as well. A new format version would require a new line and a move of all the components, though not one module changes.
- **The types of `tutor`.** A contract is needed where a type is shared by two repositories that do not call each other: the observation goes from `tutor` to `module-kit` (R83). The reading request and the analysis response go only between `api` and the library of `tutor`, and the place in them is from the contract.
- **A version of the meaning.** The verdict is repeated from the observation kept (R03), and an edit of the join rule would change it on the same messages with no sign in the package.

— *Rejected:*
- format 0.3, where the format's verdict is given from the observation, and the verdict vectors carry the reasons and two readings. That is a new line 0.7, ~140 files of `module_format_version`, new digests of the vectors of packages and indexes, and the type of the observation would be described twice;
- a rule in the format text without a new version: new reasons for "unreadable" are a new value of the list, and in v0 that is the next 0.y;
- the join in `tutor`, as architecture 3.7 tutor proposes: normalization and the key are `module-kit`'s;
- the join by the text after normalization — stricter with no gain;
- the writing parts in the observation, as architecture 3.10 tutor proposes, and the other readings, which architecture 3.2 api wants to keep;
- the reading request and the analysis response in the contract: the open view in protobuf would be decided before T64, and the analysis response before T62;
- the vectors in the same task: with the code of `tools/`, T56 would become two checks;
- an edit of the meaning within `v1`: an old observation in the database would be read by the new rule with no sign of the version.

— *Amendment 2026-11-03:* **the observation vectors are JSON files `contracts/vectors/observation/v1/<case>.json` without a schema of their own. They hold the task's items, the readers' observations with a validity flag, the taps and the joined observation with verdicts, and for an essay the outcome of the submission. `spec` reads the observations by the descriptors of buf's image and computes the result by a second implementation in `just contracts-check`. `module-kit` takes the vectors as `contracts.Vectors` of the Go module of the contracts. The [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, is refined by an editorial change: where it could be read two ways, the vectors pin one reading.** The author's answers of 2026-11-03 while T68 was planned (RUN.md), all by the plan's recommendations.
- **JSON, not YAML.** An observation in a vector is proto3 JSON with proto names, and with it the whole file. The [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 6, already names "a file of `spec`" as a writer of the contract's JSON. `module-kit` reads a vector through `encoding/json` and `protojson`, without YAML. JSON has none of YAML's type traps: `8.` and `0.5` stay strings. An observation is written as `toJson` with `useProtoFieldName` and `alwaysEmitImplicit` or `protojson` with `UseProtoNames` and `EmitDefaultValues` writes it — with every field, zeros too. A reason that the package does not have is written as a number. Rejected: YAML, like the format's vectors — rules of the format's YAML would be needed, and the observation would have to be rewritten in YAML.
- **No schema of its own.**
  - The type of the observation is described once — in `.proto` (the argument of R86). It is held by a strict `fromJson`, and the writing by a comparison with `toJson`.
  - The canvas and the items are held by the format's schema, `task.schema.json`: `#/properties/canvas` and `#/$defs/item`. The task's rules that are seen by the slot check are held by `slotBreaches` of `format-check`.
  - The keys of the file and of a case are held by the check's code, and the file is described by the [contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 10, "Test vectors".
  - Rejected: a JSON Schema of a wrapper in which the observation is just `object`. Under `contracts/` second schemas with their own conventions would appear, and the reference to the format version would have to be raised with each of its versions.
- **`contracts.Vectors`.**
  - The vectors lie in `contracts/`, so they are carried by the Go module `github.com/altnovatrail/spec/contracts` at the tag `contracts/vX.Y.Z`. `tools/gomod` already requires every file of `contracts/` in its zip.
  - The package `contracts` at the root of the module — `contracts/vectors.go`, written by hand, — embeds `vectors/` with the directive `//go:embed all:vectors`, like `spec.Format` (R64), and requires nothing beyond the standard library.
  - Its test checks that what is embedded matches the files on disk. It also reads each observation of each vector with `protojson` and compares the writing back: this shows that Go takes the vectors the same way as protobuf-es.
  - Rejected:
    - reading from the submodule `spec/` — it diverges from R64: code takes the files of `spec` from a release;
    - a release file of its own, `observation-vectors-<version>.tar.gz` — the contracts have no version of their own beyond the package ([contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 2), and a new kind of release file is a new line.
- **The descriptors of buf's image.**
