**R135. The export format is a normative part, `export/`: an export file is a ZIP of JSON files — the manifest of `app`, the part of `api` byte for byte, `api.zip`, per profile a file of what the device holds, each stored work as `GetWork` gives it, and each page from the learner's paper; one form for the export of a profile and of an account; the evidence log, the model's state and the observation are the JSON of their protobuf messages, and their `.proto` files are in the export; records — by the part's JSON Schema; the version is an integer, and a new one opens a line of `spec`.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 while T101 and T103 were planned (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; R151 and the author's answers of 2026-11-15 to В35 and В36 and to the review of T161; the author's answer of 2026-11-17 to `api` В82; R162 and the author's answers of 2026-11-18 while T225 was planned. Normative — [the part's text](../export/README.md).
- **The container is a ZIP**: any system opens it without a program of its own, and `app` puts the part of `api` as a separate file, as the method gave it, without parsing it (R98). Inside `api.zip` — `account.json` in an account export, `profiles/<id>.json` and `proto/`; beside it, the manifest, the device's files, the stored works and the pages from paper ([the part's text](../export/README.md), section 3).
- **Protobuf is JSON of the same value**, by the protobuf JSON mapping with the field names as in `.proto`, as `buf convert` does (R10 learner-model), and the `.proto` of the version of `learner-model` that computed it and `novatrail/observation/v1/observation.proto` lie in the export: the export says what each field means, and the same bytes can be assembled from it again. A history of writing and a context of submission go in as the JSON values their bytes hold. The one kind of bytes in the export is an image, in base64 — a stored work's picture, a page's photo and a task's crop —, since an image has no JSON of its own.
- **Records** — the profile with its hint mode, consents — who gave each, the owner, a parent or the learner, the request code, the state of the form, the text versions as a list —, attempts, observations, submissions with a rubric, lesson runs, engine choices, evidence, the state, counters, whether storage of works is on, the records of storage consent, the problem reports and what the device holds — by the part's schemas, by the columns «в выгрузку» of architecture 3.2 api and 3.2 app; without secrets and service data (R21 api; R84), without the minimal consent record (R117) and the scan of the form (R116).
- **Stored works** (R113; R151) — `api.zip`'s profile file names each as `ListWorks` does: the attempt, the kind — handwriting, an essay or a drawing —, when `api` kept it and the size, without its bytes. `app` writes each from `GetWork` as a file of its own: the IDs of the profile and the attempt, the kind, when kept, the history and the contexts and the picture. The rule `export.works` holds a profile to one work for each attempt, each work it names to its file and each such file to a work it names, by the profile, the attempt, the kind and the instant it was kept. A work that `GetWork` gives with another time, or does not give, makes `app` begin the export again, at most three times in a row; if the third finds a work changed or gone as well, it hands over no file and tells the owner that the works are changing on another device and to try again later. When storage on the server is on, a work may lie both at `api` and on the device; the export puts both, and a reader recognizes them by the attempt ID. The text of an essay is stored nowhere (R87).
- **Pages from paper** (R162) — the server keeps none, so `app` writes each page from the device as a file of its own: when it was taken, the photo, the frames of the tasks with who drew each, the AI or the learner, and each picked task's attempt, its frame, its crop, its history of writing, the place of its tracing paper and its submissions. `api.zip`'s profile file holds the open attempts of tasks from paper as `paper_attempts` — what `api` keeps of each while it is open: the counts, the rungs and the key's provenance, the solver or the AI —, without the key (R05). They are no evidence and no part of the evidence log. The rule `export.paper` holds each page to a profile the part of `api` holds and to the IDs its path names, each task to one of the page's frames, and an attempt to one task of one page of the profile.
- **IDs as paths.** The ID of a profile, an attempt or a page that names a file is one part of a path, `file_id`: letters, digits, `-`, `_` and `.`, never `.` or `..`, which the UUIDs of `api` fit. No two profiles of an export, and no two stored works or pages of a profile, have IDs that are one once `A`–`Z` are read as small: the rule `export.case` refuses such an export and names the files of each, and [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15, holds `api` to IDs that differ in more than letter case.
- **The evidence log.** A record of an attempt names it by `attempt_id`, and the adult's correction of a module's level (`level_set_by_adult`, R157) by `correction_id`, with the package of the module's current version as its `package_digest`; no `wrong_key` version filters a correction out (R89 api). In the reading mode `single` a record's `observation` is the one reader's.
- **One form for two scopes**: a profile export is one profile without the account, an account export is the account and all its profiles; the rules of [the part's text](../export/README.md), section 5, hold this.
- **The version** — the integer `export/VERSION` and the field `format` of each JSON file of the export; the manifest's `api_format` and the contract's `export_format_version` are the same integer as a string. A new field, a new kind of record or of file or a new rule is a new version of the part and a new line of `spec` (`tools/release/export-line.mjs`); a schema's annotations — `title`, `description`, `$comment` and `examples` — and the examples and vectors change within a version. Each version has its types, `types/exportv<version>` and `@altnovatrail/spec/exportv<version>`, from its line on, and the lines before keep theirs. An export of an earlier version is read by that version, as its `export-<version>.tar.gz` holds it, which no release changes; a reader of one version refuses another by the schema. [The part's text](../export/README.md), section 2, names each version and its line.
- **A build of `app` older than the part of `api`**: one that gets an `export_format_version` its build does not write builds no file and offers to reload, as on `unimplemented`. `api` goes out first with a new version, so the build that meets it is the older one.

— *Why:* the export is the account owner's right (privacy 1, 7; GDPR Arts. 15 and 20), and any program must read it, without the platform's library (R09), and `api` and `app` must write it by one norm.
- An image in base64, beside the history as JSON: the owner gets the picture and can build the strokes again.
- A file for each work and each page keeps every answer within one file, read with no library; a work changed between `ExportProfile` and `GetWork` would make the export say two things of it.
- The pages are `app`'s to write: the photo, the crops and the work stay on the device (R162). The open attempts of tasks from paper are what `api` keeps of the learner, so the owner gets them; the key is the program's and never leaves the server (R05).
- `export.case`: a file system that does not tell case apart would make two files or folders of the export one when it is unpacked, one lost without a word.
- `correction_id`: a correction is no attempt, and the log stays one sequence by `seq`.
- A reload is how `app` already meets a contract newer than its build, with no new field; an export stays whole.

— *Rejected:*
- one JSON file into which `app` inserts the part of `api` — fragile, and the part of `api` would become a string inside a string; both bytes and JSON in the export — two forms of one value to keep in step; only bytes — not readable without a protobuf library (R09); a proto package `novatrail.export.v1` for the records — against the author's answer 3 in E4 («нормативными частями, путём `deployment/`»);
- an image as a file of its own — a file of the export that is not JSON; the picture alone, without the history — the owner could not build the strokes again; holding the size to the work's file — the size counts the bytes `api` keeps, which the JSON value of the history does not give back;
- a reader of one version bound to read the earlier ones too — the part's check would carry two versions of its schemas;
- `ExportProfile` and `ExportAccount` naming the version `app` writes, and `api` giving either — a new field and two writers in `api`; no export and no word why until the build reloads; after the third new beginning, an export of the works as `GetWork` gave them — the rule and the manifest would change; `api` refusing `PutWork` of the profile while an export goes on — a new cause and a new state in `api`;
- `file_id` in small letters alone, with `api` held to them — it would narrow the form of the IDs `api` gives beyond what the clash needs;
- a correction's ID in `attempt_id`; the corrections as a list of their own in the profile's file — the log would no longer be one sequence by `seq`;
- the key of an open attempt of a task from paper in the export — it is the program's (R05); the attempts of tasks from paper left out of `api.zip` — the owner would not see what `api` keeps.

— *Consequence:* [the part `export/`](../export/README.md) and `tools/export/`; `spec.Export`, `types/exportv<version>`; the release file `export-<version>.tar.gz` from the line 0.14; the comment of `export_format_version` and [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15; privacy 4; concepts 15; architecture 4.5; RUN.md — T101, T103, T144, T161, T189 and T225.

— privacy 1, 4, 7; R05, R09, R80, R84, R87, R98, R113, R116, R117, R130, R134, R151, R157, R162; R08, R21 and R89 api; R04–R06 app; R08 and R10 learner-model; Д233.

**R136. The consent contract (T103): confirmation of parental consent by a signed form, the scan of which `app` uploads by the request code; a learner's own consent and its withdrawal in their profile; cancelling a waiting one and the limit of "waiting" consents; age and country anew; storage of works as a consent; the text version in each consent record; "report a problem" with storage for a year after handling.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 while T103 was planned (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; the 2026-11-10 amendments to R98, R113, R116, R123, R131 and R132, and R135.
- **Who gives consent** — by the category (R116, R134): for a learner below the country's age of digital consent — a parent, at it and above — the learner themselves, for their own profile — the owner. `ChildConsent` and `ProfileConsent` name this by the field `giver`, and `ProfileConsent.need` names what the profile waits for before the next work: the learner's own consent, a parental consent or the age; while it waits, a learning request gets `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT` or `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED` ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15).
- **Parental consent** is a signed form `parent-consent` with the request code: 10 characters of Crockford base32, `ABCDE-FGHJK`, unique among the waiting ones. A scan, a photo or a PDF up to 10 MiB the adult uploads in `app`, `SendConsentForm`; `api` puts it into the closed bucket of R116, and the operator checks it against the code with its command and confirms the consent or does not accept the form, and then a new one is sent. A card transaction — by the public launch (П-28).
- **A learner's own consent** — `GiveOwnConsent` by the text `teen-consent`, in their profile, before the first work: the profile of such a learner `CreateChildProfile` creates at once. With it too a learner who has grown to the age confirms the consent that a parent gave (R116).
- **Withdrawal** is deletion of the profile with everything in it, with the minimal record of R117 (R132): parental consent — `DeleteProfile`, one's own — `WithdrawOwnConsent`, by a learning request. A learner who gave consent themselves also exports before the withdrawal themselves: `ExportProfile` with `ACTION_LEARNING`. Neither `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT` nor `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED` refuses requests about the consent itself — `GiveOwnConsent`, `WithdrawOwnConsent`, the learner's export, turning storage off and `ReportProblem`. The profile of a learner who gave consent themselves is deleted by an adult's `DeleteProfile` too: the account is the owner's (R21 api), and `app` says so before that. Deletion leaves problem reports until their period, without an ID (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R123). `GetAccount` does not show what was withdrawn or cancelled: of them only the minimal record remains, without the account ID (R117).
- **Cancelling** — `CancelChildConsent`, at a consent without a profile: a waiting one is erased whole, with the scan (R117), and a confirmed one is cancelled as a withdrawal — with the minimal record and the scan for their period; neither counts toward the limit any more. The limit is `CAUSE_TOO_MANY_CONSENTS`, `resource_exhausted`, without data; the number is kept by `api` (R11 api), a retry with the same key gets the same consent even at the limit (the 2026-11-09 amendment to R98).
- **Age and country anew** — `RestateAge`, by an adult action: when the country raised the age of digital consent (`CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED`; R134), at the yearly confirmation, which `Profile.age_check_due` marks a year later, and with a change of country (privacy 3.3). A category that needs another consent leaves the profile waiting for it: the learner's own consent or a parental consent with a new code.
- **Storage of works** — `SetWorkStorage`: turning it on is a consent by `storage-consent` of whoever consents for the learner (R113, R127), and for a learner who gives consent themselves — by their own learning request; the wrong kind of action gets `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED` or the new cause `CAUSE_LEARNER_DECIDES`. The record lives as long as the profile lives.
- **Text version** — `LegalTextRef`, which the request that gives consent takes from `GetLegalTexts` (R130, R131); one not current — `CAUSE_TEXT_NOT_CURRENT`. `RequestChildConsent` and `RestateAge` always name `parent-consent` while the text has a version in force: who gives consent only `api` computes, and it writes the version only into a parental consent.
- **"Report a problem"** — `AttemptService.ReportProblem`, by a learning request from the task screen (to whom `app` shows the button — П-26): which answer and rung, the words as `app` showed them, a word of the closed set and a text; the answer is an ID and the review period, 3 days (R132). `api` stores it until the review and a year after (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R123).
- **The operator's commands** — to confirm or not accept a form, to read and close a report — are a decision of `api` (R34 api).
- **Export** — version 1 of the part `export/` carries all this (R135).

— *Why:* without these methods the operator has nothing to confirm consent with, a teenager nothing to give their own with, and an adult nothing to withdraw and cancel a waiting one with; the first child waits for the consent contract (dpia 8), and `api` and `app` for one release of the epic E4 (Д144, Д169, Д174).

— *Rejected:* a mail to the operator with a scan, and paper by post (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R116); `consent_id` on the form; the repeated question of age as a task of its own — `api` would wait for it longer (Д174); version 2 of the export (R135); only an adult exports (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R132); report periods of 90 days and 3 years (the 2026-11-10 amendment to R123); choosing a payment provider now.

— *Consequence:* `account.proto`, `attempt.proto`, `cause.proto`, `legal.proto` and [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15; [the part `export/`](../export/README.md); privacy 3.3, 4, 7.1 and 9 — П-28; [DPIA](dpia.md), version 6; the drafts of `privacy-policy` and `parent-consent`; RUN.md — T103 and rows of table 4.

— *Amendment 2026-11-11:* **a teenager who has grown to the age of digital consent under a parental consent also withdraws it: `WithdrawOwnConsent` is valid at a profile that waits for the learner's own consent, `CONSENT_NEED_OWN`, and deletes the profile, as `DeleteProfile` does; `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED` — only at a profile whose consent an adult gave and which does not wait for the learner's own consent. Storage of works turned on by an adult `app` offers to the teenager after the confirmation on a separate screen: the consent is the teenager's `SetWorkStorage`, which, for storage turned on by an adult, is not a repeat but a record of their own consent in place of the adult's; a refusal turns storage off and erases the copies, and `app` offers the export before that.** The author's answers during T112 (R141): R116 and the texts promise "confirm or withdraw", and New York's law requires a teenager's separate consent to what learning does not need (GBL §899-ff). Rejected: only confirm; leave storage on; turn it off at once.

— *Amendment 2026-11-15:* **the requests that neither `CAUSE_NO_CONSENT` nor `CAUSE_AGE_NEEDED` refuses also include `DeleteWork`, which goes as turning the storage off goes, and the learner's `ListWorks` and `GetWork`, which go as the learner's `ExportProfile` goes (R113; R151).** The row «в реестр spec» `api` В68, the inbox triage at the end of E12. — RUN.md, T160 and T161.

**R137. The NovaTrail operator in the texts is ALT EdTech LLC, the author's company, formed in Texas: the address, telephone and email are the company's; the terms are governed by the law of Texas, and a dispute is heard by the courts of Bexar County, Texas, — without mandatory arbitration and without a waiver of class actions. П-27 is closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 while T109 was planned (RUN.md); the 2026-11-10 amendment to R131.
- **The operator is the company**, not the author personally: the liability is on the company. Rejected: the author personally — they would be liable themselves, and changing the operator later means new versions of all texts and a transfer of data.
- **The data** — in the section "Who we are" of [the policy](../legal/texts/privacy-policy/1.md): ALT EdTech LLC, 12828 Willow Centre Dr, Ste D, Houston, TX 77066-3043, USA; +1 224 933 2890; `altedtech.info@gmail.com`, as code. This is asked for by COPPA — "The name, address, telephone number, and email address of all operators collecting or maintaining personal information from children through the website or online service" (16 CFR §312.4(d)(1), [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-312/section-312.4), read 2026-11-10) — and by GDPR Art. 13(1)(a) (R131). These are the data of a company, not of a person: in the public repository and in every release they stand by the author's choice. The email is a consumer Gmail, without a processor agreement with Google, — the open question П-29, before the policy is approved.
- **The address is the company's.** The rule does not name the kind of address, and the FTC's FAQ, C.2, repeats its words ([Complying with COPPA: FAQ](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/complying-coppa-frequently-asked-questions), the live page, read 2026-11-10; before, the site answered 403, privacy 10); where the FTC needs a kind, it names it — ""Valid physical postal address" means the sender's current street address, a Post Office box the sender has accurately registered with the United States Postal Service, or a private mailbox…" (16 CFR §316.2(p), CAN-SPAM, [eCFR](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-316/section-316.2), read 2026-11-10). Whether a mailbox is fit for COPPA neither the rule nor the FAQ says — Claude's reading (R112), — and the company's address removes this question. Rejected: a mailbox — not confirmed; a home address — forever in a public repository.
- **Law and court** — in the section "Law and disputes" of [the terms](../legal/texts/terms-of-use/1.md): the law of the State of Texas; the state courts in Bexar County or the federal court of the Western District of Texas, San Antonio Division, which Bexar belongs to — "The San Antonio Division comprises the counties of Atascosa, Bandera, Bexar, …" (28 U.S.C. §124(d)(4), [LII](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/28/124), read 2026-11-10), — unless the law of the user's country or state gives them the right to sue where they live; the consumer's rights under the law of their country the terms do not take away anyway. The court is by the author's choice, separate from the address: Houston is in Harris County, the Southern District of Texas. Rejected: mandatory arbitration with a waiver of class actions — a longer text and stricter to the family.
- **The state of formation** the author chose; T109 did not analyse it: it is a question of taxes and residence, not of learners' data. Which laws of Texas and other states concern the platform — T107.

— *Why:* without the operator and the law neither the policy nor the terms come into force (COPPA §312.4(d)(1); GDPR Art. 13(1)(a)), and `app` E3 — the first deployment with adults — waits for them.

— *Consequence:* the drafts of `privacy-policy` and `terms-of-use` of version 1 and their gist in [the passport](../legal/legal.yaml); privacy 2, 7.1, 9 — П-27 and П-29 — and 10; RUN.md — T109, T110, T111 and T107.

"Which laws of Texas and other states concern the platform — T107" is R140: of Texas, the rules for a small business (§541.002) and the breach procedure of §521.053; beside them, the laws of New York, Connecticut, Colorado, Montana and Arkansas on minors, Rhode Island's rule on the controller and the biometrics laws of Colorado and Washington, each fulfilled for all learners from the US (privacy 3.4).** — R138, R140; R143; RUN.md, T164.

**R138. The texts for adults — `privacy-policy`, `terms-of-use` and `storage-consent` version 1 — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions they rest on; the operator's mail stays consumer Gmail, `altedtech.info@gmail.com`, and the policy names Google as its recipient under Google's own terms, without a processor agreement, and asks not to write a child's data in letters; people's letters to the operator are kept a year after the letter or the last answer to it. П-29 is closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 in the planning of T110 (RUN.md); the approval is the author's, by R112.
- **The reconciliation.** The drafts were written before R136, the 2026-11-10 amendments and R137, and the reconciliation before the approval found 31 discrepancies — 21 of them such that the text in force would have said something other than what was decided —, all corrected before the approval: a version in force does not change by a byte (`legal.in-force-unchanged`):
  - parental consent — a form with the consent request code, the upload of a scan in `app`; a check by card is not promised, it is П-28 (R116, R136);
  - a teenager: the profile — at once, their own consent, they decide the storage of their work and the export themselves, withdrawal deletes the profile (R113, R116, R132, R136);
  - the age asked anew — every year, with a change of country and when the country raised the age; the country's age by which the category is given (R134, R136);
  - what remains after the withdrawal and the removal of consent, and the scan of a removed waiting consent (R117, R136);
  - disclosure — "to nobody, except as the law requires", and the basis when life is threatened, Arts. 6(1)(d) and 9(2)(c) (R123, R127);
  - the problem report and the letters to the operator — in what is collected, and in the retention periods (R123, R136);
  - the providers of the samples and who sees the IP address of the samples page (R125, R133); the volunteer's form — kept without a time limit while the samples are published (R126);
  - the terms name ALT EdTech LLC (R137) and do not accept learners from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom until there are representatives (R131); the storage consent — who stores, where and why, and the consent record (R113, R116).
- **The mail** is the company's consumer Gmail, and the policy says so plainly: in "Who receives data" — a separate table of the recipients not under a processor agreement, in "Who we are" and "Children" — a request not to write a child's data in letters, and to do the export, deletion and withdrawal in the app. There is no processor agreement for Gmail: the Cloud Data Processing Addendum covers "an Agreement for Google Workspace or Cloud Identity" ([Google](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum), read 2026-11-10), not Gmail. This is the author's answer: they are not ready to pay for Workspace yet. *Cost:* Google keeps people's letters as it decides itself, not under an agreement with the operator. For children this is not enough: before someone keeps a child's data for the operator, COPPA requires the operator to "obtain written assurances that such entities will employ reasonable measures to maintain the confidentiality, security, and integrity of the information" (16 CFR [§312.8(c)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-312/section-312.8), read 2026-11-10), and whether Google's consumer terms count as such assurances has not been checked; for learners from the EU and the United Kingdom, GDPR Art. 28 requires a processor under an agreement. Therefore **Gmail — only while adults learn**: before the first child, the mail moves to a service with a processor agreement, and the new address comes with a new version of the policy, with T112 (dpia 8). While there are no children, there must be no child's data in letters, and the policy asks not to write it anyway. *Rejected:* Google Workspace on the company's domain, under the Cloud Data Processing Addendum, — the recommendation, which has to be paid for; another mail service with an agreement — a new processor and money too.
- **The retention of letters** — a year after the letter or after the last answer to it, whichever is later: to show what the operator answered to a request about rights and when (GDPR Arts. 5(2), 12(3)) — the same year as for the problem report. Rejected: 30 days after the answer — there would be nothing to show that the request was fulfilled; 3 years — a child's data in letters would live longer.
- **The basis of letters and problem reports** — the legitimate interest in answering, in protecting learners from harm and in showing that an answer was given (GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)); an answer to a request about rights is also an obligation under the GDPR (Art. 6(1)(c)). This is Claude's reading (R112): there was no decision about it, and the reconciliation found that Art. 13(1)(c) asks for the basis of each purpose.
- **The age boundary** — "from this age", not "above it": a learner exactly at the age of digital consent of their country consents themselves (R136).
- **The mail at Google** is in data centers of Google's choosing: the policy does not promise where Gmail keeps the letters.
- **The approval** — the author reads the final texts and writes «утверждаю» ("I approve"), and `in_force_since` is the day of this word.

— *Why:* `app` E3, the first deployment with adults, waits for the policy and the terms in force: while no version is in force, `GetLegalTexts` gives an empty list.

— *Consequence:* [the part `legal/`](../legal/README.md) — three versions in force; privacy 2, 4, 7.1 and 9 — П-29; [DPIA](dpia.md), version 7; RUN.md — T110 and the rows of table 4.

The text sets of the samples page `measure` and `eval-set` version 1 — the notices `measure-notice` and `eval-set-notice`, the forms `measure-form` and `volunteer-form` — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions; the controller of the samples and the forms is ALT EdTech LLC, and the organizer acts for it, on its instructions; an eval-set sample can always be withdrawn: before it is entered into the module's repository, it is erased, and after that it leaves the next version of the module and its tests, while the released versions and others' copies remain; the organizer takes no volunteers from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom until the representatives are named.** The author's answers of 2026-11-10 in the execution of T111 (RUN.md), all by the recommendations; the 2026-11-10 amendments to R126 and R131; the approval is the author's, by R112.
- **The controller** is the operator, ALT EdTech LLC (R137): each of the four texts names it and its contacts, as GDPR Art. 13(1)(a) requires (R131), while before they said only "the operator". The organizer — the maintainer of `modules` or of the measurement, now the author — acts for the operator, on its instructions: there is one controller. Rejected: the organizer on their own — a second recipient or a joint controller, whom the texts would have to name, and an agreement between them.
- **Withdrawal** — by a letter to both the organizer and the operator, by the writer code in the measurement (Art. 7(3); the 2026-11-09 amendment to R124); one who lost the code — by the name and the date of the form; for an eval-set sample — by the name and the date of the form, within 30 days: one not yet entered into the module's repository is erased, and one entered leaves the next version of the module and its tests, while the released versions and others' copies under Apache-2.0 remain; the form lives while the sample is in the repository or in a released version (R126). The basis stays consent (Art. 6(1)(a)), as in the policy in force, and a withdrawal under Art. 7(3) stops what the platform itself does. Rejected: withdrawing nothing after publication — against Art. 7(3); the basis being a contract (Art. 6(1)(b)) — the policy in force says "consent", and its version 2 would have been needed before the sets.
- **Volunteers from the EU, the EEA and the United Kingdom** — as with learners (R131): until there are representatives under Art. 27, the organizer does not take their forms, and the form asks to declare this. Rejected: accepting them — Art. 27 requires a representative for them too.
- **Model training** — the platform trains no model of its own on eval-set samples (the 2026-11-09 amendment to R126), but after publication under Apache-2.0 anyone takes them, as the license allows, for training too: the former "not for training a model" promised what cannot be held to (R124).

Rejected: all the laws of all the states — longer, and most general laws do not concern a small operator; only Texas.

- **What concerns it now and what is missing** — privacy 3.4:

  - Texas, §521.053: the procedure in a breach — 60 days for people, 30 for the attorney general from 250 residents (Д200);

**R141. The texts for the family — `parent-consent`, `teen-consent`, `child-notice` and `teen-notice` version 1 — come into force after a reconciliation with the decisions and the state laws; with them come version 2 of `privacy-policy`, with the US consumer rights, and its translation into Russian, for which the part `legal/` gets translations of versions, by its version 2; and version 2 of the set `measure`, where a volunteer declares that they do not live in Colorado or Washington. The operator's mail stays Gmail for families too, and a teenager who has reached the age of digital consent can also withdraw the parent's consent.** The author's answers of 2026-11-11 in the planning and the execution of T112 (RUN.md); the 2026-11-11 amendments to R130, R136 and R138; the approval is the author's, by R112.
- **The reconciliation.** The drafts were written before R136–R140, and the reconciliation found 24 discrepancies, 10 of them such that the text in force would have said something other than what was decided. All were corrected before the approval:
  - not one text for the family named the controller and its contacts — now there is the section "Who we are", as in the text sets of the samples page (R139), and in the texts for the learner the company's name;
  - not one named the basis — now there is the section "Why we may": Arts. 6(1)(a) and 8, the check under COPPA, the record after deletion — Arts. 7(1) and 17(3)(e);
  - what remains after withdrawal was incomplete: the scan of the form, the problem report and the letters to the operator remain too (R117, R123, R136, R138);
  - `child-notice` said "Nobody else can see it", while the operator reads a problem report with the tutor's words — now this is said too;
  - `teen-consent` did not say that an adult can delete the profile too (R136), did not name the recipients, and reduced "what remains" to the consent record;
  - the gist of `parent-consent` and of `teen-notice` said less than the text;

- **The mail is Gmail for good, and for families with children too** — the author's answer, the 2026-11-11 amendment to R138: there will be no processor agreement for the mail. The texts for the family and the policy ask not to write a child's data in letters; what the app can do — in the app; the rest — by a letter from the address one signs in with, naming nothing about the child: by the sign-in address the operator finds the account. The risk is the new risk 18 of the DPIA, which the author accepted. *Rejected* — the services with a processor agreement, by their sites, read 2026-11-11: [Fastmail](https://www.fastmail.com/pricing/) — $5 a month when paid for a year, an address without a domain of one's own, [an agreement](https://www.fastmail.com/policies/dpa/) with erasure within 14 days after closing; [Proton Mail Plus](https://proton.me/mail/pricing) — $2.49 a month, but its [agreement](https://proton.me/legal/dpa) sets no erasure period; Zoho Mail Lite and Google Workspace — only with a domain of one's own, which there is not (О-16), and Google's Cloud Data Processing Addendum gives erasure within up to 180 days.
- **A teenager who has reached the age of digital consent under the parent's consent** confirms it by `GiveOwnConsent` or withdraws it by `WithdrawOwnConsent`, which until now refused them with `CAUSE_ADULT_NEEDED`, — the author's answer, the 2026-11-11 amendment to R136: the texts, the policy in force and R116 (EDPB 05/2020, paras. 147–149) promise "confirm or withdraw", and withdrawal is as easy as consent (Art. 7(3)). *Rejected:* only confirming, while an adult can delete the profile, — the promise would have to be taken back.
- **The storage of work turned on by the adult, after the teenager's confirmation** — `app` asks the teenager about it on a separate screen, a refusal turns storage off and erases the copies on the server, and `app` offers the export before that — the author's answer, the 2026-11-11 amendment to R136: the New York law requires a separate consent of a teenager to what learning does not need (GBL §899-ff; R140). *Rejected:* leaving it on — there is no consent of the teenager to it; turning it off at once — it erases what the teenager may have wanted.
- **At 18** the texts say only that `app` will tell the learner that the protection the law gives minors no longer applies to them (GBL §899-hh(2): "shall provide notice to such user that such user is no longer covered by the protections and rights provided under this article", [NY Senate](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-HH), read 2026-11-11). What then happens to the profile of an adult in someone else's account — a move to their own account or a new consent — is open question П-31. *Rejected:* deciding the move now — a change of the contract and the decisions, more than the task.
- **Requests about a child that the app cannot handle** — correction (Arkansas, A.C.A. §4-88-1503(b)(3)–(4)) and access beyond the export: by a letter from the sign-in address, without the child's data, and a method of its own for the request in the app is open question П-32, by the public launch. *Rejected:* a method now — a change of the contract before the first child, with no need for it.
- **The US consumer rights in version 2 of the policy.** The Connecticut law with amendment PA 25-113 has been in effect since 2026-07-01 also for whoever "control or process consumers' sensitive data" (CGS §42-516(2)), and the data of a known child are sensitive (§42-515(39)(D)), with no threshold and no small-business exemption ([2026 Supplement, ch. 743jj](https://www.cga.ct.gov/2026/sup/chap_743jj.htm), read 2026-11-11). By R140 this is fulfilled for everyone in the US:
  - the rights of §42-518(a): to know and to see — with inferences, that is with the learner model; to correct; to delete; a copy; to opt out of targeted advertising, of sale and of profiling with significant effects; to contest such profiling; the list of buyers — the platform does none of these things, and says so;
  - the answer — 45 days, and another 45 with a notice within the first 45 (§42-518(c)(1)); free of charge once in 12 months, (c)(3); the check that it is the owner who asks — by a letter from the sign-in address, (c)(4), and no new account is needed (§42-520(c)(1));
  - the appeal — by the same way, an answer in writing within 60 days, and with a refusal, how to complain to the attorney general of Connecticut (§42-518(d)) — by the form of that office, subject "Consumer Data Privacy" ([CT AG](https://portal.ct.gov/ag/common/complaint-form-landing-page), read 2026-11-11);
  - the notice of §42-520(b)(1): there are no sales and no targeted advertising; a statement on the training of large language models, (H); the month and year of the last change, (I);
  - Arkansas, Act 952 (from 2026-07-01): correction at the request of a parent or of a teenager of 13–16 ([Act 952](https://www.arkleg.state.ar.us/Home/FTPDocument?path=%2FACTS%2F2025R%2FPublic%2FACT952.pdf), read 2026-11-11);
  - Texas: a small business does not owe the rights of the TDPSA (Bus. & Com. Code §541.002(a)(3)) — the policy says so, and gives the rights anyway;
  - New York, §899-ff, -hh, -ii: a separate consent screen for what is optional, with refusal as the most prominent choice and without asking again for a year; a notice at 18; a device signal counts as a refusal ([NY Senate, §899-II](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-II), read 2026-11-11);
  - the heartbeat of the sign-in SDK (`app` row В48) — in the row "Signing in" and in the retention periods; the two phrases about samples — by R139.
- **The translation of the policy into Russian.** CGS §42-520(b)(2) requires the notice "in each language in which the controller … provides any product or service", and `app` speaks `en` and `ru` (R92). The author's answer — the translation in this task. The part `legal/` gets translations of versions, by its version 2 (the 2026-11-11 amendment to R130): the field `translations` of a text version and the file `texts/<id>/<n>.<tag>.md`, which the rules `legal.files`, `legal.markdown` and `legal.in-force-unchanged` hold too; `GetLegalTexts` gives the translation into the language of the screen, in the fields `translation` and `translation_language`; the types are `types/legalv2`, and the npm package from line 0.15 on has `./legalv2` instead of `./legalv1`; the part's version starts line 0.15. A translation has no force: the English is in force, and a consent names the version, not the translation. *Rejected:* the translation as a task of its own — without it the policy in force would not fulfill the Connecticut law for a Russian screen; a Russian interface not for the US — a change of `app` and О-2.
- **The set `measure` version 2** — `measure-notice` and `measure-form` version 2: the organizer takes no forms from those who live in Colorado or Washington, and the form asks to declare this (R140; Д202).
- **The set `child-sample`** is not here: the operator has no bucket for it yet (Д156), and texts in force would describe a storage that does not exist. T117 introduces it, when `infra` creates the bucket — the author's answer.
- **П-30 is checked** against GBL §899-gg by the primary sources 2026-11-11 ([§899-GG](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/899-GG)): the law requires an agreement with instructions, help with deletion, information and audits, notice of new processors, erasure on the operator's instruction with the instruction passed on, and a confirmation of erasure within 30 days of the request. All four — [OpenAI](https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/openai-data-processing-addendum.pdf), [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com/legal/data-processing-addendum), [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/terms/data-processing-addendum) with Firebase and [Neon at Databricks](https://www.databricks.com/sites/default/files/legal/dpa-20230721.pdf) — lack the confirmation of erasure within 30 days and the passing of the instruction to their own processors; OpenAI and Anthropic lack erasure on instruction too, Google erases within up to 180 days, Neon only on a written request. П-30 stays open: the operator asks each of them for an addendum, before the first child (privacy 9).
- **Not checked against the primary source:** "commercial purposes" for a free service in Arkansas; whether a SOC 2 report is enough for §899-gg(5)(d); the web page of OpenAI's agreement gave 403, and the PDF on its CDN was read; the rules of the New York attorney general under the child data law are not final.

— *Why:* `app` E3 waits for the texts for the family, and the first child from the US waits for what the state laws require of the policy (R140; dpia 8).

**R142. The measurement of E10 weighs the spending of Claude Code sessions by the prices of Anthropic's API, not by shares of the subscription's limit; once, on the trial T119, the weight is checked against the share of the limit that `/usage` shows.** The author's answer of 2026-11-11 to Т-39, by the recommendation (RUN.md, T118).
- NovaTrail's sessions run on the author's subscription, and Anthropic does not publish how the subscription counts spending: the help names the five-hour and the weekly limits and what spending depends on, but there is no formula that would turn cache reads, writes and output into a share of the limit (Т-39, repositories 8, with quotes and a date).
- The weight of a call is by the prices of repositories 9.2, which `tools/tokens/prices.mjs` holds; `just tokens-report` prints it in dollars.
- The check is on the trial T119: the share of the limit from `/usage` before and after each run, beside its weight by the prices. If the shares do not follow the weight, an amendment to this entry follows.

— *Why:* the prices are published by the primary source, and the measurement can be repeated in any repository without the author, while `/usage` is read only by a session that is signed in. *Rejected:* always measuring by the shares of `/usage` — they cannot be restored from the transcripts, and the line of repositories 9.3 could not be recomputed; only tokens, without weights, — they would add cache reads to output, which for Opus 5.5 is 100 times dearer: $0.20 against $20 per million.

*Amendment 2026-11-11 (T119), the author's answer at the trial:* `/usage` cannot be read from `claude -p` — neither by a field of its JSON nor by a command —, so the check was made not for each run but once, before and after the whole trial. The share of the limit over the window — +66 p.p. of the five-hour limit and +11 p.p. of the weekly one. The weight of all the sessions of this machine by API prices over the same window — ≈ $53–72 (repositories 9.4). So 1 p.p. of the five-hour limit of Max is no more than ≈ $0.8–1.1 at API prices, and of the weekly one ≈ $5–6.5. The weight by the prices stays, and the measurement of E10 converts it into shares of the limit by these numbers.

## Claude Code sessions

**R143. A session's tokens are saved by the order of its work and the structure of the documents, not by code-map tools: one task is one session, compaction at 400 thousand tokens, a thin CLAUDE.md, no claude.ai connectors, the body of a done task in the archive at once, the plan's tables and the records of sources and measurements in files of their own, `docs/` in English for the session that reads them, and a long run waited for without polling. gopls serves the diagnostics of Go code. How the savings are kept is R145.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-11 in the planning of T121, by the recommendations of measurements 1.4–1.6 but the translation, and their answers since on the sources (T133), the plugin (T134), the hook's forms (`.github` В37, T149) and long runs (`learner-model` В57, T198); the translation check and the plugin's loading are the executor's decisions of T135 and T162, on the author's word.
- **One task is one session.** A task's planning and execution run in one session; the next task starts in a new session or after `/clear`, and the inbox triage runs in the session it was started in (R81). The hook `UserPromptSubmit` of `tools/session/`, which `.claude/settings.json` of `spec` and of the template runs, stops a prompt that starts another task than the one the session has led, and names `/clear`. A task starts by RUN.md's phrases and the forms the author writes — «делай», «сделай», «делаем», «выполняй», «реализуй», «спланируй», «начинай», «приступай к реализации», «продолжай» —, each a whole word, with the task's number right after it or after «задачу», «задачи» or «реализацию»; a number followed by «.» or «-» and a digit, «T6.1», or by a question mark, «делаем T42?», starts nothing. «Сделай эпик E…» and its forms but planning start an epic, which the orchestrator's session leads as one task; «планируй эпик E…» starts nothing, and a Cyrillic «Т» or «Е» is no number. «Разбери входящие» names no task and goes on. An executor's run of the orchestrator is one task: a fresh `claude -p` is its `/clear`, `--resume` goes on with its own session, the hook runs in `-p` too (sources 2.11), and the numbers of `NOVATRAIL_RUN_TASKS` count as one task, so a run whose executor wrote its task under another number is resumed under either (R156).
- **Compaction at 400 thousand tokens**, by `autoCompactWindow` of `.claude/settings.json` of `spec` and of the template, which holds in a cloud session too, not by a variable of `containerEnv`.
- **A thin CLAUDE.md.** The checks of each part are its rule in `.claude/rules/`, with `paths`, loaded when the session reads or edits a file of the part and dropped by compaction; CLAUDE.md names the rules, and CI holds every check (measurements 1.8).
- **No claude.ai connectors**: `disableClaudeAiConnectors` in the project settings of every repository. The setting does not turn off the skills of plugins.
- **The archive at once.** A done task's body and its gist sentence go to its epic's archive in `docs/plan/` at once, and table 1 keeps its row; the tables of the plan other than table 1 are files of `run/`, of which a task reads the rows it and its files name (R153; rule 2 of RUN.md).
- **Sources and measurements.** The records of external facts are `docs/sources.md`, the results of measurements `docs/measurements.md`; a claim cites its one record as a section, `sources 5.4`, from another repository `sources 5.4 spec`, not a chain of records and the texts that also cite them (R171), and `docs/architecture.md` holds neither (RULES.md, The bar and How we work). In `spec`, architecture 8, privacy 10, product 14 and repositories 9 are pointers to them, for the texts that cite those sections; dpia 9 stays in the DPIA, which is handed over whole (R129).
- **The reader of `docs/`** is a Claude Code session that acts for an engineer, a module author or a lawyer without asking what was meant: the bar of RULES.md holds, the structure is chosen for reading in parts, and the texts people read are those RULES.md, The bar, names (R42, R154).
- **`docs/` are in English** in every repository (R14): a quote of a source keeps its language, the prefixes О-, П-, Т-, Д and В stay Cyrillic, and the numbers of entries and sections do not change. A translation is no rewrite. `translation-check` compares it with its original at a commit, unit by unit — a heading of the same level and number, a paragraph, a list item at its depth, a cell, a block of code —, and in each pair the citations, links, numbers, code, quotes of English text and the fixed words of the log (`tools/translation/vocabulary.mjs`) match; a citation or a number gone into another unit is an error. A fresh subagent that did not translate reads a sample chosen by the hash of the commit before, a tenth of the document, and names every difference of meaning. The order of a translation, by subagents of Opus, is [tools/translation/README.md](../tools/translation/README.md).
- **A long run** — tests, a simulation, a build, CI — goes to the background in a session a person leads, which waits for its notification or a Monitor of its condition, never a loop of `sleep` in the foreground (RULES.md, How we work); the orchestrator's executor waits in the foreground instead (R159).
- **gopls.** The kind `go` of the template loads the plugin `gopls-lsp`, for the diagnostics after an edit, not for savings: by the key `claudePlugins` of `repo-template/kinds.json`, `new-repo` adds `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS`, `${containerWorkspaceFolder}/spec/claude-plugins/gopls-lsp`, to `containerEnv` of the copy's devcontainer. `claude-plugins/gopls-lsp/` holds the plugin's `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `LICENSE` byte for byte from commit `e37d307` of Anthropic's marketplace, Apache-2.0; the plugin runs the gopls the kind builds from its lock file (R102), and its version is the tag of `spec`. `new-repo-check` finds each folder the variable names inside the workspace, and refuses in `.claude/settings.json` a marketplace in a local folder, a plugin turned on from `novatrail` and one the variable already loads. A plugin of the variable replaces a marketplace plugin of the same name, so a repository with the variable and the old keys starts one gopls; on a copy whose `spec` is a tag before T162, `new-repo-check` says to take a tag with T162. In a cloud session the language server does not start. The trials are measurements 1.10 and sources 2.7, 2.10.

— *Why:*
- A session's spending is set by what it has gathered: it starts at 41–45 thousand tokens, and a call's context averages 218–294 thousand. One session per task would have cut the context of the main sessions of E4 and E9 by 51%; both ran in one session though RUN.md asked for new ones, so the hook holds the rule. Compaction overlaps with it; the thin CLAUDE.md saves 5,090 tokens a call, ≈ 2%; the connectors and the list of skills carry ≈ 10 thousand tokens a call (measurements 1.5).
- The hook takes the forms the author writes: «делай» stands before a task number in 157 of the author's prompts, more than «выполни задачу», and none of the 230 prompts the forms add only names a task (measurements 1.7).
- The structure of the documents is second order, ≈ 4.4% of what is carried: the archive ≤ 1.9% across 13 repositories, table 4 in a file ≤ 3.9% for `spec`, the sources ≤ 0.8% (measurements 1.6). One rule for every external fact is simpler than one for the architecture alone, and `docs-check` checks a record's number as a section without new code.
- English is the author's word: `docs/` are written for the agent, and English is 11.4% cheaper in tokens on seven sections (measurements 1.6). Without a check by machine a translation loses a link, a number or a condition unseen; unit by unit is the strictest check without a model, and it keeps the structure citations rely on.
- Each turn of a polling loop rereads the whole context: T61 `learner-model` waited so in 76 main calls, $3.08 of the session's $14.62 (measurements 10 learner-model); one sentence every session reads costs far less.
- The plugin's version is the tag of `spec`, with neither network nor installation. The variable is one container's environment and `${containerWorkspaceFolder}` its own path, so no session depends on which container ran before it or on the trust of its folder, while a marketplace is recorded in `~/.claude`, which all NovaTrail containers share, by the path of the container that recorded it last (sources 2.10).

— *Rejected:*
- code-map tools — Serena, graphify, claude-context, repomix, ast-grep, aider's map: on the trial of T119 none is cheaper than `grep` and `Read`, LSP is +9%, graphify +25% on code and +32% on documents, and the graph of `spec`'s documents takes 69 minutes and ≈ $7–25 (measurements 1.4);
- a consolidation of the decisions in force beside the log — 0.5–0.7% for a second copy that every change drags after it; R160 rewrites the entry in its place instead (measurements 1.6, 1.14.5);
- a file per section, an entry per file, a table of contents of the log, shorter cards of architecture 3 — reads are partial anyway, and anchors and links break (measurements 1.6);
- a cheap model for subagents — Haiku was right 0 times of 3; a map of the repository in the rules — 0.65%; skills in `.claude/skills/`; a shorter output of checks — 0.1%; a shorter MEMORY.md — 0.7%; compaction at 300 thousand — −61% instead of −51%, but 18 compactions instead of 11 and more details lost (measurements 1.5);
- `docs/` left in Russian, as T125 recommended — ≈ 0.8% in all, for ≈ $65 and an edit of every line: the author decided to translate;
- the sources of the architecture alone; dpia 9 moved too; a register of records of its own, «И-…» — new code and Cyrillic in English text; a link to an anchor — it breaks when a heading is edited or translated; the measurements left in `docs/repositories.md`;
- a translation compared by sections — a link gone into another unit would pass; a link gone away accepted — the translation would change the structure; a back-translation instead of the blind reading — twice as dear, and its own errors hide differences; a sample chosen by the translator; Sonnet 5 — slower and worse in terms on the pilot of T135;
- RUN.md's phrases alone in the hook — the author writes otherwise, and such a session passed; forms the author does not write, «сделаем», «начинаем», which ask in Russian; a verb a few words before a number — «делай как в T24» only names one;
- the rule of long runs in the RUN.md of `spec` and of the template — two homes; the description of the Bash tool alone — it did not hold in T61;
- `gopls-lsp@claude-plugins-official` — its `ref` takes no commit, the marketplace updates itself, and `"version": "1.0.0"` keeps the copy in the cache by Anthropic's choice; `settings` with `git-subdir` and `sha` — it pins the commit, but fetches the plugin over the network, and each clone needs `claude plugin install`; a marketplace of `spec` — a relative `directory`, `github` or `git` at a tag — its record in the shared `~/.claude` holds one container's path, a project's `enabledPlugins` installs nothing from an external source, and a tag would pin twice (sources 2.7, 2.10); `CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR` per container — it moves the whole plugin root, and the folder would still need trust; the variable in `env` of `.claude/settings.json` — Claude Code does not take it there; gopls in `spec`'s devcontainer — its Dockerfile is the base of every kind; `typescript-lsp`; no plugin — the trial showed the diagnostics.

— *Consequence:* `.claude/settings.json`; `tools/session/`; CLAUDE.md, `.claude/rules/`; `docs/sources.md`, `docs/measurements.md`; `tools/translation/`; `claude-plugins/`, `repo-template/kinds.json`, `tools/new-repo/`; RULES.md; repositories 2.2. — RUN.md, T121.

## Account deletion and the Google sign-in

**R144. Account deletion also removes the "Sign in with Google" connection in the owner's Google account: `app` revokes the Google access token that the fresh sign-in by the window before the deletion gives, and `api` does not get this token.** The author's answer of 2026-11-12 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В52 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` 77fbf21), its first option (the 2026-11-12 amendment to R21 api); the triage before T134.
- **What was found.** Deleting the user at the sign-in service does not remove the connection: after `DeleteAccount` the user is gone, but the dev project's connection stayed among the author's connected apps (T42 `api`). Google's help says nothing about this (sources 4.6).
- **How.** Deletion requires a fresh sign-in (R98; R20 api), and the sign-in by the window gives the Google access token. After the answer "deleted", `app` revokes it at `https://oauth2.googleapis.com/revoke`, and the revocation removes everything the owner granted the project (sources 4.6). The token lives only in the memory of `app`.
- **What `app` decides** (DEBT.md, Д221): how to send the request — Google's documentation prescribes a form, without CORS, while the trial of 2026-11-12 saw CORS in the response; what to add to `csp.json` (the third 2026-11-09 amendment to R85); what the screen says if the revocation failed.
- **The texts.** The policy of version 2 does not name the connection among what remains. With the revocation the connection is not there, and no new version is needed (R130). The DPIA does not change: the connection is data of the adult owner in their Google account, and dpia 3.1 and measure 6 of dpia 6.2 — "sign-in only through the Google window" — are the same (R129).

— *Why:* deletion requires a fresh sign-in anyway, the token is already in the memory of `app`, and a connection the policy is silent about would contradict the honest retention periods (privacy 1). *Rejected:* only writing down that the connection stays — version 3 of the policy would be needed; the revocation on the server — `api` would hold a Google token it does not need (privacy 1, minimization). — *Consequence:* architecture 3.12 and 4.5; sources 4.6; Д221.

— *Amendment 2026-11-15:* **"DEBT.md, Д221" above is the row Д221 of `run/DEBT.md`, which `DEBT.md` became (R153).** — R153; RUN.md, T165.

## Keeping the token savings

**R145. The savings of R143 are kept by three levels, from the cheapest: budgets of size in `docs-check` on every pull request, without a model; a measurement by `tokens-report --row` at each epic's archive and once a month; and a new analysis only by a threshold. The budgets are in bytes, in `tools/docs-check/budgets.json`, and a repository is checked by them once its root holds `docs-budgets.json`.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-12 in the planning of T126, by the recommendations, and of 2026-11-11 with epic E10, that a threshold calls the analysis rather than the calendar; and the author's answers since to the rows «в реестр spec» `tutor` В80 on a raise, `.github` В38 on `entries` and `learner-model` В56 on the first 80 calls (T199).
- **Budgets.** `docs-check` measures each whole file named, each rule of `.claude/rules/`, each entry of the decision log, the own text under each heading of a document cited by name — to the next heading, numbered or not — and above its first heading, and each row of a table of the files named. A limit is in KB of 1,024 bytes; `sections` gives a numbered section a limit of its own, and `entries` an entry, by its number, `{"R18": 56}`, `R4` being `R04`. Over the limit is an error that names the file, the size, the limit and the file the limit came from; raising a limit is an edit of that file, seen in review. A wrong file of budgets — an unknown key, a limit that is not a whole number of KB, a limit for a file, a section or an entry that does not exist — is an error, not a check turned off. A limit is set at the largest of its kind plus 10–20% (measurements 1.9), but for `entry`, 12 KB in `spec`: an entry longer keeps a limit of its own in `entries`, its size rounded up to the KB, until a task rewrites it by R160 and drops that limit. `format/`, `legal/` and the archives of `docs/plan/` have none. The same file holds the switch `"comments": true`, by which `docs-check` checks the numbers of decisions in comments of code (R32).
- **Another repository.** The block `repository` holds its limits, read from its `spec/` submodule, and its `docs-budgets.json` names what differs, `{}` when nothing does. Without that file `docs-check-repo` does not measure, so a move to a tag does not turn red before the repository writes the file by its own numbers; the template carries it from the start (repositories 2.2). Every repository has it now, and the check without it goes by Д276. The block holds `entry` 12 and `"comments": true`, as `spec`'s does, and a repository's entries longer than 12 KB keep their own limits in `entries` until a task rewrites them by R160. A limit of the block `repository` for `run/TASKS.md`, which a repository with no open task outside an epic lacks, is no error there; a limit of its own file for a file it does not have is one, and so is a limit of the block `spec` in `spec`.
- **The measurement.** At the archive of an epic, the repository's session runs `tokens-report --since <the first day of the epic> --row` and adds the row to its measurements; once a month a session of `spec` measures the folders of transcripts of all 13 repositories on this machine, from the window of the last row, and adds a row for each to measurements 1.9. The transcripts are on the machine where the work ran, so the measurement is a session there, not a cloud task on a schedule. `just inbox` prints the date of the monthly measurement and of the quarterly check once it has come, from measurements 1.9; it runs on the author's word or once every task of the current epic is done (R81), so a monthly row may come later than its date. Beside the context of a main call, `tokens-report` prints that of the main calls among the first 80 of each session, in its report, its `--json` and the last column of `--row`, so that a table that has not taken the column keeps the others in place.
- **The threshold.** A task of analysis goes into `run/TASKS.md` (R155) when the context of a main call is more than 25% above the repository's reference, over at least 300 main calls; or when a budget was raised three times since the last analysis, by `git log` of the file of budgets; or when a quarter has passed since the last check of Claude Code's changelog — what new means of saving it brings. A raise is a commit of a file of budgets that raises one limit or more, counted once; a repository's first `docs-budgets.json`, a limit held only until a translation and a lowering are none. An analysis by the first condition starts from the context of the first 80 calls: at the reference or below it, the excess is the length of tasks, which rule 11 of RUN.md splits. Its planning decides whether an epic is needed. The references, the last analysis and the dates are measurements 1.9.

— *Why:*
- An analysis reads the documents of 13 repositories, so a weekly one spends what it saves, and frequent restructuring breaks the citations of sections and the structure the sessions rely on; it goes by occasion, like the review of the DPIA (R129).
- Bytes, since the check runs in CI, which has no key, and the lower bound of bytes per token (measurements 1.6) keeps a limit in bytes from letting more tokens through than meant.
- A repository by its own file: the other repositories' documents were far over `spec`'s limits — RUN.md up to 228 KB, `docs/architecture.md` up to 791 KB (measurements 1.6) —, and the limits would have made their move to the tag red.
- An entry with dated amendments keeps its size until a task touches it and rewrites it (R160), and one long entry would raise `entry` for every entry of its log: `.github` raised it to 50 KB for R18, `sim` to 90 for R04.
- `entry` 12 KB, not the largest plus a margin: an entry by R160 holds its text in force alone, and all but 42 of `spec`'s 160 entries fit it (RUN.md, T205); a margin over the longest would let each new entry grow to 40 KB.
- Every repository's first file set limits measured after its restructuring — `tutor`'s six, `app`'s eight —, before any document grew, and counted as a raise it would call an analysis that finds nothing.
- Epic E8 of `learner-model` was 35% above its reference while its first 80 calls were 4.5% below it: the whole excess was three long sessions (measurements 10 learner-model).

— *Rejected:*
- a weekly analysis with restructuring — the reasons above;
- counting tokens through the API — a key in CI, a call over the network on every run, and a check that turns red when the tokenizer changes; through `claude -p` — money on every pull request;
- `spec`'s limits in every repository at once, `entry` 12 and the comments too — a move to the tag would turn red before the task that rewrites the repository's entries and comments;
- only `spec` measured monthly, reminded by the rule alone — the rule rests on the session's memory, and the other repositories would have no "before";
- one `entry` for all, the second option of В38;
- a repository's first file as one raise — two more edits would call an analysis in `tutor` and `app`; each limit raised as a raise;
- the threshold by the context of the first 80 calls — a text read late in a session would no longer reach it; no such number — each analysis would count it by a script of its own;
- a check in `docs-check` that a decision that changes another rewrites it too (R160) — without a model it cannot tell an entry that changes another from one that cites it, and it would only add noise; review keeps the rule;
- a check that a consolidation of the decisions is lossless, and that tables of contents are fresh — R143 took neither.

— *Consequence:* `tools/docs-check/` — `budgets.json`, `budgets.mjs`, `comments.mjs`, `config.mjs`, `main.mjs` and tests (R32); `tools/tokens/` — `--row` and the first 80 calls; `tools/inbox/due.mjs`; measurements 1.9; RUN.md, Epics, and rule 13; the template — `docs-budgets.json` and its RUN.md (repositories 2.2); CLAUDE.md, Environment; `.claude/rules/tools.md`. — RUN.md, T126; run/TASKS.md, T199.

## Checks without the author

**R146. The executor runs the checks of a task without the author: the path in the browser — with Playwright in the devcontainer, signed in on a local build by a custom token of a conventional user; the paid calls of AI — on a stub of `tutor` in the dev mode of `api`, and a real call only where the task checks the model's words, under a spending limit the author sets once at the provider and a cap the task names; and on real devices nothing: the three engines in CI are the check. Rule 4 of RUN.md gets that exception, and the template with it. В34 of RUN.md is closed.** The author's answers of 2026-11-12 to the rows «в реестр spec» `app` В52, В58 and В59 (RUN.md of `app`, `main` 55ab358) and `api` В57 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` 6ca0caf); В52 — the triage's option, В57 — by its recommendation, В58 — by the triage's refinement, В59 — not by the recommendation: the triage advised a survey of device farms. They rest on the author's word to `app` of 2026-11-12: by hand the author walks nothing — no path, no confirmation of each call, no device.
- **The path.** The scenario lives in the repository whose screens it walks, `app`, and runs in its devcontainer, where the browser is (R79). A local build of `app` signs in by `signInWithCustomToken` with a token that a tool of `api` issues for a conventional user on the dev project, as R39 api does for `dev-check`; a release build has no such sign-in. `api` is reached by its name in the network of Docker (RUN.md, T115). The Google window stays for the deployment.
- **The calls of AI.** A run of the path calls the stub of `tutor` in the dev mode of `api`, which `api` refuses outside that mode, as R32 api refuses the emulator. A real call goes only where the task checks the words of the model: on a dev key that has its own spending limit at the provider, set once by the author — as each eval key has (R120) —, and under a cap in the task's text; the task's «Сделано» names what was spent. Anything else that costs money still waits for the author's confirmation by rule 4.
- **Devices.** Chromium, WebKit and Firefox in CI (RUN.md, T141; Д217) are the check of the engines. What only a device shows — the pen, the voices of the device, VoiceOver and TalkBack, the Home screen — the executor does not check, and `app` keeps it as its debt until the author decides otherwise.

— *Why:* a check that waits for the author does not run: the walks of T30 and T35 `app` passed only part of the path (Д14 app). A token signed by Firebase checks the real path of the sign-in, revocation included, and needs no amendment to R32 api; a stub costs nothing and calls no provider with a learner's work; a limit at the provider holds even when a session miscounts. *Rejected:*
- for the sign-in — the emulator of Firebase Auth: it does not verify a token's signature, and `api` refuses to start with it (R03 and R32 api); Playwright in the author's browser over CDP — the profile would hold the author's sign-in; walks by hand;
- for the calls — a cap held by the executor alone, a limit at the provider alone, a confirmation of each call;
- for devices — a farm of devices now: its price and what it can do were not read from primary sources, and a Google sign-in on a farm needs an account of its own; walks by hand.

— *Consequence:* rule 4 of RUN.md and of the template (repositories 2.2); Д226 and Д227; RUN.md, T146.

— *Amendment 2026-11-13 (inbox triage, `tutor` В83):* **"where the task checks the model's words" covers every paid run of eval: what it measures is what a model answers — the words, the reading of a sheet or an assessment by a rubric. The executor starts such a run itself, on an eval key whose workspace has the author's spending limit (R120) and under the cap the task names, and «Сделано» names what was spent. What a run may send stays what its eval set admits — its samples, their consents and the providers of admission (R124, R125) —, and anything else that costs money still waits for the author by rule 4.** The author's answer of 2026-11-13 to the row «в реестр spec» `tutor` В83 (RUN.md of `tutor`, `main` 4717981), by its recommendation, in the inbox triage at the end of E10. — *Why:* R146 was written for the paths of `app` and `api`, where the AI answers in words, and R28 tutor already let the executor start paid runs of eval within a task's cap; reading R146 as the words alone would put each run of reading or of a rubric behind the author's confirmation, which R146 rejected. — *Rejected:* the runs of words alone, with the author's «да» for each run of reading or assessment. — R110 tutor.

## The DPIA's approver and the fairness of the learner model

**R147. П-33 and П-34 are closed. The DPIA names whoever approves it — Aleksandr Riazanov, Staff Software Engineer, the author — and the author signs a PDF of each approved version, which the operator keeps outside the repository. The learner model is checked for fairness by a criterion of the learner simulator: virtual learners of the same skill but different grades come to the same estimate and the same kind of task within a number of attempts written down before the first run, and the result goes into dpia 10.2.** The author's answers of 2026-11-13 at the review of T127 (RUN.md), by the recommendations of П-33 and П-34. Colorado's rules ask a data protection assessment for "names, positions, and signatures of the individuals responsible for the review and approval" (4 CCR 904-3 Rule 8.04(A)(13)) and a profiling assessment for "How the Profiling system is evaluated for fairness and disparate impact, and the results of any such evaluation" (Rule 9.06(F)(10)); read 2026-11-13, sources 3.12.
- **The name and the position** are in dpia 7, with the dates of the log. The author gave them as "Aleksandr Riazanov, Staff Software Engineer"; the operator is the author's company, ALT EdTech LLC (R137).
- **The signature.** A version is approved when the author signs its PDF, with the version and the date; the operator keeps the PDF outside the repository for as long as the DPIA itself is kept (dpia 1, "Keeping"), and gives it to an Attorney General on request. The `Signed-off-by` of a commit is the Developer Certificate of Origin, not an approval, and does not stand for a signature. The PDF of version 16 is the author's step before the first child from the US (dpia 8).
- **The criterion of fairness** is the simulator's, in `sim`, which holds the criteria and the gate (architecture 3.9), and not `learner-model`'s: the library is measured, it does not measure itself. It compares populations that differ only by the grade, which sets the start band (architecture 3.8). The age category is not in it: neither the model nor the engine reads it, and `api` limits the pool by it on purpose, by the module's `age_categories` — content unsuitable for an age, which dpia 10.2 assesses as a design choice. The numbers — how many learners, how many attempts, what "the same" means — `sim` writes down before the first run, as for each criterion (R163 standalone). The task is `sim`'s, COORDINATION.md row 4.16, before the first child from the US; until its result, dpia 10.2 says that no evaluation has been made.

— *Why:* Colorado's element 13 needs a name and a signature, and a public DPIA with a name stays whole, while the signed copy is what the Attorney General gets; the simulator already decides every variant of the model by a criterion written in advance, so a run gives the "results" the rule asks for without new data of learners.

— *Rejected:*
- for П-33 — the name and the signature only in the PDF, outside the public DPIA; "the author" as it is, which leaves the element unmet;
- for П-34 — an argument in dpia 10.2 without a run; no evaluation; the age category in the criterion — the difference it makes is by design; the criterion in `learner-model` — the simulator and its gate are `sim`'s.

— *Consequence:* dpia 1, 7, 8, 10; privacy 3.4, 9; architecture 3.9; COORDINATION.md, row 4.16; the 2026-11-13 amendments to R129 and R140 name this decision. — П-33, П-34; R112, R129, R137, R140; RUN.md, T127.

— *Amendment 2026-11-15:* **the evaluation has run, and the base does not hold the criterion. The criterion is R55 sim, written down before its first run; its result, `evaluations/fairness-1/` of `sim` on `learner-model` v0.1.8 and `engine` v0.1.6, is in dpia 10.2, version 19 (R58 sim). The first child, from any country, waits for a round of `learner-model` aimed at the fairness by the grade and its judgement in `sim` (COORDINATION.md, rows 4.17 and 4.18): until the base holds the criterion, or the author accepts the residual risk in dpia 7 with that round's numbers.** The author's answer of 2026-11-15 to the rows «в реестр spec» `sim` В21 and В22 (RUN.md `sim`, `main` 59885be), the inbox triage at the end of E12 by rule 13 of RUN.md. Grades 1 and 5 come to the estimate of grade 3 by the 50th answer for 0.812 and 0.5525 of the learners, below the bound 0.90, while the kind of task holds; a model that starts above the truth leaves it most slowly. `sim` holds no rounds by plan, and this round is the one judgement in its queue (R59 sim); a start by the grade of another kind (concepts 11) is a candidate of the round and comes to `spec` as a row of its own. — *Why:* this decision and Colorado's Rule 9.06(F)(10) ask for the results whatever they are; a disparity found is risk 7 for a child of any country (dpia 10.3), not only one from the US; children wait for much else (dpia 8), so the condition costs nothing now, and the author accepts a residual risk knowing the round's numbers. — *Rejected:* the residual risk accepted now, without the round — `sim`'s author already called it a risk to children (R59 sim); the condition only for a child from the US — the disparity does not depend on the country; holding the criterion with no way to accept the risk — a round may end in an exit. — dpia 6.2, 8, 10.2; privacy 3.4 and П-34; architecture 3.9; COORDINATION.md, closed row 4.16, rows 4.17 and 4.18; R55, R58 and R59 sim; RUN.md, table 5.

First, the three rules of R157, built and checked by a short run of `sim`: the estimate starts low, an adult corrects the level, and a guard lowers the level after N failures in a row. Second, the author's acceptance of the residual risk in dpia 7, with the round's numbers. No long runs fit the model's constants until 100 children, and at 100 children the criterion is evaluated again.** The round's numbers are R42 learner-model: of 48 sets of constants, none brings grade 5 above 0.853 of the bound 0.90, and each one checked fails other cells. Of the 2026-11-15 amendment above, "until the base holds the criterion" is withdrawn until 100 children, and "or the author accepts the residual risk in dpia 7 with that round's numbers" is joined by the rules. dpia 7, 8 and 10.2 change with T173. — R157.

— *Amendment 2026-11-16 (T173):* **the author accepted the residual risk 7 on 2026-11-16, with the numbers of the round of rows 4.17 and 4.18, in version 24 of the DPIA (dpia 7). The first child, from any country, waits for the three rules of R157, built and checked by the short run of `sim`, for the legal texts that name the adult's correction (Д259) and for the signed PDF of version 24** (R157 and its amendment of T173). — run/TASKS.md, T173.

— *Amendment 2026-11-17 (T195):* **until the first child, the author signs one more PDF of the DPIA: that of the version in force before the first child, as a condition of dpia 8. The versions in between need no signature, and `spec`'s git history keeps them (the 2026-11-13 amendment to R129); the PDFs signed already, of version 1 and others, stay as they are. From the first child on, the author signs the PDF of each new version before the processing goes on by it, as before.** The author's word of 2026-11-17 to spec's orchestrator: «до появления первых детей не нужно заниматься этой бюрократией; сейчас только я один там и пишу этот прототип».
- *Why.* Only the author learns (R25 infra), codes to other adults come no earlier than 2026-11-28, and the platform processes no child's data. The three laws bind a controller that offers its service to users it knows are minors (dpia 10). Colorado's signatures, Rule 8.04(A)(13) (sources 3.12), are read here as belonging to the assessment that the processing of a minor's data goes by: the version in force when the first child comes. That is Claude's reading of the law: sources 3.12 quotes no rule on when the signature is due, and Rule 8.05(E) keeps the prior versions, which git does.

The acceptances that dpia 7 records, each with its date, stay the author's decisions, and that signature approves them with the rest of its version.
