## The look of the app by the interface mockup

**R148. The look of `app` and of the tool panel of `canvas` follows the interface mockup in `draft/mockup/`, and the documents keep the behaviour: where they differ, the documents win. The mockup's first slice holds the paper flow of R162; under its switch "Later" stand the children's screens and Pip, for epic E4 of `app`, and the canvases of other authors, for epic E5. The tutor is a panel at the side, part of the app, neutral to an adult, and speaks of the learner's work only while it is open. The first slice is for a phone, a tablet and a computer; the sign-in is Google's alone.** The author's decisions while epics E12, E14 and E11 were planned and done, by the recommendations, and the look the author approved by snapshots (RUN.md, T154, T155) and in RUN.md, T220. Where the mockup's files and its claude.ai canvas are, and which version, is [draft/README.md](../draft/README.md), "Mockups", and the README of `draft/mockup/`, "The files".
- **The mockup** is the look: the sources in `draft/mockup/` and their README — screens and states, the style, the sizes and the rules between them, the contrast and the differences from the documents. The behaviour — what a screen does, what it sends and to whom — is the documents' and the decisions'. A session of `app` or `canvas` compares its screen with the mockup by Playwright, through `tools/mockup/` of its `spec/` submodule, without the author (R146). The claude.ai Design canvas, the author's, is a copy to play that lags the sources while Д278 is open; a change of the look is made in the sources.
- **What waits**, under "Later":
  - for epic E4 of `app`, before the first child: the PIN, the steps of a parent's consent, the Help of a learner under 18, with the helplines, and Pip, the children's tutor, with the mockup's text field and microphone. They follow the mockup when they come; their behaviour is R84, R116 and R127, and a text field and voice wait for О-6 and П-5 (R82). Pip serves tasks from paper too (R162);
  - for epic E5: the canvas kinds of other authors, under «…» in the top bar of a task from paper.
- **Shown but not open:** "Add a learner" on "Who's learning?" stands disabled, with a line that a child's profile waits for a parent's consent. "Take from my paper" on home is open to every profile and opens the camera (R162).
- **The owner profile** is made after "Create account" as the mockup and `CreateOwnerProfile` have it — a made-up name, the country and an avatar from the set of `app` (R98) —, and every profile shows its avatar, the owner's too: the one chosen, or the set's own when none was (R98 keeps the field optional). "Who's learning?" opens the owner profile without the PIN while the account holds no profile of another category (R84).
- **The adult's Help**, behind its button on home, says three things and links to three pages:
  - the tutor is an AI — a computer program, not a person —, and a program checks every answer; when the AI has read the work wrongly, the learner writes it again, or tells the operator by "Report a problem" at the task (privacy 5.3; R04, R123);
  - the name is made up: real names are not written in the work, an essay's either (R127);
  - the pages "Privacy Policy", "Terms of Use" and "Accessibility" of `app` itself, without external links (R130; R90).

  It has no helplines: to an adult R127 gives "Report a problem".
- **The style** keeps the system font of `app` (R17 app): the mockup's Inter and Caveat are not taken. The quota shows a share, as `GetQuota` gives it, not a number of calls (R98). Strings do not speak in the first person of AI (R91), and each is in `en` and `ru` (R92). The gist of a legal text is the `summary` of its version in force in `legal/legal.yaml`, word for word (R130). The tooltip is white on an opaque `#1d1d1f`, and every package draws it so (R84 canvas).
- **The module card** on home shows the five states of the skills of architecture 3.3 and the marks of skills with a rubric and without assessment, by the rule of `skill-map` (R03 skill-map), one function at a second entry point of its package, `./states` — the graph, the answer of `GetSkillMap` and the time in, the states out (R08 skill-map) —; `app` draws the card and its legend. Their words and icons are shared: the map and the legend show them (architecture 6; R78, R91).
- **The lesson and the task screen** of a module are the mockup's, on both sizes (RUN.md, T155). The lesson's segments open in a pop-over from the line under its title (R06 and R23 app); a worked example's "Next" and "Demo" stand in one row with `app`'s "Continue"; the end has no score. The statement is `app`'s card above the canvas (R161). The canvas is the module's, and there is no switch of canvas kinds: the kind is the module's (concepts 8). The row holds Hint, the options of a choice behind "Choose an answer", which opens them in a pop-over, "Show the solution", which asks first, and Check; an essay with a rubric has "Done" there, its feedback drawn by the rubric (R87). A mark of the tutor is a frame beside the learner's work or on a box of the workbook, never over them. What of the screen the mockup does not draw, `app` draws by its rules of style; the canvas note `t155` names each by the key of its string.
- **A task from paper** is the mockup's paper flow, its behaviour R162's: the camera, the page with every task the AI found picked and a frame drawn by hand, and each picked task on a sheet of the learner's grid under its crop as tracing paper, with no switch of kinds. Its row is Hint · Check, with no "Show the solution" and no option buttons (R162; R82). The profile's hint mode, "Questions only" or "Show where", is in the profile's menu on home, and "Show where" draws its wavy line under the place of the first mistake.
- **The tutor's panel** opens at the side, from the tutor's button at the right edge, by Hint and by the pill of the step, not by a verdict; it belongs to the app, not to a canvas. Its buttons are Hint and "Explain differently" (R82) and the speaker of voicing (R07 app), on a task from paper too; it has no microphone, and no text field but on the page to pick from, where it takes a request about the frames (R165): elsewhere the conversation line of the first slice is buttons (product 10; R82; О-6). To an adult the tutor is neutral — no name, no fox (О-13). The verdict is the program's: a line in the panel while it is open, a card above the row while it is closed. The solving steps stand at the top of the panel, and with the panel closed a pill of the current step stands above the row; in "On my own" the panel stays closed until it is called. "Report a problem" stands under each of the AI's words to an adult (R127, R136). At the quota's end the quota's line comes instead of the AI's words, and the task's own hints stay (R82, R98).
- **The tutor speaks of the work only while its panel is open.**
  - *Closed:* a submission is read in the deployment's reading mode (R68) and gets the program's verdict, as the card. `app` asks neither `GetRungWords` nor `GetCorrectAnswerWords`: no analysis of the course of solution, no tutor's mark, no words (R67; concepts 9.1). The rung is the program's and grows with the wrong answers (R82).
  - *The opening* asks once for the words of the last submission of the task on screen that gave "not yet" or "correct", when they were not asked: after "not yet" the rung's words, with that submission's work and its number of wrong answers, and the frame they bring; after "correct" the correct answer words, with the work. A later submission "unreadable" or "unchecked" leaves the number of wrong answers as it was, and the words of the "not yet" before it are still current (R97). An earlier "not yet" whose words were not asked gets none, and another opening for the same submission asks nothing again: the panel shows the words it got. `app` holds that submission's work in memory while the task's screen is open, and asks nothing once the learner has left the screen or begun another attempt.
  - *Open:* the words come after Check; Hint and "Explain differently" only by the learner's press, and Hint after an opening gives the rung's words the attempt now keeps, without AI (R82).
  - `api` and `tutor` do not change for it: `api` reads at `SubmitWork` alone, and the analysis and the words are calls of their own, which `app` makes (R97).
- **The tool panel** is drawn by `canvas`, as the mockup's vertical glass bar at the left edge, and its accessibility stays with `canvas` (R28–R73 canvas). `app` sets its accent and glass by `--novatrail-canvas-accent` and `--novatrail-canvas-glass`, and by `--novatrail-canvas-top` the offset of the band in whose middle the bar stands (R17 app); it hides the bar by the boolean attribute `tools-hidden`, and puts its "Continue" of a worked example into the element's slot `actions`, beside the element's "Next" and "Demo" (R36). The mockup's highlighter is not taken: a new tool is behaviour.
- **Buttons without a visible caption** are the closed list of R90, each with a tooltip of its accessible name.
- **The devices** of the first slice are a phone, a tablet and a computer (product 10). The mockup is drawn in two sizes — an iPad in landscape, 1194 × 834 CSS px, and a phone in portrait, 390 × 844 —, by one `Main.dc.html` whose prop `device` is `ipad` or `phone`, the phone on its board `Phone.dc.html`: the same screens, states and logic, laid out by rules of style of its own. The sign-in, its sky filling the window, is drawn for a computer too, on `Desktop.dc.html` (the author's word, 2026-11-21). An iPad in portrait and a computer's other screens follow the rules of the README of `draft/mockup/`, and a width of 320 CSS px reflows, the sheet in two dimensions (R90; WCAG 1.4.10). On a phone the tool bar is the same vertical bar at the left edge, with no "More" (R90); the tutor's panel is a sheet from the bottom, half the height with the task in view, which its grabber takes to the whole screen and back, and while it is open the row and the tool bar hide; a pop-over is a sheet from the bottom; the legend of the skill states is behind "What the marks mean"; the sheet of a canvas is as wide as the screen and two screens tall.
- **The sign-in** is Google's alone, as the mockup and architecture 3.12 have it. Apple is the question Т-41.

— *Why:*
- The documents describe behaviour and the mockup a look, and a session that reads both needs to know which wins. A screen the mockup lacks — the section for adults, the legal pages, the failure screens — `app` draws by the mockup's rules of style. A child's screens are behaviour that waits for the children (`run/TASKS.md`, T117; R147).
- One rule of the skill states in one package keeps the card and the map from parting.
- The app is to work on a phone, not only on a tablet and a computer, by the author's word. The size of 390 × 844 is the author's choice; Apple's guidelines no longer give a table of screen sizes (sources 5.5). One logic keeps the two sizes from parting, and a lesson is drawn once for both; the same bar keeps the panel of `canvas` one shape and fits a width of 320 CSS px without "More"; the sheet keeps the task in view.
- The panel is where the tutor speaks at each step (concepts 10), so the steps stand in it; small buttons and pop-overs keep the sheet clear; one caption for one button in `app`, the mockup and the documents.
- The theme stays `app`'s and the bar's accessibility the element's, and the mockup has one row for "Next", "Demo" and "Continue".
- The panel's rule is the author's word, «когда наставник скрыт то он не должен анализировать что я решаю на доске; когда открыт то пускай анализирует», and the cost: on `novatrail` on 2026-11-17, by the author's count (RUN.md, T182) — not a measurement of `docs/measurements.md` —, the tutor's words of an hour of the author's lessons, by Opus 5.5 · `high`, cost about $0.10 for 5 calls, and the reading by one Haiku about $0.003 for 6. With the panel closed, less of the learner's work goes to the provider too (privacy 4). The verdict stays without the panel: it is the program's, and the learner goes on by it.
- Over the canvas a translucent tooltip gives a contrast that depends on the strokes beneath it, which axe cannot check; opaque it is 16.8:1, where `rgba(29,29,31,0.92)` gave 13.4:1 over white.
- A task from paper needs no choice of kinds; the learner turns its grid (R162).

— *Rejected:*
- hiding "Add a learner" until epic E4 of `app`; the children's screens before epic E4 of `app` — that is behaviour, and it waits for the children;
- only rules of style, with snapshots in a pull request; drawing every screen of `app` into the mockup; the mockup as sources and a README alone, without its runtime — a session would not see it;
- Pip for everyone; a persona of the adult's choice in the presentation style — a new field, which runs into О-23;
- captions on every icon; dropping the closed list and holding WCAG alone; a visible caption "Tutor" on the tutor's button;
- Apple in the first slice — a new provider of sign-in, a new version of `deployment/` and tasks of `api`, `app` and `infra`;
- the panel drawn by `app` — an edit of the contract `types/canvas` (R36) in both repositories, and the panel's accessibility moved to `app`; the bar as `::part(tools)`; colours fixed in `canvas`; two rows on a worked example, and "Next" and "Demo" drawn by `app`;
- only a tablet and a computer; a phone of 375 or 360 CSS px; a `Phone.dc.html` of its own; the sign-in's card at a computer window's edge; a horizontal bar at the bottom with "More"; the tutor over the whole screen at once; the legend always under the modules;
- for the skill states — a third view of `<novatrail-skill-map>` that draws the card's bar inside the card of `app`, and the rule repeated in `app`;
- helplines in the adult's Help;
- the steps on the task screen, as a strip over the sheet; the options as a static list over the sheet; the rubric's feedback left to T47 of `app`; the caption "Explain it differently", with `app` changed to it;
- the words only from a new Check after the opening — the analysis of an error already made would be lost; a button "Analyse" in the panel — a step more;
- the mockup's tooltip at 0.92, the fill of `canvas` recorded as its difference — two tooltips on one screen, and `app` left to check the contrast over the canvas alone.

— *Consequence:* product 4, 10, О-13 and О-26; concepts 9.1, 10 and 15 — "interface mockup"; architecture 3.1, 3.2, 3.3, 3.5, 4.1 and 6; repositories 8 — Т-41; privacy 4; sources 3.13 and 5.5; [the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 15; CLAUDE.md, the line of `draft/`; [draft/README.md](../draft/README.md), "Mockups", and the README of `draft/mockup/`; Д278.

## AI on the deployment

**R149. NovaTrail is not used without AI: on the deployment `novatrail`, where only the author learns, platform AI opens now — `api` runs at the rung "author", declares the facts `data_processing_agreement` and `minimal_retention` at Anthropic for `adult`, as the first app did, and calls Anthropic by the platform's key. For adults the rung "full" is no longer a condition of admission: it stays the target of quality, measured on the samples of adult volunteers (П-16). Before the first learner other than the author, the privacy policy says what the provider keeps and the table opens adults' platform AI without `minimal_retention` (RUN.md, T159). Children stay closed.** The author's word of 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15, while RUN.md, T158 was planned, which the rows «в реестр spec» `infra` В35 (pull request 75 of `infra`, a27e342) and `api` В69 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` d9a4538) brought.
- **What the author asked for.** The module "Задачи на листе", `novatrail/check-board`, works on https://novatrail.web.app as it was meant to: a task with no options, the learner solves it on the canvas, presses "Check", the AI reads the work, a program gives the verdict, and "not yet" shows where the error is. The way is all there already: reading only on "Check" (R69), two readers and a program's verdict (R03, R67, R68), and after "not yet" a frame round the first error from the words of the rung, `MARK_KIND_FRAME` (concepts 9; [the contracts](../contracts/README.md), section 15). Only the admission kept it closed: the rung "full", which no model has passed (R71 api), the refusal of "author" on a deployment (R45 api), no facts and no key (R25 infra).
- **Who learns.** By the author's word of 2026-11-15, nobody but the author uses `novatrail`: the second adult who had come by a code of `api invite` (R76) does not learn there, and the operator gives no code of `api invite` to anyone else until T159 is done. Before the rollout `infra` checks that the database holds no account but the author's, and brings any it finds to the author, deleting none.
- **`api`**, by row 6.20 of `COORDINATION.md`: on a deployment it accepts the rung "author" — amendments to R25 and R45 api —, and its own key follows the rung as R72 api has it. A release.
- **`infra`**, by row 6.21: the platform's key of Anthropic as a secret of Secret Manager, mounted as a volume, `API_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FILE` (R46 api); the facts `{"anthropic": {"data_processing_agreement": ["adult"], "minimal_retention": ["adult"]}}`; the rung "author"; the new pair by the list (R29 infra); an amendment to R25 infra. Before the key goes in, the author sets the spending limit of the provider's workspace (Д11 `api`); the adapters of `tutor` take no address from the environment since T73 `api` (Д225).
- **The fact is declared untruthfully**, as the first app declared it: the organization at Anthropic has retention "On · 30 days". The author's work is the author's data, and the author, an adult, decides where it lies. The cost is written here, not hidden.
- **Children** are closed as before: the cells under 18 (R122, R123), dpia 8.

— *Why:* the AI that reads the work on the canvas is what the platform is for, and without it the site shows a module that cannot be begun. The same exception had been weighed for the first app, where only the author learned, and the same holds on `novatrail` now.

— *Rejected:*
- AI only for accounts the operator marks, as `infra` В35 recommended: the author wants one rule for everyone who uses the program;
- the rung "author" by the adult's own key: a key on each device, and the same rung;
- waiting for the rung "full" on volunteers' samples: the site would have no AI for months;
- solving the module only locally, by `just dev-ai` of `api`, as `api` В69 recommended: the author shows the platform on the site.

## Stored works in the export

**R151. A profile's stored works reach the export as files of their own beside `api.zip`, not inside it: `app` reads each by `GetWork`, one at a time, and writes it into the ZIP, and the profile's file of `api.zip` names them only — the attempt, the kind, when it was kept and the size. This is version 3 of `export/`. Т-40 is closed.** The author's answer of 2026-11-15 to the row «в реестр spec» `api` В68 (RUN.md of `api`, `main` ca0f246), by the register's recommendation (a).

— *Why:* the export is one unary answer, and Cloud Run gives an answer over HTTP/1 at most 32 MiB without chunks or a stream (sources 4.7); `api` holds a work five or six times in memory while it builds the answer (R70 api), so a profile of a few works of 4 MiB with pictures that do not compress may not export at all. By files, every answer stays within the 4 MiB of a work, no method is new, and `app` already builds the ZIP of what the device holds (R135).

— *Rejected:* a stream of the part — a method that streams, which R83 forbids ([the contracts text](../contracts/README.md), section 7); a link to a temporary object of a bucket — a new copy of every work outside the database, a new place of privacy 4 and a task of `infra`; a limit on the sum of a profile's works — version 1 of `storage-consent`, in force, promises each work (R113), and a text in force does not change (R130); keeping version 2, as the register's recommendation had it before `v0.17.0` — `v0.17.0` is out and `api` gives version 2 (R69 api).

— *Consequence:* R113 and R135; repositories 8, Т-40; RUN.md, T161; Д233.

**R152. The breach laws of the US states (T150): the operator follows them all, by the strictest, for every learner from the US. Whoever's data a breach reached hears of it from one letter by email no later than the 30th day after discovery, whatever the harm; each authority whose law covers what was reached and whose threshold the number reached does not rule out is told, Maryland's before the letters and Vermont's by the 14th business day; nobody is asked for their state, and the privacy policy does not change.** The author's answers of 2026-11-15 in the planning of T150 (RUN.md). Read 2026-11-15, sources 10.1–10.57: from the legislatures' sites and the official codes, and where those did not open, from Wayback Machine copies of the official pages or from the session laws — for California, Connecticut, Illinois, Indiana, Georgia, Alabama, Arkansas, Tennessee, Mississippi, New Mexico and Oklahoma, as each record names; the law of the U.S. Virgin Islands was not read (sources 10.55). Privacy 3.4.

- **The scope** — the breach laws of all 50 states, the District of Columbia and the territories that have one. Rejected: by thresholds — a breach law has no threshold for people, and the authority's threshold counts residents of the state, which the operator does not know; Texas alone — §521.053(b-1) lets a resident of another state be told by that state's law, and many laws bind whoever holds data of their residents, without "conducts business in" (sources 10.1).
- **What of the platform's data they cover** (privacy 3.4): a stored work that concerns health — Texas without a name, New York and the District of Columbia with any identifier, eighteen more with a name; the writing history, where the definition of biometric data is not limited to what the holder authenticates by — Iowa, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Washington, Maryland, Florida, New York, Connecticut, North Carolina and, from 2027-01-01, Vermont; a name with a signature on a scanned form — North Dakota and North Carolina. The server holds no names, but a work can carry one and an email address often does, so the order takes a name as reached. The platform keeps no password and no security question: Google signs in, and an email alone is in no law. Taken to apply, not verified: whether writing history is "biometric" in those laws; whether the laws of Arizona, Indiana, Ohio and Pennsylvania, which find a resident by the mailing address in the records, reach an operator that has none.
- **The letter.** The shortest deadline is 30 days after discovery — California, New York, Washington; Colorado and Florida from the determination. No threshold of harm is relied on: California, Illinois, Texas and North Dakota have none, and Vermont wants a decision of no harm sent to its attorney general. Encryption excuses nothing: Wyoming has no exception for it, and Texas none for data about health. One letter fits all the laws that the platform's data reaches: California's form — "Notice of Data Breach" with its five headings, plain language, at least 10-point type — and what the laws whose rules on it were read ask (privacy 3.4) — with the total number reached, which Rhode Island asks, and no number by state, since Illinois forbids the number of its residents: a reading, В40 of RUN.md. The rules of Alabama, Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, Nebraska, North Dakota and Texas on the letter were not read, and the template is checked against them first (Д249). Massachusetts forbids the nature of the breach and the number, while California and Rhode Island ask for them; Massachusetts covers only a social security number, a licence or a financial account, which the platform does not hold, so the two do not meet.
- **By email.** Alabama, Arizona, Florida, Wyoming and others take an email letter as it is; Maryland, Colorado, Vermont and others when the business works through the Internet or by email; 26 others only "consistent with" E-SIGN, 15 U.S.C. §7001(c), which needs the person's consent, and the operator asks none. Most of these deem whoever notifies by their own written procedures within the law's timing to comply — `BREACH.md` of `infra` is written as such procedures, and whether it counts is not verified (R112). New York's text was not checked word for word beyond whom it binds and its 30 days (sources 10.34), and the rest of what this entry says of it is checked before the first letter (Д249). The District of Columbia, New York and North Carolina have no such clause: there a letter without consent is the email part of a substitute notice, which also posts the notice on the site and tells major statewide media, and in New York needs its attorney general shown that contact information is lacking — В39 of RUN.md.
- **The authorities.** Each authority whose law covers what was reached and whose threshold of residents is not above the total number reached, since any of them may live there: the attorney general of Maryland before the letters; of Vermont, a preliminary description by the 14th business day after discovery; those that want it no later than the letters — Arkansas, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Illinois, Montana, Nebraska, New York — its attorney general, department of state and state police —, North Dakota and Oregon; those of the 30th day — Texas, Colorado, Florida and Washington; and by their own terms — Rhode Island without delaying the letters, Missouri and North Carolina without unreasonable delay, Iowa 5 business days after the letters, California's sample copy 15 days after them, Alabama and Arizona — with its department of homeland security — by the 45th day; the thresholds and terms are privacy 3.4. An authority that asks for the number of its residents gets the total and the word that the state is not known. Over 500 notified, the nationwide consumer reporting agencies — Rhode Island's threshold, the lowest among the laws reached.
- **Nobody is asked for their state.** The policy in force says "We do not ask which state you live in", and the order needs no state: it is the same for every learner. Rejected: asking for the state in a breach — a new kind of data, a new version of `privacy-policy` (R130), and a letter that waits for an answer.
- **The GDPR** stays as it is: Arts. 33 and 34 wait for the first learner from the EU, the EEA or the United Kingdom (R131; [BREACH.md `infra`](https://github.com/altnovatrail/infra/blob/main/BREACH.md), section 11).
- **To watch:** a law reached by data the platform does not hold now — Puerto Rico tells its consumer affairs department within 10 days, and New Jersey its state police before the people, both for a social security number, a licence, an account or a username with its password; Massachusetts, above; Vermont's definitions from 2027-01-01; Hawaii's SB 3016 (2026), whose fate was not read; the U.S. Virgin Islands, whose law was not read (sources 10.55).

— *Why:* the platform does not know a learner's state (R140), and the deadline of Texas — 60 days — is twice that of California, New York and Washington; the first child from the US and 250 learners — the threshold at which `infra` reviews its procedure (R27 infra) — wait for this (dpia 8).

— *Rejected:* a letter per state's law — the operator does not know who lives where; reading a state's law in the breach, as [BREACH.md `infra`](https://github.com/altnovatrail/infra/blob/main/BREACH.md), section 10, does now — the day of a breach is no day to read 56 laws.

— *Consequence:* sources 10; privacy 3.4; the 2026-11-15 amendments to R137 and R140; [DPIA](dpia.md), version 22; RUN.md — T150, В39, В40 and the row `infra` В29 of table 5; Д200 closed, Д249 for the operator and `infra`.

— privacy 1, 3.4; R112, R130, R131, R137, R140; RUN.md, T150.

The letter names the total number of people reached and no number by state.** The author's answers of 2026-11-15 to В39 and В40 of RUN.md, table 3, by their recommendations (a). *Why:* the laws themselves name the substitute notice where there is neither an address nor the consent — North Carolina names the lack of consent outright (sources 10.35) —, and the texts in force do not change; one letter answers the words of both Rhode Island and Illinois, and the number of Illinois's residents the operator does not know anyway (sources 10.15, 10.41). *Rejected:* a consent to notices by email under §7001(c) — a new legal text or a version of `terms-of-use` with the statements (B) and (C), a screen of `app` and a record of the consent in `api`, and New York forbids making it a condition, so those who refuse still get the substitute notice; it is the option once the platform's growth makes messages to the media frequent; the letter alone — the three laws may count the notice as not given; a letter with no number — Rhode Island unmet; deciding with a lawyer in the breach — the day of a breach is no day to decide it. That the operator's toll-free number, which Wyoming asks (sources 10.52), is set up in the breach and not before stays as Д249 has it: the author confirmed it on 2026-11-15. — privacy 3.4; [DPIA](dpia.md), version 23; Д249.

A done task's gist sentence goes to the archive with its body. Every other repository takes the same layout from the template, with a move to a tag of `spec`, and until then the checks read both.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-15 for T165 (RUN.md); the names of the folder and of the files are the executor's.
- **The files.** Each table moves verbatim under its old heading — «Таблица 2. Эпики на потом», «Таблица 3. Вопросы автору без ответа», «Таблица 4. Технический долг», «Таблица 5. Строки других репозиториев, записанные в `spec`» —, so "table 3" and "Д173" in older texts still name it; only its relative links change, to lead from `run/`. The file opens with the table's rules, which leave «Как устроен план: эпики» of RUN.md — what a row holds, when it leaves, who reads the file —, and `run/INBOX.md` also with how the inbox triage goes, which was rule 13. The files are in Russian, as RUN.md is. The epic archives keep the section «Начала таблиц 3, 4 и 5 RUN.md» under its name. A citation such as "RUN.md, table 2" or "table 5 of RUN.md" in an older entry or archive reads through the opening of RUN.md, which names each table's file; an entry gets an amendment where its text in force says where a table is.
- **RUN.md.** The rules say the same in fewer words and point to RULES.md, CLAUDE.md and the log for what they repeated; the opening links the four files. On 2026-11-15 it went from 55,192 bytes to 16,523, with the body of the open task T117. Its limit in `budgets.json` stays 96 KB: an epic's planned bodies live in it until they are done.
- **The gist sentence.** When a task is done, its body and its gist sentence go to the archive together: the sentence is a list item without a heading at the start of the section that receives the body — «T129 — сделана 2026-11-11: <итог одной фразой>» —, and RUN.md keeps neither; the row of table 1 stays. The sentences of T149–T151 and T159–T164 went to the start of «Задачи вне эпика, сделанные после него» in `docs/plan/E12.md`.
- **The checks.** `docs-check` reads the register «В» from `run/QUESTIONS.md` and «Д» from `run/DEBT.md`. In a repository that has not moved, it reads them where they were — table 3 in RUN.md, table 4 in `DEBT.md` or, before T132, in RUN.md —; a table left in one of those places beside the one read is a second copy, an error; in `spec` only `run/` is read. A fingerprint is of the cells alone, so a move changes none.
- **The other repositories.** `repo-template/` has the layout — `run/EPICS.md`, `run/QUESTIONS.md` and `run/DEBT.md`, and a RUN.md with its rules and epic E1 —, so a new repository starts with it. Each existing one moves its tables in its move to a tag of `spec` that has this decision, by row Д250 of `run/DEBT.md`; once all have moved, the checks stop reading the old places, by the same row.

The name `run/` sits beside RUN.md and reads as its tables; `plan/` would be confused with `docs/plan/` in grep and in links. ## The orchestrator

**R156. An epic across repositories runs by itself: the author says «Сделай эпик E…» in a session of `spec` opened in its second devcontainer configuration, `.devcontainer/orchestrator/`, which sees the host's Docker. That session — the orchestrator — runs each task of the epic as one fresh `claude -p "Выполни задачу Txx из RUN.md"`, by `docker exec` in the container of its repository, in parallel wherever the graph allows; gathers every executor's questions to the author into one queue and continues the same executor session with the answers; and merges each pull request once its checks are green, without the author's review. The same container also runs a task across repositories (R166): one session, which the author leads, writes in the clone of every repository the task names, in `.epics`. The code and the procedure are `tools/orchestrator/`.** The author's decisions in planning epics E14 and E15 and in the orchestrator's pilot, and on the terms of the subscription, each by the recommendation; the task across repositories is the author's word of 2026-11-18 in planning epic E11 (RUN.md, table 1, «Порядок работы»).
- **Where.** `.devcontainer/orchestrator/devcontainer.json` mounts the host's socket `/var/run/docker.sock`; spec's documents container stays without it. Access to the socket is root on the host (sources 9.2): no code but NovaTrail's own is opened in that container. It mounts spec's folder — the folder the documents container opens too, whose branch a task of spec switches — and `.epics` (R166): so the orchestrator runs from its own clone of spec's `main`, which `sync` makes or moves forward and nobody edits, on the volume `novatrail-claude`, beside the folders of its runs and epics ([tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), Commands and The run).
- **The executor.** A task is one run of `claude -p` by `docker exec` in the container of its repository's clone, found by the labels `devcontainer.local_folder` and `devcontainer.config_file` together — spec's folder has two configurations (sources 9.3). It is a fresh session, the `/clear` of R143, with every permission, `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`. It works by the contract [tools/orchestrator/executor.md](../tools/orchestrator/executor.md), which the orchestrator copies into the run's folder from its own clone when the run starts and gives by `--append-system-prompt` on every attempt, the first and each `--resume`: a session keeps its first request's system prompt through `--resume` only until it is compacted, and then takes the later launch's (sources 2.11). By it the executor does the task by its repository's RUN.md, puts a question for the author into that repository's table 3 and returns `waiting`, carries the task to a pull request by R159 and never merges it, and returns `done` only once every check of the pull request has finished, its report in Russian in the status. `NOVATRAIL_DEVCONTAINER` is `1` there by `containerEnv`, so the run is inside the devcontainer as RULES.md requires; git pushes by `gh auth git-credential`, since the container's own helper is VS Code's and has no window under `docker exec` (sources 9.3). The run's status and cost come from its `stream-json` and its `result` (sources 2.11; README, The run and Where a run stands). spec's `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, which every repository's copies, sets `"shutdownAction": "none"`, so closing a window of VS Code does not stop a container under a running executor (sources 9.4).
- **The procedure** of «Сделай эпик E…» is the section «Сделай эпик E…» of the README, beside the commands it calls, and the hook of `tools/session/` counts the phrase as one task. E… is spec's current epic, table 1 of the clone's RUN.md; its graph is the epic's own open tasks of spec, run in spec's documents container, and the open tasks of the rows of «Порядок» it names, read from each repository's `main`. The state is the epic's folder, `epic.json` and `questions.json`, from which a compaction or a new session takes the epic. The orchestrator edits no file of spec's working tree: it names the rows done, and a task of spec deletes them. The graph is the session's, not a loop in code; a loop comes only by the trigger of Д258, with a rewrite of this entry.
- **The merge.** The orchestrator merges each pull request itself — `gh pr merge --merge` — once CI, `codecov/patch` and SonarCloud are green, SonarCloud's issues of the pull request read by its API, since a green check can hide them. Nobody reviews it, the legal texts, the DPIA and the log included: the author reads the orchestrator's report, which carries each executor's in gist. A draft is a task's product and is not merged; a red `main` is the author's, never mended by the orchestrator; after a merge that changed `.devcontainer/` the orchestrator rebuilds the container (R158) ([README](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), section 5).
- **Questions.** The executor never decides for the author. The orchestrator keeps one queue of all executors' questions, pauses only the node that waits on one, asks the author in its own session — in its window or from the Claude app (R158) — one at a time, with options and a recommendation, and continues the same executor session with all of a run's answers at once (`--resume`). A small technical question inside one repository, which no document reserves for the author, it decides itself and names in its report. A question across repositories is still a row «в реестр spec» (RULES.md, Across repositories; [README](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), section 6).
- **Plans.** The author approves neither an executor's plan nor the plan of an epic in a repository: the plan goes into the report, in Russian, and into the pull request's description, in English (R14).
- **The latest tag of spec first.** Wave 0 moves each repository of the epic that is not on spec's latest release to its tag, by the repository's own open task of a move, with a prompt that names the tag, or by `tools/orchestrator/tasks/spec-tag.md` ([README](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), section 3).
- **Parallelism and limits.** One repository runs one task at a time (R19); different ones run in parallel, with no limit on the executors at once. The subscription's limit is one for every session of the account, a window of five hours and a weekly ceiling, and no document names a limit on sessions at once (sources 2.12). A limit reached pauses every start until its reset, and then the limited runs continue; how `-p` shows a limit is sources 2.11. The orchestrator never turns on usage bought beyond the subscription, so a run stops at the limit rather than going on at API prices (sources 2.12). A task has a ceiling of cost, by measurements 1.12: `--max-budget-usd` does not count a resumed run's earlier spend, while `total_cost_usd` reports the session's whole total (sources 2.11), so the orchestrator gives each attempt only what is left; over the ceiling — a question to the author. A failed run, a red check or an issue gets two attempts in the same session, then goes to the author ([README](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), section 7).
- **The subscription.** The runs use the author's own sign-in to Claude, not an API key. Anthropic's Consumer Terms forbid access "through automated or non-human means, whether through a bot, script, or otherwise" except by an API key "or where we otherwise explicitly permit it", and its documentation of Claude Code offers a token of the subscription "for CI pipelines, scripts", runs a `-p` session on the sign-in unless `--bare` is given, and assumes "ordinary, individual usage" for the advertised limits (sources 2.12). The author reads `claude -p` as such a permission: it is Claude Code's own mode, under the author's own sign-in, in the author's own repositories, not a product of a third party that routes others' credentials. `--bare` is to become the default of `-p` in a later release, and bare mode does not use the sign-in (sources 2.11): each raise of Claude Code's version checks it, by Д251.
- **The model.** Every run, the executors' and the orchestrator's own, is Opus at effort `high`, unless the author's word or a measurement says otherwise.
- **A task across repositories** (R166) runs in this container too, as one session the author leads in its window of VS Code — no executor of `claude -p`; one task, one session (R143) —, on the epic's branch in the clones of `.epics` of every repository its body names. The session edits them with its own tools and runs each repository's checks and servers in that repository's container, by `docker exec`, through `xrepo`. The task's `spec` is its clone in `.epics` too, its bookkeeping there; the container opens spec's folder, whose rules the session reads, so no task of spec runs in that folder while it does (R166). Each finished change is pushed to the epic's branch; the pull requests, their merges and releases follow the author's «да», by `xrepo ship` (rule 4 of RUN.md).
- **The rules.** RULES.md: «Сделай эпик E…» is the word on each task it runs — the executor commits, pushes and opens the pull request, the orchestrator merges it —; the devcontainer rule holds for each executor in its own repository's container; a session of a task across repositories writes in every repository the task names, from spec's orchestrator container, and pushes each change (R166). RUN.md, the first line of Rules and rules 4 and 7; COORDINATION.md, its opening and rule 8: the orchestrator is the coordinator's role carried to the end, in the orchestrator's container. The template's RUN.md, rule 7, names the contract.

— *Why:* the author asked that an epic across repositories run in one session, with no task started by hand: each task of each repository waited for the author to open its container, type its phrase, review, commit and merge, while the coordinator only named the next one (R76). A fresh `claude -p` is one task in one session, as R143 holds; each task runs in its own repository's container, with its own toolchain, as the devcontainer rule holds; and the context lives in files — RUN.md, table 3, the log, the epic's folder. The questions stay with the author, since decisions are the author's (RULES.md, How we work), and only they stop the run. The checks a pull request meets — CI, `codecov/patch`, SonarCloud (R30, R48) — are the bar of a merge; the author reads what was done in the report. The limit is shared by every session anyway (sources 2.12), so a pause at the limit is the one brake needed. A repository behind the latest tag of spec lacks the plan's layout and language (R153–R155) and the line of the contract in its RUN.md. In the pilot (measurements 1.13) four runs returned before CI or SonarCloud had reported, so `done` waits for every check. A task across repositories is one session that holds the whole change and reaches every repository's container, with its toolchain, and the author sees it work end to end before any pull request (R166).

— *Rejected:*
- the Docker socket in spec's ordinary container — every session on documents would be root on the host; a repository of its own for the orchestrator — an amendment to R18, its own CI and tags, and it would read spec's plan past its own tag;
- for the executors, Remote Control and messages between sessions — nobody can type `/clear` into another session, and the end of a task is not seen (Remote Control is the author's channel to the orchestrator, R158); cloud sessions — no devcontainer; all repositories in one container — their toolchains differ; the Agent SDK — the same terms as the CLI's (sources 2.11), but as a package of `tools/` it would enter NovaTrail's code and its lock file, while the CLI is a development tool already in every image, named by R12;
- a review of the legal texts, the DPIA and the log, or of each pull request;
- every question to the author; deciding everything but the log itself; a board of questions on claude.ai, or another channel such as Slack (R158);
- approving each executor's plan, or the plans of epics;
- up to three executors at once, or one at a time; and, on the terms of the subscription, a cap on executors at once to stay "ordinary", an API key for the executors — the terms are plain, but every token is paid —, or a question to Anthropic's support first;
- the status's schema as a part in `types/` — a normative part, with its version, examples and vectors, in the Go module and the npm package and a new line of the release; it is `tools/orchestrator/status.schema.json`;
- a `git worktree` for the orchestrator's copy — it shares `.git` with the working tree —, or the working tree with no copy;
- a ceiling of $50, or none by default;
- the procedure in the Rules of `COORDINATION.md` — every coordinator's session would read it, and the file is at its budget; the orchestrator closing rows of «Порядок» itself — spec's working tree may be on any branch, and its clone is never edited;
- the default `shutdownAction`, `stopContainer`, with which an attempt is lost and paid again from where it stopped; `none` only for the repositories of an epic, by hand, which a repository joining one forgets;
- for a task across repositories, what R159 and R166 rejected: an executor of `claude -p` in each repository's container, the host's clones mounted, no such task at all.

— *Consequence:* RULES.md — How we work, Across repositories and Hard rules; RUN.md — the first line of Rules, rules 4 and 7, and Epics; COORDINATION.md — its opening and rule 8; `repo-template/files/RUN.md`, rule 7, and the test of `new-repo`; CLAUDE.md, Environment; `.devcontainer/orchestrator/devcontainer.json`; [tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), [tools/orchestrator/executor.md](../tools/orchestrator/executor.md), `tools/orchestrator/tasks/spec-tag.md` and `tools/session/`; sources 2.11, 2.12, 9.2, 9.3 and 9.4; measurements 1.12, 1.13; R12; the fifth 2026-11-15 amendment to R19 and the second to R31; R76, R143, R158, R159, R166; Д251, Д258.

## The fairness of the learner model until 100 children

**R157. Until 100 children learn on NovaTrail, no long runs fit the learner model's constants on `sim`. What stays is `sim`'s fast gate in CI and one-off analyses of how the model works. In place of calibration come three rules, checked by a short run of `sim`: the estimate of a new learner starts low, an adult corrects the level, and a guard lowers the level after N failures in a row. The fairness condition of dpia 8 becomes: the three rules are built and checked by that run, and the author accepts the residual risk in dpia 7, with the numbers of the round of rows 4.17 and 4.18 and with the rules as its measures. At 100 children the criterion of fairness (R147) is evaluated again.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-16 in T171 (RUN.md), each by the orchestrator's recommendation, given while the orchestrator ran rows 4.17 and 4.18:
1. «Догнать T61 и выйти»: let the exploration T61 of `learner-model` finish its decisive run, then close the round with its exit;
2. no long runs until at least 100 children, keeping the fast gate, the one-off analyses and the three rules;
3. the dpia 8 condition as "the rules and the risk".

`learner-model` and `sim` recorded the word first: R42 learner-model and R69 sim.
- **The round's numbers** (R41 and R42 learner-model; R58 sim).
  - *The base.* `learner-model` v0.1.8 with `engine` v0.1.6. By the 50th answer, 0.812 of grade 1's learners and 0.5525 of grade 5's come to grade 3's estimate, against the bound 0.90.
  - *The asymmetry.* A start 2.5 above the truth comes down in 83.33 answers on average; a start below comes up in 32.52.
  - *The cause.* The engine gives the trial series' tasks a band higher when the start is higher, so the series cannot tell a start a band too high from the truth. The step of θ after the series is slow to close that gap.
  - *The constants.* 48 sets were screened, and none brings grade 5 above 0.853. Each of the 12 sets checked against "no worse" fails 10 to 23 checks of the other cells. The bound is not reached by fitting constants.
- **The rules** answer the cause rather than fit around it:
  - a start below the band errs on the side the model leaves quickly;
  - an adult who sees the child sets the level in one step;
  - the guard bounds how long a child meets tasks that are too hard.

  How low the start is, what N is and where the adult's correction lives are for the task of the rules. That is T173 (run/TASKS.md), with the rows it adds to COORDINATION.md for `learner-model`, `engine`, `api`, `app` and `sim`. Until then they are proposals of the plan.
- **What stays.**
  - `sim`'s gate on every pull request of the model and of the engine;
  - a one-off analysis, as T59 learner-model was, when a change asks why;
  - the criterion R55 sim and the judgement `model-fair-1` (R65 sim). The judgement is deferred, like T72 and T73 of `sim` and T62 and T63 of `learner-model`, which are `[?]`.

— *Why:*
- NovaTrail is a prototype, and the round's learners are synthetic: their bands and answers are R55 sim's assumptions, not children's.
- Below 100 children, no difference between grades in real learners could be told from noise. A criterion calibrated on synthetic cells promises what nobody can check.
- A decisive run took one and a half to two and a half hours, and the exploration found the bound out of reach of constants.
- The rules remove the asymmetry by construction, and a short run can show that they do.
- The author accepts a residual risk knowing the round's numbers, as the 2026-11-15 amendment to R147 allowed.

— *Rejected:*
- carrying the round on to the bound 0.90, with more decisive runs, T62–T63 learner-model and the judgement T72 sim;
- stopping T61 before its decisive runs, which leaves no numbers for the risk;
- the rules alone, with no risk accepted: the rules are no measurement of fairness, and R147 asks for the results whatever they are;
- the risk alone, with no rules: the asymmetry would reach the first children untouched.

— *Consequence:*
- the 2026-11-16 amendment to R147;
- COORDINATION.md, rows 4.17 and 4.18 `[?]`;
- run/TASKS.md, T173: dpia 7, 8 and 10.2 and privacy 3.4, with a new version of the DPIA and the author's signed PDF (R147), and the rows of the rules;
- the rows «в реестр spec» `learner-model` В52 and В53 go to the inbox of T172.

— R147, R156; R40–R42 learner-model; R55, R58, R65 and R69 sim; RUN.md, T171.

— *Amendment 2026-11-16 (T173):* **where each rule lives and its numbers, by the author's answers of 2026-11-16, each by the recommendation. The start and the guard are `learner-model`'s, and `engine` does not change: the estimate of a new learner starts a band below the band of the grade, and three failures in a row of a module lower its level by a band. The adult's correction is "Easier" and "Harder" in the section for adults of `app`, a band in one step, by a method of `ProgressService` (T178), which `api` appends to the evidence log as a fact for `learner-model`; every learner sees that an adult set the level, and when. "Checked" is better than the base and nowhere worse: grade 5's `M11.same` by the 50th answer above 0.5525, no cell worse by `fair` (R57 sim), the guard lowering the level of at most 5 % of the learners under grade 3, by a criterion `sim` writes before the run; its numbers go to dpia 10.2. The author accepted the residual risk 7 now, low, in version 24 of the DPIA, with the rules as its measures, so dpia 8 waits only for the rules, built and checked, and the signed PDF of version 24.** The first child also waits for the versions of the legal texts that name the correction (Д259). The amendments of T173 to R51 and R147. ## The orchestrator away from VS Code

**R158. Away from VS Code the author drives the orchestrator's session through Remote Control, in the Claude app on the phone: the questions are AskUserQuestion, as in the window, with a push to the phone, and the answers and free text come from the app, typed or by its dictation. NovaTrail builds no channel, board or voice layer of its own. A question with no answer waits, and stops only its node. Free text from the app is the author's word in the session. After its own merge of a pull request that changed `.devcontainer/`, the orchestrator rebuilds the repository's container itself, and it creates the container a repository never had, both by the Dev Containers CLI in a helper container.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-17 in planning epic E15 (RUN.md, table 1, «Решено автором»), given through spec's orchestrator: the answers by AskUserQuestion, the word after the mockup of the board, and the answer to В41 — «всё уже работает в claude. ничего дополнительно делать не нужно»; the helper, the new clone, what is built and the window are the author's answers to В42 and В43 in T193, each by the recommendation.
- **The channel.** `/remote-control` in the orchestrator's session in the VS Code extension puts the session in the Code tab of the Claude app, while the host is on and the session's `claude` runs (sources 2.13). The author turns it on before the first run, and in `/config` "Push when actions required", for the questions, and "Push when Claude decides", for PushNotification ([tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), section 1).
  - PushNotification reaches the phone only with Remote Control on, and without it is a notification on the computer alone (sources 2.13). In the pilot it was off, so no push reached the phone.
  - The author said on 2026-11-17 that the answers to AskUserQuestion and free text reach the session from the app (sources 2.13): no probe checks it again.
- **Voice** is the app's dictation in the same session: speech becomes text, and the reply is text. In Claude Code "dictation is available but voice mode isn't" (sources 2.13), so nothing is read aloud. No rules of "by voice at once / from the screen" and no task of hands-free voice are made.
- **A question with no answer waits.** No time-out decides it: only its node stands, the rest of the graph goes on, and nobody decides for the author (R156).
- **The author's word away from VS Code.** Free text from the app — a new task ("do … in parallel too"), a change of order, the stop of a node — is the author's word in the session, as typed in the window. The orchestrator takes it into the graph, `epic.json`, stops a run where the word asks, and answers what it did. The hook of `tools/session/` still stops a phrase that starts a task by its number right after the verb, as R156 has it, so a new task is said otherwise — «добавь T45 `api` в граф» ([tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), section 6).
- **The containers.** The orchestrator rebuilds a repository's container after its own merge of a pull request that changed `.devcontainer/`, once CI of `main` on the merge is green, and creates the container of a repository of the graph that has none, from its `main` with CI on it green. The commands are `rebuild` and `create` of `tools/orchestrator/`; rule 4 of RUN.md names both in its exception for «Сделай эпик E…». Only NovaTrail's repositories, `altnovatrail/*`, are built: the socket is root on the host (sources 9.2), and the CLI builds what the repository's `.devcontainer/` names.
  - *The helper.* The CLI's `devcontainer up` needs the clone at the host's path (sources 9.5), and the host's folder is the container's label `devcontainer.local_folder` (sources 9.3). For each `rebuild` or `create` the orchestrator runs `docker run --rm` of its own container's image, in the stage `orchestrator` (T192), with the host's socket; the host's network, so that a repository's `initializeCommand`, which Dev Containers runs on the host (sources 9.4), reads the host's routes for its network's MTU; and the host's folder that holds the clone at the same path, where git makes a new clone and the same command makes `.epics` beside the clone on the host, where the container's bind needs it (R166; sources 9.4, 9.7). The orchestrator's own container sees spec's folder and `.epics` (R166), never the host's clones. Seen 2026-11-17: `.github` rebuilt in 15 s, a temporary clone's container made in 9 s (sources 9.6).
  - *A new clone* lies beside spec's on the host, in the folder that holds the orchestrator's own folder by its label. git in the helper clones it from `main` on GitHub, with spec as its submodule. A folder already there is used as it is, by the checks below.
  - *What is built.* Only a clone whose origin is `altnovatrail/<repo>` on GitHub, by HTTPS or SSH, and whose `.devcontainer/` is that of `main` on GitHub, unchanged in the working tree, so the CLI builds what `main` names. The clone's `.git/` is writable from the repository's own container, which has no socket, so git in the helper never runs with the clone's configuration, whose hooks and fsmonitor would run there: `main` is a fresh clone in the helper's own folder, and nothing of the clone is written. A repository with two containers on the same labels is not rebuilt: the CLI removes the one it finds. The orchestrator's own container is never rebuilt: the author rebuilds it.
  - *A window of VS Code* is not looked for. The rebuild is refused only while Claude Code runs in the container — an executor, or a session in a window —, which `docker top` lists (sources 9.6). A window without it loses its container, and the author reopens it by «Reopen in Container». The author keeps the windows of the epic's repositories closed while it runs.

— *Why:* the pilot (measurements 1.13): 4 of 9 questions waited for the author's morning, В13 `skill-map` from 06:08 to 14:23 UTC, and most repositories waited twice for a rebuild by hand, at night until the morning. Remote Control already gives the questions, the answers and the push in the session the orchestrator runs, and the author has seen it work: whatever NovaTrail built on top would be code to keep and a probe to run for what is already there. A rebuild after a green merge is a step the author only did by hand, with nothing to decide. The helper leaves the orchestrator's configuration as it is and builds from what `main` names, never from a working tree an executor could have changed.

— *Rejected:*
- a board of questions, an artifact on claude.ai with its database, which the orchestrator polls (the first two answers of planning): an artifact is a static page with no backend, and a comment reaches the session only while its watch lasts (sources 2.14), so the board is code and a probe that Remote Control spares;
- hands-free voice, by the voice mode of a chat or by a messenger a phone reads aloud in the car (the sixth word of planning): Claude Code has no voice mode, and no page read says whether the app's pushes reach CarPlay or Android Auto (sources 2.13);
- Slack, Channels — Telegram, Discord, iMessage — and the like: one more service outside, with its own sign-in and terms, and Channels are in research preview and run on Bun (sources 2.14);
- a time-out after which the recommendation is taken: the executor and the orchestrator never decide for the author (R156);
- a rebuild before CI of `main` on the merge is green, or of a repository outside NovaTrail;
- (В42) the host's folder of the clones mounted in the orchestrator's container at the host's path: it mounts whatever else lies beside the clones, as R166 rejected for `${localWorkspaceFolder}/..`. That the container could then write every clone is no reason: the socket is root on the host anyway, and every container mounts `~/.claude` (R166);
- (В43) a window found by the process of Dev Containers with `VSCODE_REMOTE_CONTAINERS_SESSION`: no document names it, a probe found it, and a version of Dev Containers may drop it; a question to the author before each rebuild.

— *Consequence:* R156, R166; the commands `rebuild` and `create` of `tools/orchestrator/`, `devcontainers.mjs`, with their tests; [tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), sections 1, 4–8, Commands and Finding the container; rule 4 of RUN.md; Д269. — RUN.md, T191, T192 and T193; sources 2.13, 2.14, 9.2–9.7; measurements 1.13.

## The executor's waits and its rounds of CI

**R159. A task is planned and ended for the fewest pull requests and rounds of CI: what can run locally runs before the pull request, and CI confirms rather than finds. Tasks of one repository in a row, none waiting on another, run as a batch on one branch with one pull request; a task across repositories runs on one branch of one name in each, by R166. The orchestrator's executor waits on a long run in the foreground — the wait under `timeout 590` in its own command and Bash's `timeout` of 600000 ms, the call repeated until the run is done —, never by `run_in_background`, Monitor or `ScheduleWakeup`; the background of RULES.md, How we work, is for a session a person leads. It commits a task's bookkeeping — «Сделано», the archive, the mark — before it waits on CI, so that a push after a green CI is only for what a check found, and after a fix that follows a finding of CI, SonarCloud or the review it runs the local recipe of CI that covers the changed files before it pushes, not one file.** The batch and the branch across repositories are the author's word of 2026-11-18, which answers В70 by its option (b), one session in the orchestrator's container, and В71 by its option (a), the pull requests in the order of their dependencies; how a task across repositories works is R166. The waits, the bookkeeping and the local recipe are the orchestrator's choices of that day on В66–В68 (run/TASKS.md, T201), each by the executor's recommendation, on the author's word «по возможности сам доведи всё до конца. завтра я всё проверю», and the author has not yet checked them; a different choice rewrites this entry.
- **A batch.** One branch `<epic>-<repo>`, as `e16-spec`, from the up-to-date `main`. Each task of the batch is one commit with its bookkeeping, its «Сделано» naming «ветка …» for the pull request not opened yet, pushed, with no pull request and no checks. The last task runs every local check of the parts the batch changed and `/code-review high` over the batch, opens the one pull request, writes its number into every «Сделано» of the batch, and waits on CI. The orchestrator merges it by a merge commit, so that each task keeps its commit, and each task of the batch is done by that merge. The batch closes early, with its own pull request, at a task whose release another node needs, one whose change of `.devcontainer/` needs the container rebuilt before the next task, or one that waits on the author. A single task has a branch of its own.
- **A task across repositories.** One branch of the same name in every repository it touches, all its code there. Such tasks are spec's: they stand in table 1 of spec's RUN.md, each naming its repositories, with no row of `COORDINATION.md` and no task in those repositories' RUN.md. One session, led by the author in spec's orchestrator container, writes into every repository the task names (R156); one task is one session (R143). Its clones, wiring, stand, gate and pull requests are R166.
- **Where.** RULES.md, How we work — the principle; RUN.md, Epics — the grouping of a plan; [tools/orchestrator/executor.md](../tools/orchestrator/executor.md), The task and Git and the pull request — the waits, the bookkeeping, the local recipe and the batch; [tools/orchestrator/README.md](../tools/orchestrator/README.md), sections 2–5 — the nodes of a batch and their prompts. The code of `tools/orchestrator/` needs no change for these: a status `done` without a pull request is valid, and `next` counts a branch with no pull request.

*Why:* measurements 1.15.
- A task took 30.4 minutes, of them 7.7 on GitHub's checks and 3.7 on the local checks, around a change that is often small (measurements 1.15.1). On one branch, `spec` T212–T216 took 4–8 minutes and $1.3–6.8 each, and the batch's six tasks 62.6 minutes and one round of CI, against 20.8 minutes a task of E16 (measurements 1.15.7).
- Under `claude -p --json-schema` a turn that ends to wait in the background is made to give its status at once (sources 2.15). Before the orchestrator's prompt asked for the foreground, 59 of 301 attempts ended with the background command stopped after their last status, 49 of them a wait on CI; with it, 0 of 17 (measurements 1.15.4).
- A call of the wait in the foreground reads the context from the cache, about $0.03, once each ten minutes at most. T61 `learner-model`, whose waits led to R143's rule of long runs, waited by short loops in 76 calls.
- 40 pushes of bookkeeping after the pull request opened, in 38 tasks, were followed by 251 minutes of waiting on CI: 1.1 minutes a task, 6.6 in a task that did it (measurements 1.15.2).
- In T87 `app` a fix that only CI checked cost 27 minutes (measurements 1.14.3).
- `[parallel]` would shorten a full `just ci` of `app` by at most 38%, under 0.8 minutes a task of `app`. The container sat under one core in 79% of its samples, waiting on the model or GitHub (measurements 1.15.3). It is debt, Д273.
- A task across repositories is one change: one session that sees every repository writes it and wires it as one, and the author sees it work end to end before any pull request.
- A pull request whose CI builds against a tag or `release-verify` of another repository cannot pass before that release; opened after it, it passes in its one round.

*Rejected:*
- a pull request and a round of CI for each task: a task's overhead is mostly its checks and its bookkeeping, and a batch shares them;
- the repositories of a task across repositories one after another, each merged and released before the next is written: nobody sees the change work end to end before its first release;
- (В70) an executor of `claude -p` for each repository, in its own container, on the shared branch, each taking the others' work by their pushed commits — the executor's recommendation: the clones share one folder instead, `.epics` (R166), and one session holds the whole change; no task across repositories, a task in each, merged and released in turn;
- (В71) every pull request at once, the dependent's CI failing until the release; CI built against another repository's branch, by a commit;
- (В66) starting the executor with `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1` and without Monitor and `ScheduleWakeup`: a task of `tools/orchestrator` and a trial on 2.1.280, while the word alone held in 17 attempts of 17; it comes back if a run breaks the rule;
- (В66) the word in the orchestrator's prompt alone: RULES.md would go on saying the opposite;
- (В67) only the bookkeeping, or no change: each rule is a line of the contract, and neither costs a round;
- (В68) `[parallel]` now, by a row of COORDINATION.md: the gain is under a minute a task, and engines run at once share their cores with the other executors;
- the executor leaving CI to the orchestrator: a failure would resume the session and write its context to the cache again, $0.7–1.2 against $0.03 a call of the wait (measurements 1.15.5);
- a shorter interval of polling: the executors poll every 20–30 s, so it gives seconds a round.

— *Consequence:* RULES.md, How we work; RUN.md, Epics; `tools/orchestrator/executor.md` and `README.md`; R143, R156, R166; Д273. — run/TASKS.md, T201 (`docs/plan/E15.md`); T219 (`docs/plan/E16.md`); RUN.md, T221; measurements 1.15; sources 2.15, 11.3.

## Texts without history

**R160. A text holds the current state, not its history, in the documents and the comments of code of every NovaTrail repository: each fact has one home; a decision is its text in force, and a change rewrites it in its place; a comment says only what the code cannot; a done task writes one line of «Сделано» with its pull request. Every other repository takes the rule with its move to a tag of `spec` that has it, by its row of `COORDINATION.md` (T206).** The author's answers of 2026-11-18 to В60–В63 (T200), each by its recommendation; the wording is the executor's (T203). Which lines a move to a tag changes, В69, is the orchestrator's choice of 2026-11-18, by the executor's recommendation: it rests on the author's word of that day, «по возможности сам доведи всё до конца. завтра я всё проверю», and the author has not yet checked it; a different choice of the author rewrites the item «Decisions».
- **One home (В60).** The current state lives where it is set: a version in `deploy/*.json`, the `spec` submodule, `package.json` or an `ARG` of the Dockerfile, a release in its tag, what a task did in its pull request. A document names the file to look at, not the value, and keeps no chronicle of versions, statuses or raises; the history is git, the releases and the archives `docs/plan/`. A fact is written once, and the other texts cite it.
- **Decisions (В61).** An entry is its text in force: what was decided, why, what was rejected and where it is described. A change rewrites the entry in its place, under its number, and every entry it changes too, in the same change, instead of an amendment that restates it; git keeps the old text, and the commit says why. The dated amendments of every log are folded into their entries in epic E22, by each repository's own task, rather than entry by entry as tasks touch them: the readability of the logs and the measurement of their citations weigh for it (R171). A repository's move to a tag of `spec` is its commit, which says why, with the lines of its CLAUDE.md and RUN.md that name the tag, and no entry of the log; its README names no tag (R21). A rewrite keeps what the entry rejected and the quotes of sources it gives itself.
- **Comments (В62).** A comment of code says what the code and its names cannot: why, a constraint, a pitfall, the contract of an exported API. It never retells the code, its history or its task, and cites no task and no section of a document. Its reason stands in words, without the log; a decision's number ends it only where the rejected options matter, `(R25)`, an anchor for `grep`, which `docs-check` checks names an entry of the log (R32; R171).
- **A done task (В63).** «Сделано» is one line: what was done and its pull request, which says how it was checked — where the author commits after review, the report says it. What stays open is rows of `run/QUESTIONS.md` and `run/DEBT.md`, not text of the body. The gist sentence and the archive stay (R153), and so does the report to the author, their way into the work (R154). The architecture describes the current design and cites a decision by its number, without retelling it.
- **Outside the rule** are texts whose entries are dated by nature, `docs/sources.md` and `docs/measurements.md`; the normative texts for authors (R42) — `format/`, `contracts/`, `admission/`, `deployment/`, `legal/`, `consent-age/` and `export/` —, whose versions are their content (R44); the `.proto` files and the descriptions of schemas that code is generated from; the archives `docs/plan/`. A task that changes one of them writes its new text by the rule.
- **Where it is said.** RULES.md — The bar, How we work and Across repositories; the openings of `docs/decisions.md` and of the template's; rule 9 of RUN.md and of the template's RUN.md, and the openings of `run/QUESTIONS.md` and `run/DEBT.md` and of the template's; `run/INBOX.md`; [docs/sources.md](sources.md), section 1; R154, whose "no history" holds for `docs/` and comments too; where a citation stands, R171. The tasks of epic E16 apply it to `spec` and to the checks (RUN.md, table 1).

— *Why:* measurements 1.14.
- The documents are 26% of the context of an executor's main calls and 23% of their output; the rule saves about 2–3 minutes and $0.51–0.85 of a session's 28.8 minutes and $5.72 (measurements 1.14.5).
- None of the three tasks traced needed a chronicle: the session takes a version from where it is set, while 9 of the last 20 pull requests of `infra` rewrote its status paragraph, which none read (measurements 1.14.3, 1.14.4).
- Amendments are 7–45% of a log: R29 `infra`, 25.9 thousand characters, holds about one paragraph in force. A session reads a whole entry to find what holds and writes amendments that restate another entry, and the author cannot read the logs.
- 42% of the comment blocks sampled retell the code; 2 of 8 numbers of decisions checked in comments were wrong, which no check saw.
- A task wrote one fact six to nine times — the decision, amendments, the architecture, «Сделано», the gist sentence, the commit, the pull request, the report —, and the review and the next task read each copy again.

— *Rejected:*
- (В60) one line of the current version, rewritten by each raise: a version written twice goes stale;
- (В61) a log kept append-only, without the amendments that only restate or raise: it keeps the history in the file and saves about half as much;
- the decisions in force consolidated beside the log, which R143 rejected by the sample of T128 (measurements 1.6): a second copy that every change drags an edit after. Rewriting in place keeps one copy, and the facts since — the logs are 6.5% of the executors' context, not 2.6%, the amendments that restate cost output and review, and the author cannot read the logs — weigh for it (measurements 1.14.5);
- (В62) no numbers of decisions in code: the anchor is the cheapest way from a line to its reason, and the check of R32 catches one that names no entry;
- (В63) «Сделано» and «Открыто» as before: they restate the pull request and the rows;
- (В69) a move that changes the submodule alone, CLAUDE.md and RUN.md naming no tag: a session would run `git -C spec describe --tags` to know it; a line of the README that names the tag, as В61 reads: a README names no version (R21).

What a session stops knowing — why and when a decision changed — is in git (`git log -p`, `git log -L`), read when a task asks; an earlier «Сделано» as a precedent is better a short recipe in the rule of the part; an entry rewritten keeps what it rejected.

— *Consequence:* RULES.md, The bar, How we work and Across repositories; the opening of [docs/decisions.md](decisions.md), without the chronicle of when entries were made and on whose answers, which git keeps; R154; R155, its amendment folded in; `repo-template/files/` — `docs/decisions.md`, RUN.md, `run/QUESTIONS.md` and `run/DEBT.md`; RUN.md, rule 9 and «Task body»; `run/QUESTIONS.md`; `run/DEBT.md`; `run/INBOX.md`; [docs/sources.md](sources.md), section 1. — RUN.md, T203; measurements 1.14.

**R161. The task statement is `app`'s card above `<novatrail-canvas>`, by the interface mockup: its picture with a description, its speaker, and on a phone folded to one line with «Show all». The element leaves its own statement out while it has the boolean attribute `statement-hidden`, a contract of `canvas` and `app` beside those of R36.** The author's answer to the row «в реестр spec» `app` В74, by its recommendation.

- **`statement-hidden`.** While the element has it, it draws no statement above the sheet or the workbook page — no text, picture or speaker of its own — and keeps the sheet; once the attribute goes, the statement comes back. It holds from markup too. `app` sets it on each task screen where it draws the card.
- **The card** is `app`'s: its speaker plays the statement by `app`'s voicing, and its fold is `app`'s layout (R148).
- **The types:** the comment of `CanvasElement` in `@altnovatrail/spec/canvas` names the attribute. No member changes (R74).

*Why:* the speaker and the fold are `app`'s voicing and layout, and `canvas` keeps only the sheet. An attribute is what `app` already sets on the element, as `lang` and `tools-hidden` (R36).

*Rejected:*
- `canvas` draws the card by the mockup, and its speaker raises an event that `app` answers with its voicing: the layout of a phone and the voice would be split between two packages;
- the mockup draws the statement as `canvas` does, inside the sheet: it gives up the card that the mockup has for a phone (R148).

— *Consequence:* [architecture 3.1 and 3.2](architecture.md); `types/canvas/index.d.ts`; [COORDINATION.md](../COORDINATION.md), rows 5.21 and 6.43.

## Tasks from the learner's paper

**R162. A task from the learner's paper is the app's main feature, open to every profile in the first slice. The learner photographs a page of their own book or worksheet; the AI finds the tasks on the whole page, each found one picked, and the learner frames by hand one it missed. Each picked task is solved on a dotted sheet of its own, under the task's crop as tracing paper. "Check" gives "Correct" or "Not yet" by a key the program holds: for arithmetic and an equation in one unknown the solver's, which a program computes from the statement the AI read into a formula; for any other task the AI's, from its solution of the task, with no mark that the AI derived it. Such a task never shows its solution, and its attempts are the profile's history on the device, not evidence of the learner model. О-11 is closed.** The author's decisions of 2026-11-18 while epic E11 was planned, and the recommendations of that planning, which the author did not change, with those of 2026-11-19 while T229 was planned and T235, and the author's word at the check of T235 that day, which is not open to discussion: a frame round several tasks is the most common case, and each of its tasks is checked; the look is the interface mockup, approved by the author in RUN.md, T220 ([draft/mockup/README.md](../draft/mockup/README.md)).
- **For whom.** Every profile, of every age category, with no setting that closes it: the card "Take from my paper" on home is open (R148). It is in the first slice (product 10).
- **The page.** The camera of `app` takes the page, or the learner picks a photo from the device. The whole page goes to the AI to find the tasks (R164), on the photo the program turned upright, by any angle, by the AI's word of which way up it is; the answer is the frames and the turn, which `app` gives its photo too (T254); every task found is picked, and the learner may ask in words to find them anew (R165). Each sum or equation of a column under one instruction is a task; the parts of one word problem are one, and with 20 found `app` says that is the most at once. A frame may still hold several tasks, each with an answer of its own — most often one the learner draws round a column of sums —, up to 20, and each of them is checked (T235). The learner unpicks a task, removes any frame by its cross, or frames one the AI missed: a rectangle dragged corner to corner by finger or pen, or two taps, a corner and then the one opposite, become a frame, which its corner resizes (R71 app; В79). `app` cuts each task's crop on the device. The photo, the crops and the work stay on the device, in the profile's storage of `app`: the profile's history (R170) and its export hold them, erased with the profile. The server keeps none of them, not even as a stored work (R113; R09). What goes to the AI provider, for what and on what terms is privacy 6: the page is a work of the learner's category, an adult's under the provider's usual retention and a minor's only where minimal retention holds (R121; R149); before the camera, `app` reminds the learner to keep names out of the photo (R127), and sends and keeps it without the metadata of its file (T223).
- **The sheet.** A task from paper is solved on a sheet whose grid the learner turns by the bar's last button, round — dots as it comes, lines, blank, squares — (T251; R88 canvas).
